tat kiṃ vidhireva? so 'pi (51)nāsti; pramāṇābhāvāt /
sandehastarhi kathamevaṃ bhaviṣyati; anupalabdhacaratvāt /
(52)vivādastarhi, kutra? anugrāhakatvasāmyātsahakāriṣvapi śaktipadaprayogāt sahakāribhede /
tatrāpi- dahanāderanugrāhako 'dhiko 'styeva, yaḥ pratibandhakairapanīyata iti yadi, tadā na vivadāmahe /
asmadabhipretasya cābhāvāderanugrāhakatvamaṅgīkṛtya niḥsādhanā mīmāsaṃkā api na vipratipattumarhanti /
tataḥ- abhāvādiranugrāhaka ityeke, netyapare, iti vivādakāṣṭhāyāṃ vyutpāditaṃ caitasyānugrāhakatvam /
kimaparamavaśiṣyate, yatra pramāṇamabhidhānīyamityalamativistareṇa /
[ku.1.152] tathāpi cetana evāyaṃ saṃskriyate, na bhūtānīti kuto nirṇaya iti cet- ucyate /
bhoktṛṇāṃ nityavibhūnāṃ sarvadehaprāptāvaviśiṣṭāyāṃ viśiṣṭairapi bhūtairniyāmakābhāvātpratiniyatabhagāsiddheḥ /
na hi taccharīraṃ tanmanastānīndriyāṇi viśiṣṭānyapi tasyaiveti niyamaḥ;niyāmakābhāvāt (viśeṣābhāvāt) /
tathā ca sādhāraṇavigrahavattvaprasaṅgaḥ /
na ca bhūtadharma eva (53)kañciccetanaṃ pratyasādhāraṇaḥ; viparyayadarśanāt /
dvitvādivaditi cenna- tasyāpi śarīrāditulyatayā pakṣatvāt /
niyatacetanaguṇopagraheṇaiva tasyāpi niyamaḥ, na tu tajjanyatāmātreṇa; svayamaviśeṣāt /
[ku.1.153] tathāpi tajjanyatayaiva niyamopapattau vipakṣe bādhakaṃ kimiti ceta- kāryakāraṇabhāvabhaṅgaprasaṅgaḥ; śarīrādīnāṃ cetanadharmopagraheṇaiva taddharmajananopalabdheḥ /
tadyathā- icchopagraheṇa prayatnaḥ, jñānopagraheṇecchādayaḥ, tadupagraheṇa sukhādaya ityādi /
prakṛte 'pi cetanagatā eva buddhyādayo niyāmakāḥ syuriti cenna; śarīrādeḥ prāk teṣāmasattvāt /
tathā ca niratiśayāścetanāḥ sādhāraṇāni
 bhūtānīti na bhuktiniyama upapadyate /
[ku.1.154] etena sāṅkhyamatamapāstam /
evaṃ hi tat /
akāraṇamakāryaḥ kūṭasthacaitanyasvarūpaḥ puruṣaḥ /
ādikāraṇaṃ prakṛtiracetanā pariṇāminī /
tato mahadādisargaḥ /
na hi citireva viṣayabandhanasvabhāvā; anirmokṣaprasaṅgāt /
nāpi prakṛtireva tadīyasvabhāvā; tathāpi nityatvenānirmokṣaprasaṅgāt /
nāpi ghaṭādirevāhatya tadīyaḥ; dṛṣṭādṛṣṭatvānupapatteḥ /
nāpīndriyamātrapraṇāḍikayā; vyāsaṅgāyogāt /
nāpīndriyamanodvārā; svapnadaśāyāṃ varāhavyāghrādyabhimānino narasyāpi naratvenātmo(54)padhānāyogāt /
nāpyahaṅkāraparyantavyāpāreṇa; suṣuptyavasthāyāṃ tadvyāpāravirāme 'pi śvāsaprayatnasantānāvasthānāt /
tad yadetāsvavasthāsu savyāpāramekamanuvartate, yadāśrayā cānubhavavāsanā, tadantaḥkaraṇamupārūḍhor'thaḥ puruṣasyopadhānī bhavati /
bhedāgrāhācca niṣkriye 'pi tasmin puruṣe kartṛtvābhimānaḥ, tasminnacetane 'pi cetanābhamānaḥ tatraiva karmāvasānā /
puruṣastu puṣkarapalāśavat (55)sarvathā nirlepaḥ /
[ku.1.155] ālocanaṃ vyāpāra indriyāṇām; vikalpastu manasaḥ; abhimāno 'haṅkārasya; kṛtyadhyavasāyo buddheḥ /
sā hi buddhiraṃśatrayavatī; puruṣoparāgo viṣayoparāgo vyāpārāveśaścetyaṃśāḥ /
bhavati hi mayedaṃ kartavyamiti /
tatra mayeti cetanoparāgo darpaṇasyeva mukhoparāgo bhedāgrahādatāttvikaḥ /
idamiti viṣayoparāga indriyapraṇāḍikayā pariṇatibhedo darpaṇasyeva niśvāsābhihatasya malinimā pāramārthikaḥ /
etadubhayāyatto vyāpāraveśo 'pi /
tatraivaṃrūpavyāpāralakṣaṇāyā buddherviṣayoparāgalakṣaṇaṃ jñānam /
tena saha yaḥ puruṣoparāgasyātātvikasya sambandho darpaṇapratibimbitasya mukhasyeva malinimnā, sopalabdhiriti /
tadevamaṣṭāvapi dharmādayo bhāvā buddhereva; tatsāmānādhikaraṇyenādhyavasīyamānatvāt /
na ca buddhireva svabhāvataścetaneti yuktam- pariṇāmitvāt; puruṣasya tu kūṭasthānityatvāditi /
children.translated_text: Nor is it correct that the intellect itself is by nature conscious — because of its being subject to transformation; whereas the <s>puruṣa</s>, being immutably [conscious], [is truly so].
[Ku 1.156] This too has already been refuted earlier.

children.text: tathā hi- kartṛdharmā niyantāraḥ cetitā ca sa eva naḥ /
children.translated_text: For thus: the possessor of agent-properties, the controller, and the cognizer — that is He alone, for us.
Otherwise, there would be no liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), or alternatively, <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) would be eternal. (Verse 14)

[Ku 1.151] Although 'the presence of the presiding deities who identify with <s>dharma</s> etc. is accepted here too; and they manifest a sign (<s>liṅga</s>) corresponding to the fruition of one's <s>karma</s>' — this is our established doctrine — nevertheless, because of the opponent's disagreement, it is stated otherwise. For even by that procedure, the very thing that is the cause of victory or defeat is manifested, and [the ordeal] brings to light the effect that reveals it. And the manifestation of <s>karma</s> is precisely the obtaining of an auxiliary cause (<s>sahakārin</s>). And that auxiliary cause is the recognition: 'I who have mounted the scales by this procedure am the same as I who am a sinner or sinless.' As they say: 'But the gods perceive them — the inner person of oneself.' Alternatively, with reference to purity corresponding to one's oath, <s>dharma</s> (merit) is produced by that [ordeal], because the procedure is prescribed on the basis of a specific occasion (<s>nimitta</s>), and because the scripture declares victory as its fruit. And with reference to impurity, <s>adharma</s> (demerit) [is produced], because the undesired fruit in the form of defeat serves as a prohibition based on the result.
[Ku 1.151 cont.] Now, what is the proof for the denial of power (<s>śakti</s>)? None. Then does it exist? Certainly. For in our system, the category of power does not fail to exist. What then is it? It is causality (<s>kāraṇatva</s>). What is that? It is belonging to a determinate universal at an earlier time, or possessing the absence of the effect due to the deficiency of an auxiliary cause. As for the denial of anything beyond that — what is there to say? Nothing. Then is there an affirmation? That too does not exist, because there is no proof. Then how will there be doubt? Because [the entity in question] moves in the realm of the unperceived. Then where is the dispute? In the difference of auxiliary causes, because of the equal applicability of the term 'power' (<s>śakti</s>) to auxiliary causes as well, since they equally function as facilitators. And there too — if it be said that there does exist something additional that facilitates fire etc., which is removed by obstacles — then we do not dispute. Having accepted that absence etc. as we intend it functions as a facilitator, even the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, without [independent] proof, ought not to disagree. Therefore: 'Absence etc. is a facilitator,' say some; 'No,' say others — at this utmost point of dispute, the facilitating role of this [absence] has been demonstrated. What more remains, for which a proof needs to be adduced? Enough of excessive elaboration.
[Ku 1.152] Even so, it is this conscious soul alone that is conditioned, not the elements — how is this determined? It is said: Because for the experiencers (<s>bhoktṛ</s>), who are eternal and all-pervading, when their pervasion of all bodies is undifferentiated, even differentiated elements cannot determine [the connection], and so the assignment of particular enjoyments cannot be established. For there is no rule that this body, this mind, and these sense-organs, even though differentiated, belong to this [soul] alone; because there is no determining factor. And thus the absurd consequence arises that bodies would be shared. Nor is any property of elements uniquely associated with a particular conscious being; because the contrary is observed. If it be said, like duality (<s>dvitva</s>) etc. — no, because that too, being on par with body etc., is itself what is to be proved. Even its regularity is [established] only through the apprehension of the qualities of a determined conscious being, not merely through being produced by it; because by itself it is undifferentiated.
[Ku 1.153] Even so, if the regularity can be accounted for by being produced [by the elements] alone, what evidence opposes the counter-thesis? — The consequence would be the collapse of the cause-effect relation; because the production of properties of [bodies etc.] is observed only when assisted by properties of a conscious being. For example: effort [arises] when assisted by desire; desire etc. when assisted by cognition; pleasure etc. when assisted by those — and so forth. Even in the present case, [it might be said that] the determinants would be cognition etc. residing in the conscious being — no, because these do not exist prior to the body etc. And thus, since conscious beings without distinction are equal, and elements are shared, the regulation of experience cannot be accounted for.
[Ku 1.154] By this, the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> doctrine is also set aside. For it is as follows: The <s>puruṣa</s> (soul) is non-causal, non-effectual, of the nature of immutable consciousness (<s>kūṭastha-caitanya</s>). The primordial cause is <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) — unconscious and subject to transformation. From that arises the creation beginning with <s>mahat</s> (the Great). For it is not consciousness itself that has the nature of bondage to objects; because [otherwise] liberation would be impossible. Nor is <s>prakṛti</s> alone of that nature; for even then, being eternal, liberation would be impossible. Nor is it a product like a pot that, having struck [consciousness], becomes 'its'; because it could not be either seen or unseen. Nor [does it occur] merely through the channel of the sense-organs; because attachment could not arise. Nor through the sense-organs and mind as doors; because even in the dream state, a man who identifies with a boar or tiger etc. cannot be presented [to himself] as a man. Nor through the operation extending up to the ego-sense (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>); because even in deep sleep, when the operation of that [ego] has ceased, the continuity of breath and effort persists. That which, in all these states, continues as a single [entity] with operations — and that on which experiential impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) rest — that inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), having assumed its meaning, becomes the presenter to the soul (<s>puruṣa</s>). And due to the non-apprehension of distinction, even in that inactive <s>puruṣa</s>, there is the false identification of agency; in that unconscious [inner organ], the false identification of consciousness; and <s>karma</s> culminates there alone. But the <s>puruṣa</s>, like a lotus leaf [untouched by water], is utterly unstained.
[Ku 1.155] Perception is the operation of the sense-organs; conceptualization is [the operation] of the mind; self-identification (<s>abhimāna</s>) is [that] of the ego-sense; determination of action is [that] of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>). That intellect has three aspects: the coloring by the soul (<s>puruṣoparāga</s>), the coloring by the object (<s>viṣayoparāga</s>), and the entry of operation (<s>vyāpārāveśa</s>). For there is [the thought] 'I must do this.' There, 'I' is the coloring by the conscious being — like the reflection of a face in a mirror — and is non-ultimate due to non-apprehension of distinction. 'This' is the coloring by the object — a differentiation of transformation through the channel of the senses — like the smudge on a mirror breathed upon, and is ultimately real. The entry of operation depends on both of these. In this way, knowledge is the object-coloring aspect of the intellect characterized by such operation. The relation of the non-ultimate coloring by the soul with that [knowledge] — like the [relation of the] reflected face in a mirror with the smudge — is perception (<s>upalabdhi</s>). Thus all eight states beginning with <s>dharma</s> belong to the intellect alone; because they are determined as having the same substrate as it.

children.text:
kṛtisāmānādhikaraṇyavyavasthitāstāvaddharmādayo niyāmakā iti vyavasthitam /
cetano 'pi kartaiva; kṛticaitanyayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyenānubhavāt /
na cāyaṃ (nāyaṃ) bhramaḥ; bādhakābhāvāt /
paraṇāmitvādghaṭavaditi bādhakamiti cenna- kartṛtve 'pi samānatvāt /
tathā ca kṛtirapi (56)(svā)bhāvikī mahato na syāt /
dṛṣṭatvādayamadoṣa iti cet tulyam /
(57)acetanākāryatvaṃ bādhakam, kāryakāraṇayostādātmyāditi cenna- asiddheḥ /
na hi kartuḥ kāryatve pramāṇamasti /
pratyuta "vītarāgajanmādarśanā'(nyā-3.1.25.)diti nyāyādanāditaiva siddhyati /
yadyacca kārye rūpaṃ dṛśyate tasya tasya kāraṇātmakatve rāgādayo 'pi prakṛtau svīkartavyāḥ syuḥ /
tathā ca saiva buddhiḥ, na prakṛtiḥ; bhāvāṣṭakasampannatvāt /
sthūlatāmapahāya sūkṣma(rūpa)tayā te tatra santīti cet caitanyamapi tathā bhaviṣyati /
tathāpyasiddho hetuḥ /
tathā sati ghaṭādīnāmapi caitanyaprasaṅgaḥ, tādātmyāditi cet- rāgādimattvaprasaṅgo 'pi durvāraḥ /
saukṣmyaṃ ca samānamiti /
tasmāt yajjātīyāt kāraṇādyajjātīyaṃ kāryaṃ dṛśyate, tathā bhūtāttathābhūtamātramanumātavyam; na tu yāvaddharmakaṃ kāraṇaṃ tāvaddharmakaṃ kāryam, vyabhicārāditi kimanenāprastutena /
[ku.1.157] yadi ca buddhirnityā; anirmokṣaprasaṅgaḥ /
puṃsaḥ sarvadā sopādhitve svarūpeṇānavasthānāt /
atha vilīyate, tato nānādervilaya ityādimattve, tadanutpattidaśāyāṃ ko niyantā? prakṛteḥ sādhāraṇyāt /
tathā cāsaṃsāraḥ /
pūrvapūrvabuddhivāsanānuvṛtteḥ sādhāraṇye 'pyasādhāraṇīti cet- buddhinivṛttāvapi taddharmavāsanānuvṛttirityapadarśanam /
saukṣmyānna doṣa iti cet- muktāvapi punaḥpravṛttiprasaṅgaḥ /
niradhakāratvānnaivamiti cet- tarhi sādhikārā (58)prasuptasvabhāvā buddhireva prakṛtirastu, kṛtamantarā prakṛtyahaṅkāramanaḥśabdānāmarthāntarakalpanayā /
saiva hi tattadvyāpāra(59)yogāttena tena śabdena vyapadiśyate śārīravāyuvaditi āgamo 'pi saṅgacchate ityato 'pi heturasiddhaḥ /
adhikāranivṛttyā buddherapravṛttirapavargaḥ /
vāsanāyogaścādhikāraḥ /
tataḥ saṃsāraḥ /
[ku.1.158] dharmadharmiṇoratyantabhede ca kauṭasthyāvirodhaḥ /
bhedaśca viruddhadharmādhyāsalakṣaṇo ghaṭapaṭādivat pratyakṣasiddhaḥ /
na ca sāmānādhikaraṇyādabhedo 'pi /
taddhi samānaśabdavācyatvam, ekajñānagocaratvam, ekādhikaraṇatvam, ādhārādheyabhāvaḥ, viśeṣyatvam, sambandhamātraṃ vā bhede eva bhede 'pi cacopapadyamānam, nābhedaṃ spṛśatīti sarvamavadātam /
[ku.1.159] syādetat /
nityavibhubhoktṛsadbhāve sarvametadevaṃ syāt /
sa eva kutaḥ? bhūtānāmeva
 cetanatvāt /

children.translated_text: The elements are like that, being transformed into the form of the body — as is perceived through [the methods of] agreement (<s>anvaya</s>) and difference (<s>vyatireka</s>).

children.text: karmajñānavāsane tu sarvatra pratibhūtaniyate anuvartiṣyete, yato bhogapratisandhānaniyama iti cet- ucyate /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] The latent impressions of action and knowledge will follow [each individual] in a per-element restriction everywhere, whence the regularity of experience and continuity. — [We] reply:
One [person] does not remember what another experienced; a single element does not [persist] due to departure.

children.text: vāsanāsaṅkramo nāsti na ca gatyantaraṃ sthire //15 //
children.translated_text: There is no transference of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>); nor is there an alternative course for what is stable.  [verse 15]

[Ku.1.156] It is established that <s>dharma</s> and other [factors] are the determinants, as they are co-located with volition (<s>kṛti</s>). A conscious being is indeed an agent, since volition and consciousness are experienced as co-located. Nor is this an error, since there is no sublating cognition. [Objection:] The sublating cognition is that [consciousness] is transformative like a pot. — No, because the same [applies] to agency as well. And thus volition too, being natural, would not [belong to] the <s>mahat</s> (great principle). [Objection:] This is not a fault because it is observed [to be so]. — [That rejoinder is] equal [to ours]. [Objection:] The sublating cognition is that [the self] is an effect of the non-conscious, since cause and effect are identical in nature. — No, because [this is] unestablished. For there is no valid means of knowledge [proving] that the agent is an effect. On the contrary, from the principle 'because one free from passion is seen to be unborn' (<s>Nyāya-Sūtra</s> 3.1.25), [the self] is established as beginningless. And if whatever form is seen in an effect must be of the nature of its cause, then passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like would also have to be accepted in <s>Prakṛti</s>. In that case, that [Prakṛti] would be <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) itself, not [something called] <s>Prakṛti</s>, since it would be endowed with the eight dispositions. [Objection:] Setting aside grossness, they exist there in subtle form. — Then consciousness too will be [present] in the same way. Even so, the reason [for your thesis] remains unestablished. [Objection:] In that case, there would be the unwanted consequence that pots and the like also have consciousness, due to identity [of cause and effect]. — Then the unwanted consequence of possessing passion and the like is also unavoidable. And subtlety is the same [in both cases]. Therefore, from whatever type of cause whatever type of effect is observed, from such a [cause] only such [an effect] is to be inferred — but not that the effect has as many properties as the cause, because of deviation. So what is the point of this irrelevant [argument]? [Ku.1.157] If moreover <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is eternal, there would follow the impossibility of liberation — since the <s>puruṣa</s> (person) would always have limiting adjuncts, and would never abide in its own nature. If, on the other hand, it dissolves, then since what is beginningless cannot dissolve [into nothing], if it has a beginning, who determines [its arising] in its pre-origination state? — <s>Prakṛti</s>, since it is common [to all]. But then there would be no transmigration [for distinct individuals]. [Objection:] Due to the continuity of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) from prior <s>buddhis</s>, it is specific even though the [cause] is common. — [This is] refuted by the observation that even after <s>buddhi</s> ceases, the continuity of impressions of its properties [would persist]. [Objection:] There is no fault due to subtlety. — Then there would be the unwanted consequence of re-engagement even after liberation. [Objection:] That does not [happen] because there is no more entitlement (<s>adhikāra</s>). — Then let <s>buddhi</s> itself, with dormant entitlement, be [what is called] <s>Prakṛti</s>; there is no need to postulate <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>manas</s>, and the sense-organs as separate entities. For it is that very [<s>buddhi</s>] which, through connection with various functions, is designated by various names — just like bodily wind (<s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, etc.). Thus scripture also agrees. Therefore, the reason [of the opponent] is unestablished for this [reason] as well. Liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) is the cessation of <s>buddhi</s>'s functioning through the cessation of entitlement. Connection with latent impressions is the entitlement. From that, transmigration. [Ku.1.158] And if there is absolute difference between property and property-bearer, there is no contradiction with immutability. And the difference, characterized by the superimposition of contradictory properties, is established by perception, just as with a pot and a cloth. Nor is there non-difference from co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). For that [co-location] — whether [it means] being denoted by the same word, being the object of a single cognition, having a single substratum, the relation of container and contained, being a qualificand, or mere relation — is possible only where there is difference, and even where there is difference, [it obtains]; so it does not touch [the thesis of] non-difference. Thus everything is clear. [Ku.1.159] It may be objected: All this would be so if an eternal, all-pervading experiencer existed. But whence [comes] that very [entity]? Because it is the material elements alone that are conscious.

children.text:
n.a hi bhūtānāṃ samudāyaparyavasitaṃ caitanyam; pratidinaṃ tasyānyatve pūrvapūrvadivasānubhūtasyāsmaraṇaprasaṅgāt /
nāpi pratyekaparyavasitam; karacaraṇādyavayavāpāye tadanubhūtasya smaraṇāyogāt /
nāpi mṛgamadavāsaneva vastrādiṣu, saṃsargādanyavāsanānyatra saṅkrāmati; mātrānubhūtasya garbhasthena bhrūṇena smaraṇaprasaṅgāt /
na copādānopādeyabhāvaniyamo gatiḥ; sthirapakṣe paramāṇūnāṃ tadabhāvāt /
khaṇḍāvayavinaṃ prati ca vicchinnānāmanupādānatvāt /
pūrvasiddhasya cāvayavino vināśāt /
[ku.1.160] astu tarhi kṣaṇabhaṅgaḥ /
na cātiśayo (60) vyatiricyate; kiṃ tu sādṛśyatiraskṛtatvāt drāgeva na vikalpyate /
kāryadarśanādadhyavasīyate antyātiśayavat /
tathā ca bhūtānyeva tathā tathotpadyante, yathā yathā pratisandhānaniyamādayo 'pyupapadyante /

children.translated_text: [This would hold] only if momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) were established.
But that very [doctrine] has been refuted at length elsewhere.

children.text: api ca-[ku.1.161] na vaijātyaṃ vinā tatsyānna tasminnanumā bhavet /
children.translated_text: Moreover — [Ku.1.161] Without heterogeneity [in the cause], that [effect] would not arise; without that [effect], inference would not be possible.

children.text: vinā tena na tatsiddhirnādhyakṣaṃ niścayaṃ vinā //16 //
children.translated_text: Without that [inference], that [heterogeneity] is not established; nor [does] perception [yield] certainty without [inference].  [verse 16]

For the consciousness of the material elements does not consist in [their] aggregate — because if it were different every day, there would be the unwanted consequence of not remembering what was experienced on previous days. Nor does it consist in each [element] individually — because upon the loss of limbs such as hands and feet, the memory of what was experienced by them would be impossible. Nor does it transfer from one [element] to another through contact, like the fragrance of musk in garments — because there would be the unwanted consequence that a fetus in the womb remembers what the mother experienced. Nor is the course [of impressions] a rule of material-cause-and-product; because in the thesis of permanent [atoms], there is no [destruction and re-origination of] those. And because disconnected [atoms] are not the material cause of a partial whole. And because a previously established whole is destroyed. [Ku.1.160] [Objection:] Then let there be momentary destruction. And the increment [of change] is not distinct [from the entity]; rather, being concealed by similarity, it is simply not discriminated immediately. It is inferred from the observation of effects, just like the final increment. And thus the elements themselves originate in such and such ways, such that the regularity of continuity and the like are also explained.

children.text:
n.a hi, "karaṇākaraṇayostajjātīyasya sataḥ sahakārilābhālābhau tantra'mityabhyupagame kṣaṇikatvasiddhiḥ; tathaikavyaktāvapyavirodhāt /
tadvā tādṛgveti na kaścidviśeṣa iti nyāyāt /
tatastāvanādṛtya vaijātyamaprāmāṇikamevābhyupeya(gantavya)m /
[ku.1.162] evaṃ ca, "kāraṇavat kārye 'pi kiñcidvaijātyaṃ syāt yasya kāraṇāpekṣā, na tu dṛṣṭajātīyasya" iti śaṅkayā na tadutpattisiddhiḥ /
dṛṣṭajātīyamākasmikaṃ syāditi cenna- tatrāpi kiñcidanyadeva prayojakaṃ bhaviṣyatītyaviredhāt /
"na kāryasya viśeṣastatprayuktatayopalabhyate; nāpi kāryasāmānyasyānyaprayojakaṃ dṛśyate" iti cet- tat kiṃ kāraṇasya viśeṣaḥ svagatastatprayojakatayopalabdhaḥ, kāraṇasāmānyasya vānyatprayojyāntaraṃ dṛśyate; yato vivakṣitasiddhiḥ syāt /
śaṅkā tūbhayatrāpi sulabheti /
kāryajanmājanmabhyāmunnīyata iti cenna- sahakārilābhālābhābhyāmevopapatteḥ /
unnīyatāṃ vā; kāryeṣu śaṅkiṣyate; niṣedhakābhāvāt /
na hi dhūmasya viśeṣaṃ dahanaprayojyaṃ pratiṣeddhuṃ svabhāvānupalabdhiḥ prabhavati /
kāryaikaniśceyasya tadanupalabdherevāniścayopapatteḥ /
kāryasya cātīndriyasyāpi sambhavāt; ata evānupalabdhyantaramapi niravakāśamiti /
[ku.1.163] evaṃ vidhirūpayorvyāvṛttirūpayorvā jātyorvirodhe sati na samāveśaḥ /
samāviṣṭayośca parāparabhāvaniyamaḥ; anyūnānatiriktavṛttijātidvayakalpanāyāṃ pramāṇābhāvāt /
vyāvartyabhedābhāvena virodhānavakāśe bhedānupapatteḥ /
parasparaparihāravatyośca samāveśe gotvāśvatvayorapitathā bhāvaprasaṅgāt /
sāmagrīvirodhānnaivamiti cet- (61)kuta etat? parasparaparihāreṇa sarvadā vyavasthiteriti cet- nedamapyadhyakṣam /
ekadeśasamāveśena tu sāmagrīsamāveśo 'pyunnīyate (62)yāvat /
(63)tatkāryayoḥ parasparaparihṛtisvabhāvatvāditi cettarhi kampaśiṃśapayoḥ parasparaparihāravatyorna samāveśaḥ syāt /

[ku.1.164] tato vipakṣe bādhakābhāvāt svabhāvaheturapyapāstaḥ /
nanu- asti tat /
tathā hi- vṛkṣajanakapatrakāṇḍādyantarbhūtā śiṃśapāsāmagrī /
sā vṛkṣamatipatya bhavantī svakāraṇamevātipatet /
evaṃ śākhādimanmātrānubandhī vṛkṣavyavahāraḥ; tadviśeṣānubandhī ca śiṃśapāvyavahāraḥ /
sa kathaṃ tamatipatyātmānamāsādayediti- cet- evaṃ tarhi śiṃśapāsāmagryantarbhūtā calanasāmagrī /
tatastāmatipatya calanādirūpatā bhavantī svakāraṇamevātipatet /
tathā śākhādimadviśeṣānubandhī śiṃśapāvyavahāraḥ, tadviśeṣānubandhī ca calanavyavahāraḥ /

[ku.1.165] nodanādyāgantukanibandhanaṃ calanatvam, na tu tadviśeṣamātrādhīnamiti cet- yadi nodanādayaḥ svabhāvabhūtāḥ; tatastadviśeṣā eva /
athāsvabhāvabhūtāḥ; tataḥ sahakāriṇa eva /
tataḥ (tathā ca) tānāsādya nirviśeṣaiva śiṃśapācalanasvabhā(vatvamā)(vān ā)vamārabhata iti /
tathā ca kutaḥ kṣaṇikatvasiddhiḥ? [ku.1.166] svabhāvabhūtā evāgantukasahakāryanupraveśādbhavantīti cet- evaṃ tarhi vṛkṣasāmagryāmāgantukasahakāryanupraveśādeva śiṃśapāpi jāyata iti na kaścidviśeṣaḥ /
[ku.1.167]
 evametat /
kintu śiṃśapājanakāstarusāmagrīmupādāyaiva calanajanakāstu na tāmeva; kiṃ tu mūrtamātram; tathā darśanāditi cenmaivam; kampajanakāḥ śiṃśapājanakaviśeṣā api santastānatipatanti; na tu vṛkṣajanakaviśeṣāḥ śiṃśapājanakāstāniti niyāmakābhāvāt /
[ku.1.168] śiṃśapājanakāstadviśeṣā eva /
kampakāriṇastu na tathā; kintvāgantavaḥ[ntuka] sahakāriṇa iti cet- evaṃ tarhi tānāsādya sadṛśarūpā api kecit kampakāriṇaḥ, anāsāditasahakāriṇastu na tathā /
tathā ca tadvā tādṛgveti na kaścidviśeṣa (64) iti syāt /
[ku.1.169] tasmādviruddhayorasamāveśa eva /
samāviṣṭayośca parāparabhāva eva /
anevaṃbhūtānāṃ dravyaguṇakarmādibhāvenopādhitvamātram /
teṣāṃ tu viruddhānāṃ na samāveśo vyaktibhedāt /
jātīnāṃ ca bhinnāśrayatvāt /
tathā ca kutaḥ kṣaṇikatm? vaijātyābhyupagame ca kuto 'numānavārtā /
[ku.1.170] mā bhūdanumānamiti cenna- tena hi vinā (65)na tat siddhyet /
na hi kṣaṇikatve pratyakṣamasti; tathā niścayābhāvāt /
gṛhītaniścita evārthe tasya prāmāṇyāt /
anyathātiprasaṅgāt /
[ku.1.171] nanu vartamānaḥ kṣaṇo 'dhyakṣagocaraḥ /
na cāsau (66) pūrvāparakṣaṇātmā /
tato vartamānatvaniścaya eva bhedaniścaya iti cet- kimatra tadabhi[pi] matamāyuṣmataḥ? yadi dharmyeva nīlādiḥ, na kiñcidanupapannam; tasya sthairyāsthairyasādhāraṇyāt /
atha dharmaḥ "tadbhedaniścaye 'pi dharmiṇaḥ kimāyātam? tasya tato 'nyatvāt /
vartamānāvartamānatvamekasya viruddhamiti cet- yadi sadasattvaṃ tat" tanna; anabhyupagamāt /
tādrūpyeṇaiva pratyabhijñānāt /
sadasatsambandhaścet- kimasaṅgatam? jñānavattadupapatteḥ /
krameṇānekasambhandha ekasyānupapanna iti cet- astitāvadato nirūpaṇīyam kṣaṇapratyayastu bhrānto 'pi nāstīti viśeṣaḥ /
[ku.1.172ṭasyādetat /
mā bhūdadhyakṣa(67)manumānaṃ vā kṣaṇikatve; tathāpi sandeho 'stu /
etāvatāpi siddhaṃ samīhitaṃ cārvākasyeti cet- ucyate /
ekatāniścayo yena kṣaṇe, tena sthire mataḥ //17 //

n.a hi sthire taddarśane vā svarasavāhī sandehaḥ; pratyabhijñānasya durapahnavatvāt /
nāpi tatprāmāṇye; sa hi na tāvatsārvatrikaḥ; vyāghātāt /
tathā hi- prāmāṇyāsiddhau sandeho 'pi na siddhyet; tatsiddhau vā tadapi siddhyet /
(68)niścayasya tadadhīnatvāt koṭidvayasya cādṛṣṭasyānupasthāne kaḥ sandehārthaḥ? taddarśane ca kathaṃ sarvathā tadasiddhiḥ /
etenāprāmāṇikastadvyavahāra iti nirastam; sarvathā prāmāṇyāsiddhau tasyāpyasiddheḥ? [ku.1.173] prakṛte prāmāṇyasandehaḥ, lūnapunarjātakeśādau vyabhicāradarśanāditi cet- na ekatvaniścayasya tvayāpīṣṭatvāt /
aniṣṭau vā na kiñcitsiddhyet /
siddhyatu, yatra viruddhadharmaviraha iti cet- tenaiva sthiratvamapi niścīyate /
sa iha sandihyata iti cet- tulyametat /
kvacinniścayo 'pi kathañciditi cet- samaḥ samādhiḥ /
[ku.1.174] nanvetat kāraṇatvaṃ yadi svabhāvo bhāvasya, nīlādivat, tadā sarvasādhāraṇaṃ syāt /
na hi nīlaṃ (69) kañcitpratyanīlam /
athāsādhāraṇatvamapyasya svabhāva eva; tata utpatterārabhya kuryāt; sthirasyaikasvabhāvatvāditi cet- ucyate-[ku.1.175] hetuśaktimanādṛtya nīlādyapi na vastusat /
tadyuktaṃ tatra tat śaktamiti sādhāraṇaṃ na kim //18 //

sarvasādhāraṇanīlādivaidharmyeṇ.a kālpanikatvaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvasya vyutpādayatā nīlādi pāramārthikamevābhyupagantavyam, anyathā tadvaidharmyaiṇa hetuphalabhāvasyāpāramārthikatvānupapatteḥ /
na ca kāryakāraṇabhāvasyāpāramārthikatve nīlādi pāramārthikaṃ bhavitumarhati, nityatvaprasaṅgāt /
tasmādasya pāramārthikatve 'paramapi tathā, navobhayamapīti /
[ku.1.176] ṭhakathamekamanekaṃ parasparaviruddhaṃ kāryaṃ kuryāt /
tatsvabhāvatvāditi yadi, tadotpatterārabhya kuryādaviśeṣāt" ityapi na yuktam; tattatsahakārisācivye tattatkāryaṃ karotīti svabhāvavyavasthāpanāt (svabhāvavyavahārasthāpanāt) /
idaṃ ca sādhāraṇameva, sarvairapi tathopalambhāt /
na hi nīlāderapyanyat sādhāraṇyamiti /

children.translated_text: because the referent of the expression 'possessor of that' is absent.

children.text: bhāve vā sa eva kāraṇaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Or if [such a possessor] exists, that [limiting condition] itself would be the cause.

children.text: atrocyate-[ku.1.178] pūrvabhāvo hi hetutvaṃ mīyate yena kenacit /
children.translated_text: Here it is said — [ku.1.178] For <s>hetutva</s> (causality) is measured by prior existence, by whatever means;
For even of the all-pervading eternal [entity], the cognition of the property-bearer cannot be otherwise. || 19 ||

By one who demonstrates the fictitious nature of <s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s> (the cause-effect relation) through its dissimilarity from universally common things such as blue and the like, blue and the like must be accepted as ultimately real; otherwise, the unreality of the cause-effect relation cannot be established through its dissimilarity from those [blue things and the like].
Nor can blue and the like be ultimately real if the cause-effect relation is unreal, because the undesirable consequence of their being eternal would follow.
Therefore, if this [cause-effect relation] is ultimately real, the other too is likewise; it is not the case that both are [unreal].
[ku.1.176] [Objection:] How can one thing produce many mutually contradictory effects?
If [one says] 'because it is of that nature,' then from the moment of origination it should produce [all effects], since there is no distinction — this too is not correct; because the fixed principle is established that it produces particular effects with the assistance of particular auxiliary causes (<s>sahakārin</s>).
And this is common to all [systems], since all acknowledge it thus.
For even with blue and the like, there is no other commonality.
[ku.1.177] [Objection:] Let this be granted. Let [the cause] be permanent; even so, <s>kāraṇatva</s> (causality) is not tenable for what is eternal and all-pervading.
For thus: causality is ascertained through <s>anvaya</s> (co-presence) and <s>vyatireka</s> (co-absence), not through co-presence alone, because of overextension.
Nor is co-absence possible for eternal and all-pervading entities.
Nor is it correct to say 'it has a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), this is not [a problem]'; because even in the relation with a limiting condition of such a nature, [the eternal entity] has no eligibility.
For that [limiting condition] would either be produced by it, or be eternal.
Not the first, for the same reason as before.
Nor the second, for the very same reason as before.
Even so, the co-absence pertains only to the limiting condition, not to [the eternal entity] itself, since there is no distinction.
[Objection:] If it be said 'of the possessor of that [limiting condition]' — no; for since [the limiting condition] too is a limiting condition, there is no entity possessing that [limiting condition] that is other [than the limiting condition itself],

children.text:
bhavedeva.m, yadyanvayavyatirekāveva kāraṇatvam; kiṃ tu kāryānniyataḥ pūrvabhāvaḥ /
sa ca kvacidanvayavyatirekābhyāmavasīyate, kvaciddharmigrāhakātpramāṇāt /
anyathā kāryāt kāraṇānumānaṃ kvāpi na syāt; tena tasyānuvidhānānupalambhāt upalambhe vā kāryaliṅgānavakāśāt /
pratyakṣata eva tatsiddheḥ /
tajjātīyānuvidhānadarśanātsiddhiranyatrāpi na vāryate /
[ku.1.179] tathāpi koṣṭhagatyānuvihitānvayavyatirekameva kāryāt kāraṇaṃ siddhyet; anyatra tathā darśanāditi cenna- bādhena saṅkocāt; vipakṣe bādhakābhāvena cāvyāpteḥ /
darśanamātreṇa cotkarṣasamatvāt /
asya ceśvare vistaro vakṣyate /
sarvavyāpakānāṃ sarvān pratyanvayamātraviśeṣe kāraṇatvaprasaṅgo bādhakamiti cenna- anvayavyatirekavajjātīyatayā vipakṣe bādhakena ca viśeṣe 'natiprasaṅgāt /
tathā hi- kāryaṃ samavāyikāraṇavad dṛṣṭamityadṛṣṭāśrayamapi tajjātīyakāraṇakam- āśrayābhāve kiṃ pratyāsannam asamavāyikāraṇaṃ syāt /
tadabhāve nimittamapi kimupakuryāt /
tathā cānutpattiḥ satatotpattirvā sarvatrotpattirvā syāt evamapi nimittasya sāmarthyādeva niyatadeśotpāde sa eva deśo 'vaśyāpekṣaṇīyaḥ syāt /
tathā ca sāmānyato deśasiddhau itarapṛthivyādibādhe tadatiriktasiddhiṃ ko vārayet /
children.translated_text: And thus, when [the existence of] place is established in general, and when the other [candidates such as] earth and the like are defeated, who could prevent the establishment of something beyond those?
Similarly, when [the need for] the non-inherent and efficient causes is to be established [as well].

children.text: [ku.1.180] ityeṣā sahakāriśaktirasamā māyā durunnītitaḥ mūlatvātprakṛtiḥ prabodhabhayato 'vidyeti yasyoditā /
children.translated_text: [ku.1.180] This unequal power of auxiliary causes, [which has been] called <s>māyā</s> (illusion) because it is difficult to overcome, [called] <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) because it is the root [of all], [and called] <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) because of the fear of awakening — [is the power] of that [God].

children.text: devo 'sau virataprapañcaracanākallolakolāhalaḥ sākṣātsākṣitayā manasyabhiratiṃ badhnātu śānto mama //20 //
children.translated_text: May that <s>Deva</s> (God), who has ceased from the tumultuous waves of cosmic creation, who is the direct Witness by virtue of being the witness, bind my mind in delight, being tranquil. || 20 ||

This would be so if <s>anvaya</s> (co-presence) and <s>vyatireka</s> (co-absence) alone constituted causality; but [causality is] prior existence that is invariably connected with the effect.
And that is sometimes ascertained through co-presence and co-absence, and sometimes through a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) that apprehends the property-bearer.
Otherwise, the inference of a cause from an effect would never be possible anywhere; because co-presence and co-absence with respect to it are not observed — or if they are observed, there would be no scope for the inferential mark of the effect,
since [the cause] would already be established by direct perception alone.
From observing conformity among things of the same class, establishment [of causality] in other cases too cannot be denied.
[ku.1.179] [Objection:] Even so, only what is established through co-presence and co-absence observed step by step would be a cause from the effect; in other cases, due to [merely] having been observed thus — no, [we reply], because [over-extension is] restricted by a <s>bādhaka</s> (defeating cognition); and because in the absence of a defeating cognition in the counter-instance, there is non-pervasion [of the objection].
And [the two methods] are equal in [relying on] mere observation.
And the elaboration of this [argument] regarding <s>Īśvara</s> (God) will be stated [later].
[Objection:] If for all-pervading entities there is mere co-presence with everything, there would be the undesirable consequence of causality with respect to everything — and this constitutes a defeating cognition — no, [we reply]; because just as with co-presence and co-absence, by virtue of being of the same class, the defeating cognition in the counter-instance prevents overextension in particular cases.
For thus: an effect is observed to possess an <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause); therefore even what lacks an observed substrate is [inferred to be] caused by a cause of the same class — [Objection:] In the absence of a substrate, what would be the proximate <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause)?
In the absence of that, how would a <s>nimittakāraṇa</s> (efficient cause) also be of any help?
And in that case, there would either be non-origination, or perpetual origination, or origination everywhere. Even so, if origination in a determinate place is due to the power of the efficient cause alone, that very place must necessarily be postulated.
Thus ends the first <s>stabaka</s> (chapter) of the illustrious <s>Nyāyakusumāñjali</s>.
<s>Śrīḥ</s> (Auspiciousness).
The second <s>stabaka</s> (chapter) of the <s>Nyāyakusumāñjali</s>.

children.text:
tadevaṃ sāmānyataḥ
(70)siddhe alaukike hatau- tatsādhanenāvaśyaṃ
bhavitavyam /
na ca tacchakyamasmadādibhirdraṣṭum /
na cādṛṣṭena vyavahāraḥ- tato lokottaraḥ sarvānubhāvī sambhāvyate /
children.translated_text: Nor is there any practical dealing with what is not perceived — therefore, a supramundane, omnipotent [being] is to be postulated.

[ku.2.202] [Objection:] The tradition of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) may be based either on eternally omniscient [beings] without faults, through the <s>Veda</s>, or through omniscient [beings] who have attained [omniscience] through <s>yoga</s> and <s>karma</s> (spiritual practice and action).

children.text: kiṃ parameśvarakalpanayeti cet- (72)atrocyate- pramāyāḥ paratantratvāt sargapralayasambhavāt /
children.translated_text: What need is there for the postulation of a <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord)? To this it is said: Because <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) is dependent [on something else]; because creation and dissolution occur;
Because of the impossibility of trust in anyone other than that [Supreme Lord], no alternative injunction is possible. || 1 ||

Thus, when [the existence of] a supramundane [entity] is established in general — the means of proving that must necessarily exist.
Nor can that [means] be perceived by us and the like.

[ku.2.203] tathā hi...pramājñānahetvatiriktahetvadhīnā kāryatve sati tadviśeṣatvāt apramāvat /

tadaprāmāṇye doṣā eva kāraṇam; gumanivṛttistvavarjanīyasiddhasannidhiriti cet- prāmāṇyaṃ prati guṇeṣvapi tulyametat /
guṇānāṃ doṣotsāraṇaprayuktaḥ sannidhiriti cet- doṣāṇāmapi guṇotsāraṇaprayukta ityastu /
niḥsvabhāvatvamevamapauruṣeyasya vedasya syāditi cet- ātmānamupālabhasva /
tasmāt yathā- dveṣarāgābhāvāvinābhāve 'pi rāgadveṣayo (76)ranuvidhānaniyamāt pravṛttinivṛttiprayatnayo rāgadveṣakāraṇakatvam; na tu nivṛttiprayatno dveṣahetukaḥ, pravṛttiprayatnastu satyapi rāgānuvidhāne dveṣābhāvahetuka iti vibhago yujyate; viśeṣābhāvāt- tathā prakṛte 'pi /
[ku.2.207] tathāpi vedānāmapauruṣeyatve siddhe apetavaktṛdoṣatvādeva prāmāṇyaṃ setsyati /
tataḥ siddhe prāmāṇye guṇābhāve 'pi taditi doṣābhāva eva hetuḥ; akāraṇaṃ guṇā iti cenna- apetavaktṛguṇatvena satpratipakṣatvaprasaṅgāt /
"svata eva prāmāṇyaniścayaḥ /
kiṃ tu śaṅkāmātramanenāpanīyate; doṣanibandhanatvāttasya tadabhāve 'bhāvāt /
ato nedamanumānavat (anumānaṃ) satpratisādhanīkartumucitamiti cet-na-guṇanivṛttinibandhanāyāḥśaṅkāyāḥsulabhatvāt /
tasyāḥ kevalāyā aprāmāṇyaṃ pratyanaṅgatvānna śaṅketi cet- doṣanivṛtterapi kevalāyāḥ prāmāṇyaṃpratyanaṅgatvānna tayā śaṅkānivṛttiriti tulyamiti /
[ku.2.208] evaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ parato jñāyate anabhyāsadaśāyāṃ sāṃśayikatvāt aprāmāṇyavat /
yadi tu svato jñāyeta, kadācidapi prāmāṇyasaṃśayo na syāt jñānatvasaṃśayavat; niścite tadanavakāśāt /
nahi sādhakabādhakapramā(sādhakapramā)ṇābhāvamavadhūya samānadharmādi darśanādevāsau; tathā sati tadanucchedaprasaṅgāt /
[ku.2.209] atha pramāṇavadapramāṇe 'pi tatpratyayadarśanāt viśeṣādarśanāt bhavati śaṅketyabhiprāyaḥ- tat kiṃ pramāṇajñānopalambhe 'pi na tatprāmāṇyamupalabdham, pramāṇajñānameva vā nopalabdham? ādye kathaṃ svataḥ prāmāṇyagrahaḥ; pratyayapratītāvapi tadapratīteḥ /
dvitīye kathaṃ tatra śaṅkā; dharmiṇa evānupalabdheriti /
[ku.2.210] yadapi jhaṭiti pracuratarasamarthapravṛttyanyathānupapattyā svataḥ prāmāṇyamucyate- tadapi nāsti; anyathaivopapatteḥ /
jhaṭiti pravṛttirhi jhaṭiti tatkāraṇopanipātamantareṇānupapadyamānā
 tamākṣipet /
pracurapravṛttirapi svakāraṇaprācuryam /
icchā ca pravṛtteḥ kāraṇam /
tatkāraṇamapīṣṭābhyupāyatājñānam /
tadapi tajjātīyatvaliṅgānubhavaprabhavam /
so 'pīndriyasannikarṣādijanmā /
na tu prāmāṇyagrahasya kvacidapyupayogaḥ /
upayoge vā svata eveti kuta etat? tataḥ samarthapravṛttiprācuryamapi prāmāṇyaprācuryāttadgrahaṇaprācuryādvā svatastvaṃ tu tasya kvopayujyate /
na hi pipāsūnāṃ jhaṭiti pracurā samarthā ca pravṛttirambhasīti pipāsopaśamanaśaktistasya pratyakṣā syāt /
[ku.2.211] syādetat- prāmāṇyagrahe sati sarvametadupapadyate /
sa ca svato yadi na syāt, na syādeva; parataḥpakṣasyānavasthāduḥsthatvāditi- cet- na- tadagrahe 'pyarthasandehādapi sarvasyopapatteḥ /
na cānavasthāvapi; prāmāṇyasyāvaśyajñeyatvānabhyupagamāt /
anyathā svataḥpakṣe 'pi sā syāt /
[ku.2.212] liṅgaṃ niścitameva niścāyakam /
tatastanniścayārthamavaśyaṃ liṅgāntarāpekṣāyāmanavastheti cet- tatkimanupapadyamānor'thaḥ aniścita eva svopapādakamākṣipati; yenānavasthā na syāt /
pratyakṣeṇa tasya niścayāttasya ca sattayaiva niścāyakatvānnaivamiti cet- mamāpi pratyakṣeṇa liṅganiścayāt tasya ca sattayaiva niścāyakatvānnaivamiti tulyam /
[ku.2.213] liṅgajñānasya prāmāṇyāniścaye kathaṃ tanniśca(liṅganirṇa)yaḥsyāditi cet- anupapadyamānārthajñānaprāmāṇyāniścaye kathaṃ tanniścaya iti tulyam /
na hi niścayena svaprāmāṇyaniścayena vā viṣayaṃ niścāyayati pratyakṣam; api tu svasattayetyuktamiti cet- tulyam /
[ku.2.214] tathāpi yadi tat liṅgābhāsaḥ syāt, tadā kā vārteti cet- anupapadyamāno 'pyartho yadyābhāsaḥ syāt, tadā kā vārteti tulyam /
so 'pi prāmāṇyamākṣipatītyutsargaḥ /
sa ca kvacidvādhakenāpodyata iti cet- liṅge 'pyevamiti tulyam /
tarhi prāmāṇyānumāne'pi śaṅkā tadavasthaiveti niṣphalaḥ prayāsa iti cet- etadapi tādṛgeva /
anupapadyamānor'tha evāsau tathāvidhaḥ kaścit yaḥ svapne 'pi nābhāsaḥ syāt /
tato nā'śaṅketi cet- liṅge 'pyevamiti samaḥ samādhiḥ /
[ku.2.215] kaḥ punarasāvarthaḥ, yaḥ svapne 'pi nābhāsaḥ syāt? yadanupalambhe vibhramāvakāśaḥ, (77)yādṛgupalambhe ca tadbādhavyavasthā /
anyathā hi tathābhūtasyāpi vyabhicāre sāpi na syāt /
mā bhūditi cenna- bhavitavyaṃ hi tattvātatvavibhāgena (tattvātattvavyavasthā) anyathā vyāghātāt /
kathaṃ hi niyāmakaniḥśeṣaviśeṣopalambhe 'pi viparītāropaḥ? tathābhāve vā tadatiriktaviśeṣānupalambhe kathaṃ bādhakam? tadabhāve tvabādhasya kathaṃ bhrāntatvamiti /
[ku.2.216] syādetat- parataḥprāmāṇye 'pi nityatvādvedānāmanapekṣatvam; mahājanaparigrahācca prāmāṇyamiti ko virodhaḥ? na; ubhayasyāpyasiddheḥ /
[ku.2.217] na hi varṇā eva tāvānnityaḥ /
tathā hi- "idānīṃ śrutapūrvo gakāro nāsti" (stīti) "nivṛttaḥ kolāhala" iti pratyakṣeṇaiva śabdadhvaṃsaḥ pratīyate /
na hi śabda evānyatra gataḥ; amūrtatvāt /
nāpyāvṛtaḥ; tata eva sambandhavicchedānupapatteḥ /
nāpyanavahitaḥ śrotā; avadhāne 'pyanupalabdheḥ /
nāpīndriyaṃ duṣṭam; śabdāntaropalabdheḥ /
nāpisahakāryantarābhāvaḥ; anvayavyatirekavataḥ(kataḥ) tasyāsiddheḥ /
(78) nāpyatīndriyam; tatkalpanāyāṃ pramāṇābhāvāt /
anyathā ghaṭādāvapi tatkalpanāprasaṅgāt /
na ca śabda(sya) nityatvasiddhau tatkalpaneti yuktam; nirākariṣyamāṇatvāt /
[ku.2.218] yattvekadeśino naivamicchanti tān pratyucyate- vivādādhyāsitaḥ śabdapradhvaṃsa indriyagrāhyaḥ aindriyikābhāvatvāt ghaṭābhāvavat /
naitadevam; indriyāsannikṛṣṭatvādatīndriyādhāratvādveti cenna- idaṃ hyupādhyudbhāvanaṃ vā syāt, vyāpakānupalabdhyā satpratipakṣatvaṃ vā /
na prathamaḥ; svarūpayogyatāṃ prati (gyatāyāṃ)sahakāriyogyatāyā anupādhitvāt /
tasyāstāmapekṣyaiva sarvadā vyavasthiteḥ /
nāpyaindriyikādhāratvaprayuktamabhāvasya pratyakṣatvam; dharmādyabhāvasyāpi tathātvaprasaṅgāt /
ata eva nobhayaprayuktam /
[ku.2.219] nāpi dvitīyaḥ; prathamasyāsiddheḥ /
asti hi śrotraśabdābhāvayoḥ svābhāviko viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ /
viśeṣyasyātīndriyatvātkathamaindriyikaviśiṣṭajñānaviṣayatvam? tathā viśeṣyamavyavasthāpayataśca kathaṃ viśeṣaṇatvamiti cet- na; tathā viśeṣyavyavasthāpanāyāḥ phalatvāt /
na tu tadeva viśeṣaṇatvam; ātmāśrayaprasaṅgāt- viśeṣaṇabhāvena samavāyābhāvayorgrahaṇam, tathā grahaṇameva ca viśeṣaṇatvamiti /
tasmāt sambandhāntaramantareṇa tadupaśliṣṭasvabhāvatvameva hi tayoḥ /
saiva ca viśiṣṭapratyayajananayogyatā viśeṣaṇatetyucyate /
sā cātra durnivārā /
pratiyogyadhikaraṇena svabhāvata evābhāvasya
 militatvāt /
[ku.2.220] tathāpi tayā tathaiva pratītiḥ kartavyeti cenna- gṛhyamāṇaviśeṣyatvāva(ṣyāva)cchinnatvādvyāpteḥ /
anyathā saṃyuktasamavāyena rūpādau viśiṣṭavikalpadhījananadarśanāt gandhādāvapi tathātvaprasaṅgāt /
[ku.2.221] tathāpi nendriyaviśeṣaṇatayā kasyacit grahaṇaṃ dṛṣṭam; api tvindriyasambaddhaviśeṣaṇatayā; sā cāto nivartata iti cenna- asya pratibandhasyendriyasannikṛṣṭārthapratisambandhiviṣayatvāt /
anyathā saṃyuktasamavāyena gandhādāvupalabdhidarśanāt samavāyenādarśanācchabdasyāgrahaṇaprasaṅgāt /
[ku.2.222] nāpyabhāvatve sati atīndriyādhāratvātsatpratipakṣatvam; yogyatāvirahaprayuktatvādvyāpteḥ /
na cātīndriyādhāratvameva tasya yogyatāvirahaḥ; tadviparyayasyaiva yogyatātvāpatteḥ /
na caivameva; dharmādipradhvaṃsagrahaṇaprasaṅgāt /
dṛśyādhāratvaṃ dṛśyapratiyogitāceti dvayamapyasya yogyateti cenna- ubhayanirūpaṇīyatvaniyamānabhyupagamāt /
pratiyogimātranirūpaṇīyo hyabhāvaḥ /
[ku.2.223] anyathā "iha bhūtale ghaṭo nāstī'tyeṣāpi pratītiḥ pratyakṣā na syāt /
saṃyogo hyatra niṣidhyate /
tadabhāvaśca bhūtalavad ghaṭe 'pi vartate /
tatra yadi pratyakṣatayā bhūtalasyopayogaḥ, ghaṭasyāpi tathaiva syāt /
aviśeṣāt /
atha ghaṭasyānyathopayogaḥ; bhūtalasyāpyanyathaiva syāt, aviśeṣāt /
kathamanyatheti cet- pratiyoginirūpaṇārthamabhāvasannikarṣārthaṃ ca /
tatra pratiyoginirūpaṇaṃ smaraṇalakṣaṇamanupalabhyamānenāpīti, na tadarthamadhyakṣagocaratvamapekṣaṇīyamanyatarasyāpi; kuta ubhayasya /
sannikarṣastu bhūtalaghaṭasaṃyogābhāvasyendriyeṇa sākṣānnāsti /
yenāsti, tenāpi yadīndriyaṃ na sannikṛṣyeta, kathamiva taṃ gamayet /
na copalabdhopalabhyamānābhyāmevendriyaṃ sannikṛṣyate; itaretarāśrayaprasaṅgāt /
[ku.2.224] tasmāt sannikarṣe sati yogyatvāt bhūtalamapyupalabhyate; na tu tasyopalabhyamānatvamabhāvopalabdheraṅgamiti yuktamutpaśyāmaḥ /
prakṛte tu na pratiyoginirūpaṇārthaṃ tadupayogaḥ tasya saṃyogavat ādhārānirūpyatvāt /
nāpi sannikarṣārtham; tadabhāvasya sākṣādindriyasannikarṣāditi /
[ku.2.225] na cedevam; kuta eṣā pratītiḥ, idānīṃ śrutapūrvaḥ śabdo nāstīti? "anumānā'diti cenna śabdasyaiva pakṣīkaraṇe (80)hetoranāśrayatvāt /
anityatvamātrasādhane 'bhāvasya niyatakālatvāsiddheḥ /
ākāśasya pakṣatve tadvattayānupalabhyamānatvasya hetoranaikāntikatvāt /
śabdasadbhāvakāle 'pi tasya sattvāt /
evaṃ kālapakṣe 'pi doṣāt /
[ku.2.226] ahamidānīṃ niḥśabdaśrotravān śabdopalabdhirahitatvāt badhiravaditi cet-na-dṛṣṭāntasya sādhyavikalatvāt, vyāhatatvācca; badhiraśca śrotravāṃśceti vyāhatam /
tasyāpi ca śravaso niḥśabdatve pramāṇaṃ nāsti /
anupabhogyasyotpādavaiyarthyaṃ pramāṇamiti cet-na-ādyādiśabdavadupapatteḥ /
teṣāṃ śabdāntarārambhaṃ pratyupayogaḥ; antyasya na tatheti cet-na-antyatvāsiddheḥ /
sarveṣāṃ cotpādavatāṃ prayojanatadabhāvayorasmādṛśairanākalanāt; suṣuptyavasthāyāṃ śvāsapraśvāsaprayojanavacca tadupapatteḥ /
ārambhe sati prayojanamavaśyamiti vyāpteḥ /
na tvāpātataḥ prayojanānupalambhamātreṇārambhanivṛttiḥ; tathā sati karṇaśaṣkulyavacchedotpāda eva nabhasastaṃ prati nivarteta; badhirasya tenānupayogāt /
vivādakāle badhirakarṇaḥ śabdavān yogyadeśa(81)sthānāvṛtakarṇaśaṣkulīsuṣiratvāt taditarakarṇaśaṣkulīsuṣiravaditi /
[ku.2.227] niḥśabdāḥ paṇavavīṇāveṇavaḥ (82)tadekajñānasaṃsargayogyatve sati tadanupalambhe 'pyupalabhyamānatvāt /
yat yadekajñānasaṃsarga(83)yogyaṃ(ya) tasyānupalambhe 'pyupalabhyate tat tadabhāvavat, yathāghaṭaṃ bhūtalamiti cet-na-ekajñānasaṃsargayogyatvābhāvāt; śabdasya śrautatvāt, vīṇādīnāṃ cākṣuṣatvāt /
abhimānamātrāditi cenna, tathāpi śabdapradhvaṃsasyātaddeśatvāt, atyantābhāvasya ca kālaniyamāt /
[ku.2.228] syādetat- śabdavadākāśopādhayo hi bheryādayaḥ /
tena teṣu vidhīyamānaḥ śabdaḥ ākāśa eva vihito bhavati; pratiṣiddhyamānaśca tatraiva pratiṣiddho bhavati, śarīre sukhādivat iti cet na- tatra sopādhāvātmani pratyakṣasiddhe sukhādiniṣedhasyāpi pratyakṣāsiddhatvāt /
na caivamihāpi; tadupahitasya nabhaso 'pratyakṣatvāt /
upādhayastāvat pratyakṣā iti cenna- tairabhāvānirūpaṇāt /
nirūpaṇe vā pratyakṣeṇāpi grahaṇaprasaṅgāt /
na caivaṃ sati pāramārthikādhikaraṇanirūpaṇīyatvamabhāvasya /
na ca te 'pi pratyakṣasiddhāḥ (84) sarvatra; śabdakāraṇavyavadhāne 'pyupalabdhasya
 śabdasya nāstitāpratīteḥ /
ānumānikaistaistathā vyavahāra iti cenna- hetostadvattayānupalabhyamānatvasyānaikāntikatvāt; abhāvapratītikāle sandigdhāśrayatvācca /
upalabhyamānaviśeṣyatvapakṣe cāsiddheḥ; indriyavyavadhānāt, śabdaliṅgasya cānupalambhāt /
[ku.2.229] api ca naṣṭāśrayāṇāṃ dravyaguṇakarmaṇāṃ nāśopalambhaḥ katham? na kathañciditi cet- āśrayanāśātkāryanāśa iti kuta etat? anumānatastathopalambhāditi cet- na- tulyanyāyenoktottaratvāt /
tantuṣu naṣṭeṣvapi yadi paṭo, na naśyet, tadvadevopalabhyeteti cet- etasya tarkasyānugrāhyamabhidhīyatām /
[ku.2.230] yadatropalabhyate na tat kāryaparamparāvat, yogyasya tathānupalabhyamānatve sati upalabhyamānatvāditi cet-na-tantvavayavānāṃ paṭānādhāratve sādhye siddhasādhanāt /
paṭapradhvaṃsavattve sādhye bādhitatvāt tasya svapratiyogikāraṇamātradeśatvāt /
[ku.2.231] ye paṭadhvaṃsavantastantavaḥ, tadabhāvavanta ete aṃśavaḥ iti sādhyamiti cenna- tantunāśottarakāle paṭanāśāttadvattānupapatteḥ /
yogyatāmātrasādhane ca paṭapradhvaṃsāsiddheḥ; tasya nāśānāśayoḥ samānatvāt /
[ku.2.232] ananyagatikatayā viśiṣṭaniṣedhe kṛte viśeṣaṇānāmapyabhāvaḥ pratīto bhavati; guṇakriyāvatpaṭādhārāstantavo na santi svāvayaveṣviti hi pratyaya iti cet- tathāpi guṇakarmaṇāṃ paṭasya ca pradhvaṃsaḥ kimadhikaraṇaḥ pratīyata iti vaktavyam /
aśvādhikaraṇa eveti cet- bhrāntistarhīyam; tasyātaddeśatvāt /
āśrayāvacchedakatayā teṣāmapyadūraviprakarṣeṇa taddeśatvam evaṃbhūtenāpi deśena tannirūpaṇam; yogyatāyā avyabhicārāditi cet- na tarhi pratiyogisamavāyideśenaiva pradhvaṃsanirūpaṇamiti niyamaḥ; prakārāntareṇāpi nirūpaṇāt /
[ku.2.233] tasmāt yasya yāvatī grahaṇasāmagrī, taṃ vihāya tasyāṃ satyāṃ tadabhāvo yatra kvacinnirūpyo deśe kāle vā /
iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ- sā satī cet, pratyakṣeṇa /
asatyeva jñātā cet, (85)anumānādineti sthitiḥ /
[ku.2.234] etena "sadbhyāmabhāvo nirūpyate" ityādiśāstra(86)virodhaḥ parihṛto veditavyaḥ; ubhayanirūpaṇīyapratiyogiviṣayatvāt anumānaviṣayatvācca /
anyathā āśrayāsiddhiprasaṅgāt /
tatrāpi na graṅaṇe niyamaḥ, jñānamātraṃ tu vivakṣitam; tāvanmātrasyaiva tadupayogāt /
kvacit grahaṇasya sāmagrīsampātāyātatvāt /
[ku.2.235] yadicādhikaraṇagrahe śāstrasya nirbharaḥ syāt, "vahnerdāhyaṃ vināśyānuvināśavattadvināśaḥ" iti nodāharet; asiddhatvāt /
na hi vahnivināśastadavayavaparamparāsvakṣa(87)nirūpyaḥ tāsāmanirūpaṇāt /
nāpyanyatra gamanābhāvādinā pāriśeṣyādanumeyaḥ; hetoreva nirūpayitumaśakyatvāt; āśrayānupalabdheḥ /
nāpi nimittavināśāt sarvamidamekavāreṇa setsyatīti yuktama; tasyānaikāntikatvāt /
tejasā viśeṣitatvādayamadoṣa iti cenna- vyāptyasiddheḥ /
na hīndhanavināśāt tejodravyamavaśyaṃ vinaśyatīti kvacitsiddham; (88)pratyakṣavṛtteranabhyupagamāt /
[ku.2.236] tasmāt yattyāgenānyatra gamanaṃ na sambhāvyate, tena nimittādināpi deśena pradhvaṃso nirūpyate ityakāmenāpi svīkaraṇīyam; gatyantarābhāvāt /
ata eva tamasaḥ pratyakṣatve 'pyabhāvatvamāmanantyācāryāḥ /
etena śabdaprāgabhāvo vyākhyātaḥ /
[ku.2.237] evaṃ (89)vyavasthite anumānamapyucyate- śabdo 'nityaḥ (90)utpattidharmakatvāt ghaṭavat /
na cedaṃ pratyabhijñānabādhitam; tasya jvālādipratyabhijñānenāviśeṣāt /
[ku.2.238] naivam; abādhitasya tasya svataḥ pramāṇatvāditi cet- tulyam /
"jvālāyāṃ tannāsti; viruddhadharmādhyāsena (91)bādhitatvāt /
anyathā bhedavyavahāravilopaprasaṅgaḥ /
nimittābhāvāt /
ākasmikatve vātiprasaṅga" iti cet- tulyam,(92)śabde 'pi tīvratīvrataratvamandamandataratvāderbhāvāt /
[ku.2.239] tadiha na svābhāvikamiti cenna- svābhāvikatvāvadhāraṇanyāyasya tatra tatra siddhasyātrāpi tulyatvāt /
na hyapāṃ śaityadravatve svābhāvike, tejaso vā auṣṇyabhāsvaratve ityatrānyatpramāṇamasti pratyakṣādvinā /
"tattathaiva yujyate; anyasyopādheranupalambhāt, niyamena tadgatatvena copalambhā'diti cet- tulyametat /

ekasyānyatamāṅgavaikalyacintāyāmasya vaikalye tasyaiva (94)vācyatvāt /
avaikalye, tvādīyenaiva vikalena bhavitavyamiti hīnasya na satpratipakṣatvam /
tathāpi nityaḥ śabdaḥ (95)adravyadravyatvādatyitrāpi sādhanadaśāyāṃ kiñcidvācya'miti cet- asiddhiḥ /
[ku.2.245] dravyaṃ śabdaḥ sākṣātsambandhena gṛhyamāṇatvādghaṭavaditi siddhyatīti cenna- etasyāpyasiddheḥ /
na hi śrotraguṇatve dravyatve vāsiddhe sākṣātsambandhe śabdasya pramāṇamasti /
"pariśeṣo 'sti /
tathā hi- sadādyabhedena sāmānyāditrayavyāvṛttau mūrtadravyasamavāyaniṣedhena karmatvaniṣedhāt dravyaguṇatvapariśeṣe saṃyogasamavāyayoranyataraḥ sambandhaḥ" iti cenna- bādhakabalena pariśeṣe dravyatvasyāpi niṣedhālliṅgagrāhakapramāṇabādhāpatteḥ /
bādhake satyapi vā dravyatvāpratiṣedhe karmatvādīnāmapyapratiṣedhaprasaktau paraśeṣāsiddheḥ /
tasmādekadeśapariśeṣo na pramāṇam /
sandehasaṅkocamātrahetutvāt /
atha dravyatve kiṃ bādhakam? ucyate- śabdo na dravyaṃ bahirindriyavyavasthāhetutvādrūpādivat /
iti pariśeṣādguṇatvena (96)samavāyi(ya)siddhau liṅgagrāhakapramāṇabādhitatvānnāvyavahitasambandhagrāhyatvena dravyatvasiddhaḥ /
ni cāsiddhena satpratipakṣatvam; asiddhasya hīnabalatvāt /
[ku.2.246] nanu śabdastāvada(97)śrotraguṇo naiveti tvayaiva sādhitaṃ prabandhena /

yad yenendriyeṇa gṛhyate, nāsau tasya guṇaḥ; yathā gṛhyamāṇo gandhādiḥ /
śrotraṃ vā na svavaguṇagrāhakam indriyatvāt ghrāṇavat iti na guṇatvasiddhiriticet- tataḥ kim? na caitadapi; ghrāṇādisamavetagandhādyagrahe svaguṇatvasyāprayojakatvāt /
(98)ayogyatvaṃ hi tatropādhiḥ /
[ku.2.247] anyathā- sukhādirnātmaguṇaḥ tena gṛhyamāṇatvāt rūpādivat /

ātmā vā na tadgrāhakaḥ tadāśrayatvāt gandhādyāśrayaghaṭādivadityādyapi śaṅkyeta /
tasmāt svaguṇaḥ paraguṇe vāyogyo na gṛhyate; gṛhyate tu yogyo yogyona /
tat kimatrānupapannam /
[ku.2.248] avaśyaṃ ca śrotreṇa viśeṣaguṇagrāhiṇā bhavitavyam indriyatvāt /
anyathā tannirmāṇavaiyarthyāt /
(99)tadanyasyendriyāntareṇaiva grahaṇāt /
na ca dravyaviśeṣagrahaṇe tadupayogaḥ; (100)viśeṣaguṇayogyatāmāśrityaivendriyasya dravyagrāhakatvāt; na dravyasvarūpayogyatāmātreṇa /
anyathā cāndramasaṃ tejaḥ svarūpeṇa yogyamiti tadapyupalabhyeta; ātmā vā mano grāhya iti suṣuptyavasthāyāmapyupalabhyeta; anudbhūtarūpe 'pi vā cakṣuḥ pravartate /
tasmāt guṇayogyatāmeva puraskṛtyendriyāṇi dravyamupādadate; nāto 'nyatheti sthitiḥ /
ata eva nākāśādayaścākṣuṣāḥ /
[ku.2.249] astu tarhi śabdo nityaḥ nityākāśaika(101)guṇatvāt tadgataparamamahat(102)parimāṇavaditi pratyanumānamiti cenna- akāryatvasyopādhervidyamānatvāt /
anyathā-
 ātmaviśeṣaguṇā nityāḥ tadekaguṇatvāttadgataparamamahattvavadityapi syāt /
"asya pratyakṣabādhitatvādahetutvamiti cenna- nirupādherbādhānavakāśāt /
svabhāvapratibaddhasya ca tatparityāge svabhāvaparityāgaprasaṅgāt /
tasmādbādhena vopādhirunnīyate, anyathā veti na kaścidviśeṣaḥ /
[ku.2.250] etena śrāvaṇatvācchabdatvavadityapi parāstam; atrāpi tasyaivopādhitvāt /
anyathā gandharūparasasparśā api nityāḥ prasajyeran; ghrāṇādyekaikendriyagrāhyatvāt gandhatvādivadityapi prayogasaukaryāt /
[ku.2.251] virodhavyabhicārāvasambhāvitāvevātretyasiddhireva (103)śiṣyate /

tathā hi- śabdastāvat "pūrvokta(104)nyāyena svābhāvikatīvramandataratamādibhāvena prakarṣanikarṣavānupalabhyate /
iyaṃ ca prakarṣanikarṣavattā kāraṇabhedānuvidhāyinī sarvatropalabdhā /
akāraṇakā hi nityāḥ prakarṣavanta eva bhavanti, yathā'kāśādayaḥ; nikṛṣṭā eva vā , yathā paramāṇvādayaḥ /
na tu kiñcadatiśayānāḥ kutaścidapakṛṣyante /
tadiyaṃ nityebhyo vyāvartamānā kāraṇavatsu (tāṃ) ca bhavantī jāyamānatāmādāyaiva viśrāmyatīti pratibandhasiddhau prayujyate- śabdo jāyate, prakarṣanikarṣābhyāmupatatvāt mādhuryādivat /
anyathā niyāmakamantareṇa bhavantī nityeṣvapi sā syāt (bhavatīti nitye 'pi syāt); niyamahetorabhāvāt /
śabdādanyatreyaṃ gatiriti cenna- sādhyadharmiṇaṃ vihāyeti pratyavasthānasya sarvānumānasulabhatvāt /
na ceha (105) vyañjakatāratamyādvyañjanīyatāratamyam; asvābhāvikatvaprasaṅgāt /
vyavasthitaṃ ca svābhāvikatvam /
na ca vyañjakotpādakābhyāmanyasyānuvidhānamasti /
na ca svābhāvikatvaupādhikatvābhyāmanyaḥ prakāraḥ sambhavati /
[ku.2.252] ṭhasyādetat /
tathāpyutpatternityatvena ko virodhaḥ? yena pratibandhasiddhiḥ syāt /
asiddhe ca tasmin, bhavatāṃ vyāpakatvāsiddhaḥ, asmākamaprayojakaḥ saugatānāṃ sandigdhavipakṣavṛtti(vyāvṛtti)rayamupakrānto hetuḥ" iti cet- na /
idaṃ hyutpattimattvaṃ vināśakāraṇasannidhiviruddhebhyo nityebhyaḥ svavyāpakanivṛttau nivartamānaṃ vināśakasannidhimati vināśini viśrāmyatīti /
"vināśakāraṇasannidhānenāvaśyaṃ jāyamānasya bhavitavyamiti kuto nirṇīta'miti cet- na tadasannidhānaṃ hi na tāvadākāśāderiva svabhāvavirodhāt; utpattivināśa(śaka)yoḥ saṃsargadarśanāt /
aviruddhayorasannidhistu deśaviprakarṣāddhimavadvindhyayoriva syāt /
deśayorapi viprakarṣo virodhādvā hetvabhāvādvā /
pūrvoktādeva na prathamaḥ /
dvitīyastu paṭakuṅkumayoriva syāt, yadi kuṅkumasamāgamādarvāgiva pradhvaṃsakasaṃsargādarvāgeva paṭo vinaśyet /
yathā hivināśakāraṇaṃ vinā na vināśaḥ, tathā yadi kuṅkumasamāgamaṃ vinā na vināśaḥ paṭasyeti syāt, kastayoḥ saṃsarga vārayet /
tasmādaviruddhayorasaṃsargaḥ kālaviprakarṣaniyamena vyāptaḥ /
sa (106)cāto nivartamānaḥ svavyāpyamupādāya nivartata iti pratibandhasiddhiḥ /
[ku.2.253] ṭhasyādetat /
yadyevamāsthiraḥśabdaḥ, kathamarthena saṅgatirasyopavabhyate" iti cet- yathaivārthasyāsthirasya (107)tena /
"jātireva padārthaḥ, na vyaktiriti cenna- śabdāttadalābhaprasaṅgāt /
ākṣepata iti cet- kaḥ khalvayamākṣepo nāma? tāvadanumānam; anantābhiḥsaha saṅgativadavinābhāvasyāpi grahītumaśakyatvāt /
śakyatve vā, saṅgaterapi tathaiva sugrahatvāt vyaktimātrarūpeṇāvinābhāva" iti cenna- vyaktitvasya sāmānyasyābhāvāt /
bhāve vā, tadākṣepe 'pi viśeṣānākṣepāt /
vācyatvamapi vā tathaivāstu? kimākṣepeṇa; saṅgateravirodhāditi /
[ku.2.254] arthāpattirākṣepa iti cenna- vyaktyā[ktiṃ] vinā kimanupapannam? "jāti'riti cenna- tannāśānutpādadaśāyāmapi sattvāt /
"tathāpi na vyaktimātraṃ vine'ti cenna- mātrārthābhāvāt /
"vyaktijñānamantareṇa jātijñānamanupapanna'miti cenna- tadabhāve 'pyutpādāt /
"vyaktiviṣayatāṃ (tvaṃ)vinā jātiviṣayatā tasyānupa(tānupa)panne'ti cenna- evaṃ tarhyekajñānagocaratāyāṃ kimanupapannaṃ (108)kiṃ pratipādayediti /
"jātīnāmanvayānupapattyā vyaktiravasīyata" iti cenna- (109)parasparāśrayaprasaṅgāt /
[ku.2.255] syādetat- pratibandhaṃ vināpi pakṣadharmatābalāt yathā liṅgaṃ viśeṣe paryavasyati, tathā saṅgatiṃ vināpi śabdaḥ śaktiviśeṣādviśeṣe paryavasyati /
sa evā'kṣepa ityucyate iti cet- na tāvat pratītiḥ krameṇa; apekṣaṇīyābhāvena viramyavyāpārāyogāt /
jātipratyāyanamapekṣata iti cet- kṛtaṃ tarhi śabdaśaktika(ktibhedaka)lpanayā; tāvataiva tatsiddheḥ /
omiti cenna- vyaktyanālambanāyā jātipratīterasambhavādityuktatvāt; pramāṇāntarāpātaprasaṅgācca /
smaraṇaṃ tadityayamadoṣa iti cenna- ananubhūtānanvayaprasaṅgāt /
astvekaiva pratītiriticet- kṛtaṃ tarhi śaktibheda(dvaya)kalpanayā /
[ku.2.256] evaṃ ca yathā sāmānyaviṣayā śaktirekaiva tadvati paryavasyati, tathā sāmānyāśrayāsaṅgatistadvati paryavasyediti /
na ca nityā api varṇāḥ svarānupūrvyādihīnāḥ padārthaiḥ saṅgamyante /
na ca tadviśiṣṭatvamapi teṣāṃ nityam /
tasmāttattajjātīyakroḍaniviṣṭā eva padārthāḥ padāni ca sambadhyante, nāto 'nyatheti, naitadanurodhenāpi śabdasya nityatvamāśaṅkanīyamiti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, objects and words are connected only as situated within the scope of their respective universals, and not otherwise — hence, the eternality of words should not be suspected even in deference to this [argument].

children.text: [ku.2.257] yadā ca varṇā eva na nityāḥ, tadā kaiva kathā puruṣavivakṣādhīnānupūrvyādiviśiṣṭavarṇasamūharūpāṇāṃ padānām? kutastarāṃ ca tatsamūharacanāviśeṣasvabhāvasya vākyasya? kutastamāṃ (māṃ ca?)tatsamūhasya vedasya? [ku.2.258] paratantrapuruṣa (110)paramparādhīnatayā pravāhāvicchedameva nityatāṃ brūma iti cet- etadapi nāsti; sargapralayasambhavāt /
children.translated_text: [Ku 2.257] And when the phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) themselves are not eternal, what then can be said of words, which have the form of collections of phonemes distinguished by sequence and other features dependent on the speaker's intention to express? Still less of the sentence, whose nature is a specific arrangement of such collections? And even less of the <s>Veda</s>, which is [merely] a collection of those? [Ku 2.258] [Objection:] If [it is said that] we call the unbroken continuity of the stream itself 'eternality,' due to dependence on a succession of dependent persons — this too does not hold, because of the occurrence of creation and dissolution.

children.text: ahorātrasyāhorātrapūrvakatvaniyamāt, karmaṇāṃ viṣamavipākasamayatayā yugapadvṛttinirodhānupapatteḥ, varṇādivyavasthānupapatteḥ, samayānupalabdhau(nupapattau)śābdavyavahāravilopaprasaṅgāt, ghaṭā(ṭapaṭā)disampradāyabhaṅgaprasaṅgācca kathamevamiti cet- [ku.2.259] ucyate- varṣādivad bhavopādhiḥ vṛttirodhaḥ suṣuptivat /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Because of the rule that day and night are preceded by [another] day and night, because the simultaneous cessation of all activities is impossible given that the times of maturation of <s>karmas</s> (actions) are unequal, because the arrangement of phonemes and the like would be impossible [to re-establish], because upon the non-apprehension of conventions there would be the undesirable consequence of the destruction of verbal usage, and because there would be the undesirable consequence of the breakdown of traditions [of making] pots and the like — how can this [creation and dissolution] be so? [Ku 2.259] It is said: The limiting condition of existence [is periodic] like the rains and the like; the cessation of activity is like deep sleep;
Phonemes are like sprouts and scorpions; conventions and the like are like magic. || 2 ||

tatpūrvakatvamātre siddhasādhanāt(nam), anantaratatpūrvakatve aprayojakatvāt; varṣādidinapūrvakataddinaniyamabhaṅgavadupapatteḥ /
rāśyādiviśeṣasaṃsargarūpakālopādhiprayuktaṃ hi tat; tadabhāva eva vyāvṛtteḥ /

na ca tadanutpannamanaśvaraṃ vā; avayavitvāt /

bhavati ca sarvasyaiva (112)susvāpaḥ /
krameṇa, na tu yugapaditi cenna- kāraṇakramāyattatvātkāryakramasya /

children.translated_text: And given such a state of affairs, enjoyment too is to be accomplished by <s>karmas</s> (actions) in just this way, without transgressing the nature of things — thus, from the two-atom aggregate up to the cosmic egg and everything in between, this is the very course [of things] — and so the invariable concomitance is established.

children.text: [ku.2.266] tathā ca brahmāṇḍe paramāṇusādbhavitari paramāṇuṣu ca svatantreṣu pṛthagāsīneṣu tadantaḥpātinaḥ prāṇigaṇāḥ (119)kva vartantām, kupitakapikapolāntargatodumbaramaśakasamūhavat, davadahanadahyamānadārūdaravighūrṇamānaghuṇasaṅghātavat, pralayapavanollāsanīyaurvānalanipātipotasāṃyātrikasārthavadveti /
children.translated_text: [Ku 2.266] And thus, when the cosmic egg has dissolved into its ultimate atoms, and the atoms are independent and situated separately, where do the living beings contained within it dwell? — Like a swarm of gnats inside a fig fruit in the cheeks of an angry monkey, or like a mass of woodworms whirling about in the hollows of logs being burned by a forest fire, or like a group of merchants in a boat that is falling into the submarine fire stirred up by the wind of dissolution.
[Ku 2.267] Moreover: From the observed decrease in the power of birth, <s>saṃskāra</s> (purificatory rites), learning, and the like, and of <s>svādhyāya</s> (Vedic recitation) and ritual actions,
Let the decline of the tradition be measured. || 3 ||

[Objection:] If [it is argued that creation must be] preceded by [something of the same kind] — this is establishing what is already established; if [the requirement is that it be] immediately preceded, that is ineffective, because it is explained like the breaking of the rule that such-and-such a day is preceded by a day of such-and-such a kind, as with rainy days. For that [regularity] is caused by a temporal limiting condition in the form of the conjunction of specific zodiacal signs and the like; and the cessation [of the pattern] occurs precisely when that [condition] is absent. Similarly here too, since [the periodicity of creation] is caused by a temporal limiting condition in the form of the continued existence of the cosmic egg, which is the reason for the continuation of creation — what fault is there if the cessation occurs precisely when that [condition] is absent? And that [cosmic egg] is not unproduced, nor is it imperishable, since it has parts. [Ku 2.260] And the cessation of activity is also explained as being like the state of deep sleep. children.translated_text: Because the power to create [bodies] without [a pre-existing] body and the supernatural powers (<s>vibhūti</s>) of <s>aṇimā</s> etc. must necessarily be accepted [for God].

children.translated_text: If it be said: let there be one [such being] only — [we reply:] no, for then there is no confidence in anyone other than God.
[Ku 2.267] Moreover: from the observation of decline in the power of birth, sacramental rites, learning, etc., and of Vedic study and ritual action,
the decline of the tradition should be inferred. (Verse 3)

[Ku 2.278] What then is this acceptance by the great multitude? It is the learning, retention, understanding, practice, etc. [of the Veda] by those devoid of perception of [independent] reasons. For that [acceptance] would not occur here without a cause.
[Ku 2.279] Now, laziness etc. is not the cause [of Vedic acceptance]; because it chiefly involves actions that are painful. Nor is it the case that, having accepted the authority [of the Veda] as already established elsewhere, one enters here without qualification and as having no other recourse; because even those revered by others do not enter here [in that way]. Nor is it an attachment to food, drink, etc. arising from non-discrimination; because [the Veda] is primarily concerned with prescribing the division of these. Nor is it delusion arising from the force of habitual sophistry; because the practice [of Vedic acceptance] begins from childhood. Nor is it the contact with possibly deceptive heretical [teachers]; because the practice proceeds in succession from father etc. Nor is it the intention of freedom from exertion through pride in yogic practice; because the beginner is even more exerted in the ritual portion (<s>karmakāṇḍa</s>) alone. Nor is it livelihood; because, by the reasoning stated earlier, there is no visible fruit. Nor is it deceit and trickery; because that is impossible in the present case.
[Ku 2.280] However, these reasons are possible for the acceptance of the Buddhist and other scriptures. For thus: since there is greater lightness of action there, lazy people [accept them]; since even those fallen from here can enter, those with no other recourse [accept them]; since there is no restriction on food etc., those with attachments [accept them]; since acceptance is by one's own will, those habituated to sophistry [accept them]; since practice is not [inherited] in succession from father etc., those in contact with heretics [accept them]; since they hear [statements] like 'Knowing the difference between both, for whom is purity ordained?', those who pride themselves on freedom from exertion [accept them]; since livelihood is assured through [receiving] meals every seven <s>ghaṭikās</s> etc., the unqualified [accept them]; since they are captivated by tricks such as stopping the sun, splitting rocks, breaking branches, spirit possession, statues speaking, and alchemy — it is plausible that those deceived by trickery accept them. Therefore, they are not accepted by the great multitude — this is the distinction.
[Ku 2.281] It may be objected: if thus all actions are opposed to continued existence, nothing arises, nothing perishes — in a universe like motionless space, whence would re-creation arise from what distinction? 'From the transformation of <s>prakṛti</s>' — this suits the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>. 'From the transformation of <s>Brahman</s>' — this is proper in the lineage of <s>Bhāskara</s>. 'From the maturation of impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>)' — this follows the Buddhist doctrine. 'From a temporal distinction' — this is improper due to the absence of distinguishing conditions. And non-existent adventitious factors cannot serve as differentiators; because they are of identical nature at all times. 'Nor through knowledge as a door' — because if that [knowledge] is non-eternal, it is absent at that time; and if eternal, there is no distinction either in its object or its nature — [if this is the objection,] no.
[Ku 2.282] Just as in beings who have fallen asleep due to the fatigue of bodily agitation, the continuity of breathing persists with the sole purpose of gradually bringing about the maturation of lifespan — so too, for the atoms that have acquired dispositions through the agitation of the dissolution of the great elements, the continuity of the series of actions called 'accumulation' (<s>pracaya</s>), culminating in conjunction, which is the exhalation of <s>Īśvara</s> (God), persists — [with levels of] sluggishness being less and less [gradual] — with the sole purpose of temporal demarcation. As to the question 'how long is this [period]?' — since there is no contradiction, following scriptural tradition, it is inferred to be just that [scripturally stated] duration of time. Or the activity within another <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg) serves as the condition for time. In that time-segment, re-creation [occurs]. Just as fruits are strung along the vine of a gourd, so thousands of cosmic eggs are threaded upon the power of the Supreme Lord — thus it is heard [in scripture].
[Ku 2.283] When such interruption is possible, whose acceptance of whom [would establish] authoritativeness? And this [matter of Vedic authority] is informative (<s>jñāpaka</s>), not productive (<s>kāraka</s>). Hence, how could an effect that ceases due to the absence of a productive [cause] be maintained by what is merely intended as informative?
[Ku 2.284] It may be objected: there exist <s>Kapila</s> and others who have directly perceived <s>dharma</s>, who are accomplished through <s>karma-yoga</s>. They, seeing beings roasting on the coals of <s>saṃsāra</s>, being supremely compassionate, will grace [them] with instructions on what is dear and beneficial — what need of a Supreme Lord who lacks comprehensive knowledge of the number of insects etc.? — No, because there is no confidence in anyone other [than God]. For thus: even granting that the means for perceiving supersensory objects is meditation, it does not necessarily produce a true direct perception; so that we may have confidence. If it be said: because of agreement with other means of valid knowledge — [the example of] non-injury (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) etc. [confirms this] — no, because that [agreement] is absent in the [claim that meditation] is a means to well-being. If it be said: there is scriptural authority — no, because that too, having mere meditation as its root, is itself the subject of non-confidence. If it be said: there is engagement even from partial agreement — no, because, as in dream-narratives, it could be otherwise. And there is no meditation on what is not perceived. For even thieves, serpents, etc. that are perceived are [then] meditated upon by the fearful.
[Ku 2.285] And the efficacy of <s>karma</s> and <s>yoga</s> as means to well-being has not been perceived from any source. Nor is the perception of their essential nature of use anywhere, nor is it attainable by meditation. Nor is positive and negative concomitance possible here; because the fruit pertains to another body [in a future life]; and because in the practice of that [in this life], that [fruit] is absent due to its not being experienced. Nor does the continuity of both bodies — as agent and experiencer — establish that; because of the absence of that [continuity]. For no one connects: 'I am now experiencing the fruit of this previous <s>karma</s>.'
[Ku 2.286] Even the mere supposition that 'some may become so [i.e., directly perceiving]' does not inspire confidence; because there is no proof for the determination [of who they are]. If it be said that confidence in <s>Kapila</s> etc. comes from mutual agreement — like a teacher who falls asleep at nightfall and wakes at dawn, [confirming each other's reports] — no, because there is no proof for connecting [experiences across] different births as there is for connecting [experiences within] a single birth. And even so, without connecting [the previous birth's] Brahmin status etc. through the particular qualification [of the person], there is no confidence of the form that would [justify] practice. For there is no rule that Brahmin status in a subsequent [birth] follows from the parents' Brahmin status in a previous birth; by which the establishment of <s>varṇa</s> and other duties at the beginning of creation would be possible. Because of the non-perception of distinctions in elements determined by particular unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), as in the case of God [being required for such determination]. And the non-confidence in supersensory perception has already been stated.
[Ku 2.287] By this, the [view that] the tradition is propagated by the orderly arrangement of <s>varṇas</s> migrating between cosmic eggs is also set aside — because of the absence of the power of such migration. For it is indeed difficult to travel to another continent. How then [could there be] travel to another world? And how much more so, travel to another cosmic egg? If it be said that through the attainment of the powers of <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute) etc. this too would be possible — no, because of the absence of proof even for that. From mere supposition, confidence cannot arise. If it be said that the inability to explain the acceptance by the great multitude in any other way is itself the proof here — no, because when the explanation is possible through the postulation of just one such [being, i.e., God], there would be the fault of superfluity in postulating more.
