syādetat- taddharmā iha na santītyavagate, arthādāpadyate- ihāvidyamānāstatra santīti /
na hi tadvidharmatvametasyopapadyate, yadyetadvidharmāsau na bhavati iti cet- evaṃ tarhi prakṛtamapyarthāpattireva /
na hi tatsādṛśyaviśiṣṭatvametasya pratyakṣasiddhamapi tasyaitatsādṛśyaviśiṣṭatvaṃ vinopapadyate /
[ku.3.352] etena dṛṣṭā(189)sannikṛṣṭapratyabhijñānaṃ vyākhyātam /
tatrāpi taddharmaśālitvaṃ tasya smaraṇābhivyaktamanupapadyamānaṃ tadidantāspadasyaikatāṃ vyavasthāpayati /
children.translated_text: Even there, the fact that it possesses those properties, which is made manifest through recollection and cannot be otherwise accounted for, establishes the identity [of the referred thing] with the object of the 'that-this' [judgment].
Therefore, <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) is not an additional [means of knowledge].

children.text: [ku.3.353] evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate- sambandhasya paricchedaḥ (190)(daṃ?) sañjñāyāḥsañjñinā saha /
children.translated_text: [Ku 3.353] When [the matter] has thus arrived [at this conclusion], it is stated: The ascertainment of the relation of a name with its named object —
Since it cannot be accomplished by perception and the like, the wise know it to be the result of <s>upamāna</s> (analogy). || 10 ||

For when one cognizes 'that is dissimilar from this,' the same [analysis] applies there too. For that [cognition of dissimilarity] is not perception, since it has a non-proximate object. It is not recollection, since the qualified [object] has not been experienced [before]. It is not <s>upamāna</s> (analogy), since its object is dissimilarity. [Objection:] But the dissimilarity of that [thing] is precisely its being qualified by the absence of the properties of this [thing], and that is acknowledged to be known through absence itself. And let not [the same apply] in the present case, since similarity is a positive entity. No, [we reply] — because being qualified by properties excluded from this also has the form of dissimilarity, and that too is a positive entity. [Further objection:] It may be said: when it is known that 'the properties of that do not exist here,' it follows as a matter of course that 'those which do not exist here exist there.' For that is not [established otherwise].

children.text:
yath.ā gaustathā gavayaḥ iti śrutātideśavākyasya, gosadṛśaṃ piṇḍamanubhavataḥ, smarataśca vākyārthaṃ ayamasau gavayaśabdavācya iti bhavati matiḥ /
seyaṃ na tāvat vākyamātraphalam, anupalabdhapiṇḍasyāpi prasaṅgāt /
nāpi pratyakṣaphalam, aśrutavākyasyāpi prasaṅgāt /
nāpi samāhāraphalam, vākyapratyakṣayorbhinnakālatvāt /
vākyatadarthayoḥ smṛtidvāropanītāvapi gavayapiṇḍasambaddhenāpīndriyeṇa tadgatasādṛśyānupalambhe samayaparicchedāsiddheḥ /
phalasamāhāre tu tadantarbhāve anumānāderapi pratyakṣatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
tat kiṃ tatphalasya tatpramāṇabahirbhāva eva? antarbhāve vā kiyatī sīmā?- tattadasādhāraṇendriyādisāhityam /
asti tarhi sādṛśyādijñānakāleviṣphāritasya cakṣuṣo vyāpāraḥ- na- upalabdhagosādṛśyaviśiṣṭagavayapiṇḍasya vākyatadarthasmṛtimataḥ kālāntare 'pyanusandhānabalāt samayaparicchedopapatteḥ /
[ku.3.354] nanu ca vākyādevānena samayaḥ paricchinnaḥ, gosadṛśasya gavayaśabdaḥsañjñeti /

prayogādva'numitaḥ, yo yatrāsati vṛttyantare vṛddhaiḥ prayujyate, sa tasya vācakaḥ, yathā gośabda eva goḥ, prayujyate cāyaṃ gosadṛśe iti kimupamāneneti- na- sādṛśyasyānimittatvānnimittasyāpratītitaḥ /

na hi gavayaśabdasya sādṛśyaṃ pravṛttinimittam, apratītagūnāmavyavahāraprasaṅgāt /
nacobhayamapi nimittam, svayaṃpratītasamayasaṅkrāntaye 'tideśavākyaprayogānupapatteḥ /
gavayattve hyayaṃ vyutpanno vṛddhavyavahārāt, na sādṛśye /
kathametannirdhāraṇīyamiti cet- vastugatistāvadiyam, tadāpātataḥsandehe 'pi na phalasiddhiḥ, gandhavattvamiva pṛthivītvasya, gosādṛśyaṃ gavayaśabdapravṛttinimittasyopalakṣaṇam, idameva vā nimittamityanirdhāraṇāt /

[ku.3.355] syādetat- pūrvaṃ nimittānupalabdherna phalasiddhiḥ, idānīntu tasminnupalabdhe tadeva vākyaṃ smṛtisamārūḍhaṃ phaliṣyati, adhyayanasamayagṛhīta iva vedarāśiraṅgopāṅgaparyavadātasya kālāntare /
na ca vācyam, vākyena (191) svārthasya prāgeva bodhitatvāt prāgevaparyavasitamiti- gosādṛśyasyopalakṣaṇanimittatvayoranyataratra tātparye sandehāt /
idānīntu gavayatve 'vagate tarkapuraskārātsādṛśyasyopalakṣaṇatāyāṃ vyavasthitāyām, gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa itivadanvayapratipattiriti cet- na- śrutānvayādanākāṅkṣaṃ na vākyaṃ hyanyadicchati /

gosadṛś.o gavayaśabdavācya iti sāmānādhikaraṇyamātreṇānvayopapattau viśeṣasandehe 'pi vākyasya paryavasitatvena mānāntaropanītānapekṣaṇāt, taktāraktasandehe 'pi ghaṭo bhavatīti vākyavat /
anyathā vākyabhedadoṣāt /
na ca gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa itivat padārthā evānvayāyogyāḥ, yena pramāṇāntaropanītenānvayaḥsyāt /
atha (192)pratītavākyārthabalāyāto 'pyartho yadi vākyasyaiva, divābhojananiṣedhavākyasyāpi rātribhojanamarthaḥsyāt /
tasmādyathā gavayaśabdaḥ kasyacidvācakaḥ śiṣṭaprayogāditi sāmānyato niścite 'pi, viśeṣe mānāntarāpekṣā, tathā gosadṛśasya gavayaśabdo vācaka iti vākyānniścitepi sāmānye, viśeṣavācakatve 'sya mānāntaramanusaraṇīyamiti /
[ku.3.356] astvanumānam /
tathāhi- gavayaśabdo gavayasya vācakaḥ asati vṛttyantare 'bhiyuktaistatra prayujyamānatvat,gavi gośabdavaditi cet- na- asiddheḥ /
na hyasati vṛttyantare tadviṣayatayā prayogaḥsaṅgatimavijñāya jñātuṃ śakyate /
sāmānādhikaraṇyāditi cenna- piṇḍamātre siddhasādhanāt, nimitte cāsiddheḥ, sādṛśyasyānimittatvādityuktam /
[ku.3.357] nanu vyāptiparamidaṃ vākyaṃ syāt, yo gosadṛśaḥ sa gavayapadārtha iti /
tathāca vākyādavagatapratibandho 'numinuyāt- ayamasau gavayo gosadṛśatvāditideśavākyāvagatapiṇḍavaditi- na- viparyayāt /
na hi gosadṛśaṃ buddhāvāropyānena pṛṣṭaḥ, sa kiṃ śabdavācya iti /
kintu sāmānyato gavayapadārthamavagamya sa kīdṛgiti /
tathāca yadyogaprāthamyābhyāṃ tasyaiva vyāpyatvam /
tataḥ kiṃ tena, prakṛtānupayogāt /
[ku.3.358]
 atha (193)kiṃlakṣaṇako 'sāviti praśnārthaḥ /
tadā vyatirekiparaṃ (194)syāt, lakṣaṇasya tathābhavāt /
tathāca gosadṛśo gavaya ityasyārthaḥ- yo gavaya iti na vyavahriyate nāsau gosadṛśa iti /
evañca prayoktavyam- ayamasau gavaya iti vyavahartavyaḥ gosadṛśatvāt, yastu na tathā, gosadṛśaḥ yathā hastī /
na ca hastyādīnāṃ vipakṣatve pramāṇamasti, sarvāprayogasya duravadhāra(ṇa)tvāt; katipayāvyavahārasya cānaikāntikatvāt /
[ku.3.359] nanu liṅgamātre praśno bhaviṣyati, kīdṛk kiṃ liṅgamiti- na- na hyanena liṅgamavijñāya gavayaśabdasya vācakatvaṃ kasyacidvācyatvaṃ vāvagatam, yena tadarthaṃ praśnaḥsyāt /
pravṛttinimittaviśeṣaliṅge praśnaḥ, yena nimittena gavayaśabdaḥ pravartate tasya kiṃ liṅgamiti cenna- na hi tadavaśyamanumeyamevetyanena niścitam, yata idaṃ syāt /
jñānopāyamātrapraśne tadviśeṣeṇottaramiti cenna- aviśeṣādindriyasannikarṣamapyuttarayet; paryāyāntaraṃ vā /
yathā- gavayamahaṃ kathaṃ jānīyāmiti praśne, vanaṃ gato drakṣyasīti; yathā vā- kaḥ pika ityatra, kokila iti /
tasmānnimittabhedapraśna evāyam, gavayo gavayapadavācyaḥ kīdṛk kena nimitteneti yuktamutpaśyāmaḥ /
tasya ca nimittaviśeṣasya sākṣādupadarśayitumaśkyatvāt pṛṣṭastadulakṣaṇaṃ kiñcidācaṣṭe /
taccopamānasāmagrīsamutthāpanameva /
tasya ca pramāṇasya satastarkaḥsahāyatāmāpadyate- "sādṛśyasyaiva nimittatāyāṃ kalpanāgauravam, nimittāntarakalpane ca kḷptakalpyavirodha" iti tadeva nimittamavagacchatīti /
[ku.3.360] lakṣaṇantvasya anavagatasaṅgatisañjñāsamabhivyāhṛtavākyārthasya sañjñinyanusandhānamupamānam /
vākyārthaśca kvacit sādharmyaṃ kvacidvaidharmyam /
ato nāvyāpakam /
tasmānniyataviṣayatvādeva na tena bādhaḥ, na tvanatirekāditi sthitiḥ /
ku.3.[361ṭaśabdo 'pi na bādhakamanumānānatirekāditi vaiśeṣikādayaḥ /
tathā hi- yadyapi ete padārthā mithaḥ saṃsargavantaḥ vākyatvāditi vyadhikaraṇam; padārthatvāditi cānaikāntikam; padaiḥsmāritatvādityapi tathā /
yadyapi caitāni padāni smāritārthasaṃsargavanti tatsmārakatvādityādau sādhyābhāvaḥ /
na hyatra matvarthaḥ saṃyogaḥ samavāyastādātmyaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo vā sambhavati /
jñāpyajñāpakabhāvastu svātantryeṇa anumānāntarbhāvavādibhirneṣyate /
na ca liṅgatayā jñāpakatvaṃ yat liṅgasya (195) viṣayastadeva tasya, parasparāśrayaprasaṅgāt /
tadupalambhe hi vyāptisiddhistatsiddhau ca tadanumānamiti /
tathāpi- ākāṅkṣādimadbhiḥ padaiḥ smāritatvāt gāmabhyājeti padārthavaditi syāt /
na ca viśeṣāsiddhirdeṣaḥ, saṃsargasya saṃsṛjyamānaviśeṣādeva viśiṣṭatvāt /
yadvā etāni padāni smāritārthasaṃsargajñānapūrvakāṇi ākāṅkṣādimattve sati tatsmārakatvāt gāmabhyājeti padavat /

children.translated_text: And there is no non-establishment of the probandum in this way, because it is established precisely through being a delimitor of knowledge.
And because only what is presented [to cognition] as being connected serves as a delimitor, there is no failure to apprehend the particular.

children.text: [ku.3.362] atrocyate- anekāntaḥ paricchede sambhave ca na niścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Ku 3.362] Here it is said: There is inconclusiveness regarding delimitation, and where [connection] is possible, there is no certainty.
Expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) is the cause, along with existence; fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) and contiguity (<s>āsatti</s>) are not the [independent] basis [of sentence-meaning]. (Verse 13)

[Ku 3.356] [The sentence] 'That which resembles a cow is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>' — when the connection (<s>anvaya</s>) can be accounted for through mere co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) alone, even when there is doubt about the particular, the sentence has reached its conclusion without depending on another means of knowledge, just as [in the case of] the sentence 'this is a pot' even when there is doubt whether it is red or yellow. Otherwise, there would be the fault of splitting the sentence. Nor are the word-meanings here unfit for connection, as in 'a cowherd-settlement on the Ganges,' so that the connection would require [something] supplied by another means of knowledge. If it be said that whatever meaning arises by the force of the understood sentence-meaning also belongs to the sentence — then even the sentence prohibiting eating during the day would have as its meaning eating at night. Therefore, just as the word <s>gavaya</s>, even when it is determined in general from the usage of the learned that it denotes something, requires another means of knowledge for the particular [identification]; so too, even when it is determined in general from the sentence that the word <s>gavaya</s> denotes what resembles a cow, another means of knowledge must be sought for its denotation of the particular.
[Ku 3.356 cont.] Let it be inference. For thus: the word <s>gavaya</s> denotes the <s>gavaya</s> [animal], because in the absence of another denotative convention, it is used for that [animal] by the learned — like the word <s>go</s> (cow) for a cow — [if this is the argument,] no — because of non-establishment. For in the absence of another convention, its being applied to that object cannot be known without knowing the connection. If [it be established] from co-referentiality — [this was] already accomplished for the mere individual (<s>piṇḍa</s>), and the ground (<s>nimitta</s>) is unestablished, and similarity is not the ground — this has been stated.
[Ku 3.357] Now, this sentence might have universal concomitance as its purport: 'Whatever resembles a cow is the referent of the word <s>gavaya</s>.' And thus, having understood the invariable relation from the sentence, one would infer: 'This is that <s>gavaya</s>, because of resembling a cow' — like the individual apprehended from a pointing-sentence — no, because of the reversal. For the one who was asked, having superimposed 'cow-resemblance' on his cognition, [was] not [asked] 'What word denotes that?'; rather, having understood the referent of <s>gavaya</s> in general, [he was asked] 'What does it look like?' And thus, by priority of connection, that [cow-resemblance] itself is the pervaded [term]. Then what is the use of that, since it is irrelevant to the matter at hand?
[Ku 3.358] If the meaning of the question is 'What is its distinguishing mark?' — then [the sentence] would have the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) as its purport, since that is the nature of a distinguishing mark. And thus the meaning of 'a <s>gavaya</s> resembles a cow' is: 'Whatever is not referred to as <s>gavaya</s>, that does not resemble a cow.' And so, the application should be: 'This should be referred to as <s>gavaya</s>, because of resembling a cow; whatever is not so [referred to], [yet] resembles a cow, like an elephant.' But there is no proof that elephants etc. are the counter-examples, because the universal non-use [of the term] is difficult to ascertain; and the occasional non-use is inconclusive.
[Ku 3.359] Now, the question might be merely about the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) — 'What kind, what mark?' — no, for he did not, without knowing the mark, understand either the denotation of the word <s>gavaya</s> or that it denotes something, so that the question would be for that purpose. If the question is about the specific mark that is the ground of application — 'What is the mark of that ground by which the word <s>gavaya</s> is applied?' — no, for he had not determined that it must necessarily be inferred, so that this [question] would arise. If the question is merely about the means of knowledge — the answer would be about a particular [means] — no, he might also answer with sense-contact which is non-specific; or with a synonym. For example, to the question 'How shall I know a <s>gavaya</s>?' [the answer might be] 'Go to the forest, you will see [one].' Or to 'Who is the <s>pika</s>?' [the answer:] 'The <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo).' Therefore, this is a question about the specific ground of application. That the <s>gavaya</s>, denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>, is of what kind, by what ground — this is what we rightly discern. And since that specific ground cannot be directly shown, the one asked states some defining characteristic of it. And that is precisely the bringing about of the aggregate [of conditions for] comparison (<s>upamāna</s>). And for that valid means of knowledge, once it exists, reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) becomes an auxiliary — reasoning that 'postulating similarity alone as the ground avoids conceptual excess, while postulating another ground contradicts what is already established' — thus one understands that very [similarity] as the ground.
[Ku 3.360] The definition of this [comparison] is: the recognition of the named [object] — whose name, uttered together with [a description of] the connection [between name and referent] that was not previously understood — [constitutes] comparison (<s>upamāna</s>). And the sentence-meaning is sometimes similarity, sometimes dissimilarity. Therefore, it is not under-inclusive. Hence, the position is that because it has a determined domain, there is no sublation by it [i.e., by inference]; and not because it is not different [from inference].
[Ku 3.361] Verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) too is not sublated, because it is not merely a non-different [form] of inference — [say] the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and others. For thus: although 'these word-meanings are mutually connected, because of being a sentence' — [this inference] has the wrong locus; and 'because of being word-meanings' is inconclusive; and 'because of being remembered by words' is likewise. And although 'these words are associated with the connection of remembered meanings, because of being reminders thereof' — here the property to be proved is absent. For here neither the possessive relation, conjunction, inherence, identity, nor the qualifier-qualified relation is possible. And the relation of 'what is made known and what makes known' is not accepted by those who advocate the inclusion [of testimony] within inference, as [being] independent. Nor can the making-known [function] in the capacity of a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) have as its object the very thing that is the object of the mark — because of mutual dependence. For the establishment of pervasion depends on the apprehension of that [object], and the inference [of that object] depends on its [the pervasion's] establishment. Even so: 'because of being recalled by words having expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) etc., [these word-meanings are connected] like the word-meanings of <s>gām abhyāja</s> (drive the cow near)' — [this might work]. And the non-establishment of the particular is not a defect, because the connection is specific precisely through the specificity of what is being connected. Or: 'These words have as their antecedents the knowledge of the connection of recalled meanings, because, given that they have expectancy etc., they are reminders thereof — like the words of <s>gām abhyāja</s>.'

children.text:
et.e padārthāmithaḥsarṅgavanta iti saṃsṛṣṭā eveti niyamo vā sādhyaḥ sambhāvitasaṃsargā iti vā /
[ku.3.363] na prathamaḥ, anāptoktapadakadambasmāritairanekāntāt /
āptoktyā viśeṣaṇīyamiti cenna- vākyārthapratīteḥ prāk tadasiddheḥ /
na hyavipralambhakatvamātramihāptaśabdena vivakṣitam, tadukterapi padārthasaṃsargavyabhicārāt /
apitu tadanubhavaprāmāṇyamapi /
na caitacchakyam (196)asarvajñe sarvadā sarvaviṣaye satyajñānavānayamiti niścetum, bhrānteḥ puruṣadharmatvāt /
yatra (197)kvacidāptatvamanāptasyāpyastīti na tenopayogaḥ /
tato 'sminnarthe 'yamabhrānta iti kenacidupāyena grāhyam /
nacaitat saṃsargaviśeṣamapratītya śakyam; buddherarthaṃbhedamantareṇa nirūpayitumaśakyatvāt /
padārthamātre cābhrāntatvasiddhau na kiñcit; anāptasādhāraṇyāt /
eteṣāṃ saṃsarge 'yamabhrānta iti śakyamiti cenna- eteṣāṃ saṃsarge ityasyā eva buddherasiddheḥ /
ananubhūtacare smaraṇāyogāt, tadanubhavasya liṅgādhīnatayā tasya ca viśeṣaṇāsiddhatvenānupapatteriti /
[ku.3.364ṭa nāpi dvitīyaḥ, yogyatāmātrasiddhāvapi saṃsargāniścayāt, vākyasya ca tadekaphalatvāt /
yogyatāmātrasya prāgeva siddheḥ /
anyathā tadasiddhāvāsannasākāṅkṣapadasmāritatvādityeva hetuḥsyāt /
tathācāgninā siñcedityādinā smāritairanaikāntaḥ; tathāvidhānāṃ sarvathā saṃsargāyogyatvāditi /
[ku.3.365] evaṃ dvitīye 'pi prayoge heturākāṅkṣādimattve satīti /
tatra keyamākāṅkṣā nāma? na tāvadviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ, tasya saṃsargar(gaviśeṣa)svabhāvatayā sādhyatvāt /
nāpi tadyogyatā, yogyatayaiva gatārthatvāt /
nāpyavinābhāvaḥ, nīlaṃ sarojamityādau tadabhāve 'pi vākyārthapratyayāt /
tatrāpi viśeṣākṣiptasāmānyayoravinābhāvo 'stīti
 (vopyākāṅkṣeti) cenna- aho vimalaṃ jalaṃ nadyāḥ, kacche mahiṣaścaratītyādau vākyabhedānupapattiprasaṅgāt /
nāpi pratipatturjijñāsā, paṭo bhavatītyādau śuklādijijñāsāyāṃ (sayā)raktaḥ paṭo bhavatītyasyaikadeśavat sarvadā vākyāparyavasānaprasaṅgāt /
"guṇakriyādyaśeṣaviśeṣajijñāsāyāmapi padasmāritaviśeṣajijñāsā ākāṅkṣā /
paṭa ityukte kiṃrūpaḥ, kutra kiṃ karotītyādirūpajijñāsā /
tatra, bhavatītyukte, kiṃ karotītyeṣaiva padasmāritaviṣayā, na tu kiṃ rūpa ityādirapi /
yadā tu rakta ityucyate, tadā kiṃrūpa ityeṣāpi smāritaviṣayā syāt iti na kiñcidanupapanna'miti cet- evaṃ tarhi cakṣuṣī nimīlya paribhāvayatu bhavān, kimasyāṃ jātāyāmanvayapratyayaḥ atha jñātāyāmiti /
tatra prathame nānayā vyabhicāravyāvartanāya (vāraṇāya)heturviśeṣaṇīyaḥ, manaḥsaṃyogādivatsattāmātreṇopayogāt /
āsattiyogyatāmātreṇa viśiṣṭastu niścito 'pi na gamakaḥ; ayameti putro rājñaḥ puruṣo 'pasāryatāmityādau vyabhivacārāt /
[ku.3.366ṭadvitīyastu syādapi, yadyanumānāntaravattatsadbhāve 'pi tajjñānavaidhuryādanvayapratyayo na jāyate /
natvetadasti, āsattiyogyatāmātrapratisandhānādeva sākāṅkṣasya sarvatra vākyārthapratyayāt /
nivṛttākāṅkṣasya ca tadabhāvāt /
kathameṣa niścayaḥ, sākāṅkṣa eva pratyeti, na tu jñātākāṅkṣa iti cet- tāvanmātreṇopapattāvanupalabhyamānajñānakalpanānupapatteḥ /
anyatra tathā darśanācca /
yathā (dā) hi dūrāddṛṣṭasāmānyo jijñāsate ko 'yamiti, pratyāsīdaṃśca, sthāṇurayamiti pratyeti, tadāsya jñātumahamicchāmītyanuvyavasāyābhāve 'pisthāṇurayamityartha(nvaya)pratyayo bhavati- tathehāpyaviśeṣāt viśeṣopasthānakāle saṃsargāvagatireva jāyate, na tu jijñāsāvagatiriti /
na ca viśeṣopasthānātprāgeva jijñāsāvagatiḥ prakṛtopayoginī, tāvanmātrasyānākāṅkṣā(ṅkṣa)tvāt /
[ku.3.367] na caivambhūto 'pyayamaikāntiko hetuḥ /
yadā hyayameti putro rājñaḥ puruṣo 'pasāryatāmiti vaktoccārayati, śrotā ca vyāsaṅgādinā nimittena ayameti putra ityaśrutvaiva; rājñaḥ puruṣo 'pasāryatāmiti śṛṇoti, tadāstyākāṅkṣādimattve sati padakadambakatvam? na ca smāritārthasaṃsargajñānapūrvakatvamiti /
[ku.3.368ṭasyādetat- yāvatsamabhivyāhṛtatvena viśeṣite hetau nāyaṃ doṣaḥ, tathāvidhasya vyabhicārodāharaṇāsaṃsparśāt /
kutastyastarhi katipayapadaśrāviṇaḥ saṃsargapratyayaḥ? aliṅga eva liṅgatvādhyāropāt /
etāvānevāyaṃ samabhivyāhāra iti tatra śroturabhimānaḥ- na- tatsandehe 'pi śrutānurūpasaṃsargāvagamāt /
bhavati hi tatra pratyayaḥ, na jāne kimaparamanenoktam, etāvadeva śrutam, yadrājñaḥ puruṣo 'pasāryatāmiti /
bhrāntirasāviti cet- na tāvadasau duṣṭendriyajā, parokṣākāratvāt /
na liṅgābhāsajā, liṅgābhimānābhāve 'pi jāyamānatvāt /
etāvatpa(dṛkpa)dakadambapratisandhānameva tāṃ janayatīti cet /
yadyevam, tadevāduṣṭaṃ sadabhrāntiṃ janayat kena vāraṇīyam /
vyāptipratisandhānaṃ vināpi tasya saṃsargapratyāyane sāmarthyāvadhāraṇāt cakṣurādivat /
[ku.3.369] nāstyeva tatra saṃsargapratyayaḥ; asaṃsargāgrahamātreṇa tu tathā vyavahāra iti cet- tarhi yāvatsamabhivyāhāreṇāpi viśeṣaṇenāpratīkāraḥ, tathābhūtasyānāptavākyasya saṃsargajñānapūrvakatvābhāvāt /
asaṃsargāgrahapūrvakatvamātre sādhye na vyabhicāra iti cet- evaṃ tarhisaṃsargo na siddhyet /
āptavākyeṣu setsyatīti cenna- sarvaviṣayā'ptatvasyāsiddheḥ, yatra kvacidāptatvasyānaikāntikatvāt, prakṛtaviṣaye cāptatvasiddhau saṃsargaviśeṣasya prāgeva siddhyabhyupagamādityuktam /
[ku.3.370] na ca sarvatra jijñāsā nibandhanam, ajijñāsorapi vākyārthapratyayāt /
ākāṅkṣāpadārthastarhi kaḥ? jijñāsāṃ prati yogyatā /
sā ca smā(198)ritatadākṣiptayora(ptā)vinābhāve sati śrotari tadutpādyasaṃsargāvagamaprāgabhāvaḥ /
na caiṣo 'pi jñānamapekṣate, (199)pratiyoginirūpaṇādhīnanirūpaṇatvāttadabhāvasya, tasya ca viṣayanirūpyatvāditi /

[ku.3.371] prābhākarastu lokavedasādhāraṇavyutpattibalenānvitābhidhānaṃ prasādhya vedasyāpauruṣeyatayā vaktṛjñānānumānānavakāśāt saṃsarge śabdasyaiva svātantryeṇa prāmāṇyamāsthiṣata; loke tvanumānata eva vaktṛjñānopasarjanatayā saṃsargasya siddheranvitābhidhānabalāyātepi pratipādakatve 'nuvādakatāmātraṃ vākyasyeti nirṇītantaḥ /

yāvatī hi vede sāmagrī, tāvatyeva loke 'pi bhavantī kathamiva nārthaṃ gamayet /
nahyapekṣaṇīyāntaramasti /
liṅge tu paripūrṇe 'pyavagate vyāptismṛtirapekṣaṇīyāstīti, vilambena kiṃ nirṇeyam; anvaya(artha)sya prāgeva pratīteḥ /
[ku.3.372ṭaloke vakturāptatvaniścayo 'pekṣaṇīya iti cenna-
 tadrahitasyāpi svārthapratyāyane śabdasya śakteravadhāraṇāt /
anyathā vede 'pyarthapratyayo na syāt, tadabhāvāt /
na ca loke anyānyeva padāni; yena śaktivaicitryaṃ syāt /
anāptoktau vyabhicāradarśanāt tulyāpi sāmagrī sandehena śithilāyate iti cenna- cakṣurādau vyabhicāradarśanena (rasatvena) śaṅkāyāmapi satyāṃ jñānasāmagrītastadutpattidarśanāt /
jñāyamānasyāyaṃ vidhiḥ, yat sandehe sati na niścāyakam,(200) yathā liṅgam; cakṣurādi tu sattayeti cenna- vākyasya niścatatvāt; āptoktatvasya cārthapratyayaṃ pratyanaṅgatvāt /
loke 'pi cāptatvāniścaye 'pi vākyārthapratīteḥ /
bhavati hi vedānukāreṇa paṭhyamāneṣu apauruṣeyatvābhimānino gauḍa(201)mīmāṃsakasyārthaniścayaḥ /
na cāsau (cāyaṃ) bhrāntiḥ, pauruṣeyatvaniścayadaśāyāmapi tathāniścayā(thātvā)diti /
[ku.3.373] syādetat- nāptoktatvamarthapratīteraṅgamiti brūmaḥ; kintvanāptoktatvaśaṅkānirāsaḥ (sam) /
sa ca kvacidapauruṣeyatvaniścayāt, kvacidāptoktatvāvadhāraṇāditi cet- tat kimapauruṣeyatvasyāpratītau, sandehe vā vedavākyādviditapadārthasaṅgaterarthapratyaya eva na bhavet, bhavannapi vā na śraddheyaḥ? prathame satyādaya eva pramāṇam /
nacāsaṃsargāgrahe tadānīṃ saṃsargavyavahāraḥ, bādhakasyātyantamabhāvāt /
tathāpi tatkalpanāyāmanvayocchedaprasaṅgāt /
dvitīye tvaśraddhā pratyakṣavat nimittāntarānnivartsyatīti vede yadi, loke 'pi tathā syādaviśeṣāt /
[ku.3.374] anyathā vedasyāpyanuvākatāprasaṅgaḥ (ṅgāt) /

children.translated_text: [We] say [in response]:
[Listen] —
Since the words — free from the suspicion of defects in [any particular] person — cause recollection, these [word-meanings]

children.text: anvitā iti nirṇīte vedasyāpi na tat kutaḥ // 15//
children.translated_text: are connected [in their meanings]. When this is established, how could even the <s>Veda</s> lack that [capacity]?  [verse 15]

For whatever [epistemic] aggregate exists in the <s>Veda</s>, that very same exists in ordinary [speech] too — how could it not convey the meaning? For there is nothing additional that needs to be expected. But when the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is fully understood, the recollection of invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) remains to be expected — so what is to be ascertained through the delay? Since the meaning of the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is already understood beforehand. [Ku.3.372] [Objection:] In ordinary [speech], the ascertainment of the speaker's trustworthiness is to be expected. — No, because the power of the word to convey its own meaning is established even without that [trustworthiness]. Otherwise, in the <s>Veda</s> too there would be no understanding of meaning, since that [trustworthiness of a speaker] is absent [in an authorless Veda]. Nor are the words in ordinary [speech] entirely different [from Vedic words], such that there would be a difference in [their] denotative power. [Objection:] Because deviation is seen in untrue statements, even an equal [epistemic] aggregate becomes weakened by doubt. — No, because even when doubt arises due to observed deviation in the eyes and other [sense-organs], the generation [of knowledge] is observed from the knowledge-aggregate. [Objection:] This is the rule for what is [already] being known — that when there is doubt, it does not produce certainty, just like an inferential mark; but the eyes and the like [do so] simply by existing. — No, because the sentence produces certainty; and because the trustworthiness of the speaker is not a subsidiary factor for the understanding of meaning. For even in ordinary [speech], there is understanding of sentence-meaning even without certainty of the speaker's trustworthiness. Indeed, a <s>Gauḍa</s> (Bengali) <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> who believes in the authorlessness [of the Veda] achieves certainty of meaning when [Vedic texts] are recited in imitation of the Veda. Nor is that an error, because even in the state of certainty of [the Veda's] being authored, such certainty [of meaning] obtains. [Ku.3.373] It may be objected: We do not say that the trustworthiness of the speaker is a subsidiary of meaning-cognition; rather, [what is needed is] the removal of the suspicion of untrustworthiness. That is [achieved] sometimes by the certainty of authorlessness, sometimes by the ascertainment of the speaker's trustworthiness. — Then what? Would there be no understanding of meaning at all from a Vedic sentence whose word-meanings are known, when authorlessness is not cognized, or when it is doubtful? Or would such understanding, even if it occurs, not be worthy of trust? In the first case, the means of knowledge [for meaning] are only [the words'] truth and the like. And when the connection [of word-meanings] is not [yet] grasped, there is no employment of [sentence-]connection at that time, because a sublating cognition is entirely absent. Even with such a postulation, there would follow the destruction of [all] positive concomitance. In the second case, if the distrust is to be removed by some other cause, as with perception, then in the case of the <s>Veda</s>, the same should apply in ordinary [speech] too, since there is no distinction. [Ku.3.374] Otherwise, even the <s>Veda</s> would have the unwanted consequence of being merely repetitive.

[ku.3.375] kiṃ cedamanvitābhidhānaṃ nāma? na tāvadanvitapratipādanamātram, avivādāt /
nāpi svārthābhidhāyāstatra tātparyam, avivādādeva /

children.translated_text: But [only] through expressing the word-meanings; not otherwise.

children.text: yathā tavaiva, āptasya saṃsargaparatayā padasamabhivyāhāramātreṇa; na tvanyathā /
children.translated_text: Just as for you too, [it is] merely through the utterance of words by a trustworthy person with the intention of [conveying] the connection; not otherwise.

children.text: anyathā gurumatavidāmeva śloka āptapadaprakṣepeṇa paṭhanīyaḥ- prāthamyādabhidhātṛtvāt tātparyopagamādapi /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, the following verse should be recited by those who know the teacher's doctrine, with the insertion of the word 'trustworthy': 'Due to priority, due to being the expresser, and due to the acceptance of intention,
let that power be attributed to trustworthy [speakers] alone — [that would be] better.'

For when the position is that the <s>Veda</s> says nothing at all prior to the certainty of its authorlessness, then — just as in ordinary [speech] after the certainty of the speaker's trustworthiness — in the <s>Veda</s> too, after the certainty of authorlessness, inference enters subsequently. But this is the specific [point]: here, taking the word-meanings themselves as the subject, words that possess [the properties of] expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) and the like and are free from the suspicion of human defects — since they cause recollection — establish connection [of meanings] as a whole, just like word-meanings recalled by a collection of words spoken by a trustworthy person; whereas in the other case [ordinary speech], [the connection] is mediated by [awareness of the] intellect [of the speaker]. In result, there is no difference whatsoever. And thus even in the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (expression of connected meaning) view, because of its secondary status, the <s>Veda</s> would have the unwanted consequence of being merely repetitive. And in that case, there is no means of knowledge [for it]. For the power of words to [convey] that [connected meaning] must be postulated only through the otherwise-inexplicability of the cognition of a qualified [meaning]. And that is accomplished by inference alone — so the effort [to postulate a separate word-power] is futile. Therefore, the [view that] words in ordinary [speech] are merely repetitive is the perverse postulation of the venerable [opponents]. [Ku.3.375] What indeed is this 'expression of connected meaning' (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>)? It is not merely the communication of connected [meaning], since there is no dispute [about that]. Nor is it the intention (<s>tātparya</s>) of [words] that express their own meaning toward that [connected meaning], since again there is no dispute. Nor is it the communication of that [connected meaning] through the force of syntactic connection (<s>saṅgati</s>), since the sentence-meaning is novel (<s>apūrva</s>). Nor through the force of [each word's] own-meaning connection, since that is exhausted in its own meaning alone. Nor is that very connection the producer of both, since the order of cognition cannot be accounted for. If simultaneity is conceded, then even without the synthesis of fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) and the like, there would be the unwanted consequence of sentence-meaning cognition just like word-meaning cognition. Nor is it proper [to say] that the same connection is independent with respect to [conveying] one's own meaning but has a subsidiary function of word-meaning communication with respect to sentence-meaning — since that [connection] is not itself an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). For the connected words are the instrument, not the connection [itself]. [Objection:] The words endowed with connection conducive to that communication [are the instrument]. — [We reply:] The conduciveness of connection to sentence-meaning communication is not [established] as its basis, since [connection] has only the general as its domain, or only the possessor of that [general] as its domain. Nor as having a function conducive to that, since it has been said that [connection] is not an instrument. If [its conduciveness is] through generating the instrumental function conducive to that — we have no dispute about that. [Objection:] The power [of words] is in the connected [meaning] itself. — [We] have said: because sentence-meaning is novel, and because the order of cognition cannot be accounted for. [Ku.3.376] [Objection:] The connection is [between] the action as recollected and the [grammatical] factor involved, and [between] the action and the recollected factors involved in it. Hence there is no room for the stated faults. Nor does the consequence of synonymy follow, since there is restriction by predominance. Nor is there redundancy, since the intention is toward the specific connection. Nor mutual dependence, since [each word] does not depend [on others] for recollecting its own meaning. Nor does sentence-splitting follow, since when the word-meanings of each other are recalled in proximity, nothing further is needed. — [We reply:] What is the meaning of 'grasping the connection in the connected'? If wherever there is connection, by virtue of that object, [the meaning] is connected with [other] word-meanings — nothing useful for the present [discussion follows]. For just because the capacity of the eye is known with respect to some object, it does not follow that tangibility too is its domain, by virtue of that object. If the meaning is that linguistic competence (<s>vyutpatti</s>) [is acquired] there in the connected form itself — that is wrong, for lack of a means of knowledge. [Ku.3.377] [Objection:] The otherwise-inexplicability of the cognition of connected meaning [is the proof]. — No, because it is explained even by the <s>abhihitānvaya</s> [view]. Let the [objection about] expectancy remain. For if connection-in-general is not known, there would be no desire to know a specific connection. — No, because it is explained even through implication (<s>ākṣepa</s>), just as when a specific [kind of] fruit is seen, there arises the desire to know [its] specific taste. [Ku.3.378] [Objection:] Without the potency of words, cognition of connection could arise from anywhere among the recalled word-meanings. But that does not happen. Therefore, word-power must necessarily be postulated. — Then how do poets' poems shine? For there is no such thing as sentence-composition without cognizing a specific connection. And in one's own imagination, neither perception, inference, verbal testimony, nor their semblances are possible — apart from word-meaning recollections arising through mental intention. [Objection:] That is non-grasping of the connection. — For me, it is precisely a grasping of the connection. And for you too, the same sequence of words sometimes culminates in connection and sometimes in non-grasping of connection — so whence the difference? [Ku.3.379] [Objection:] By virtue of the speaker's being trustworthy or untrustworthy. — Does such a speaker produce some specific [effect] there? Or is the speaker himself the distinguisher through determination? In the first case, you too bear the burden of postulating [word-]power, just like the <s>abhihitānvaya</s> proponents. In the second case, let the words too, just like the speaker, serve as distinguishers through determination. [Objection:] Then the words too would have a role in the cognition of connection. — What doubt [is there about that]?
Thus.

[ku.3.380] tasmāt prakārāntareṇa saṃsargapratyayo bhavatu mā vā, padārthānāmākāṅkṣādimattve sati abhihitānāmavaśyamanvaya iti kuto 'tiprasaṅgaḥ? [ku.3.381] na caivaṃ sati padārthā eva karaṇam, teṣāmanāgatādirūpatayā kārakatvānupapattau tadviśeṣasya karaṇatvasyāyogāt /
tatsaṃsarge pramāṇāntarāsaṅkīrṇodāharaṇābhāvācca /
padānāṃ tu pūrvabhāvaniyamena padārthasmaraṇāvāntaravyāpāravattayā tadupapatteḥ; vyāpārasyāvyavadhāyakatvāditi kṛtaṃ prasaktānuprasaktyā /
children.translated_text: But for words, this [instrumentality] is established because, through the rule of prior occurrence, they have the subsidiary function of causing recollection of word-meanings; and because [their] function is not an intervening [obstacle]. Thus enough of digression upon digression.

children.text: [ku.3.382] astu tarhi śabda eva bādhakaṃ sarvajñe kartari /
children.translated_text: [Ku.3.382] [Objection:] Then let verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) itself be the sublating cognition against an omniscient creator.

children.text: tathāhi- prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: For thus: 'Actions are performed in every way by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature);
the self deluded by ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) thinks: "I am the doer."'  [<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 3.27, verse 14 in this text]

[Ku.3.380] Therefore, whether or not the cognition of connection arises through some other means, when word-meanings possess expectancy and the like, there is necessarily connection of the expressed [meanings] — so whence the overextension? [Ku.3.381] Nor in that case are the word-meanings themselves the instrument, since when their form is [partly] future and the like, their being causal factors is impossible, and therefore the specific [property of] being an instrument would not apply. And because there is no example uncontaminated by other means of knowledge in [establishing] their connection.
