(g.ī.) ityādi paṭhanti /
asyāyamarthaḥ- na pāramārthikaṃ cetanasya kartṛtvamasti /

children.translated_text: That [agency] is merely due to egoism (<s>abhimāna</s>).
And there is no egoism in an omniscient being (<s>sarvajña</s>).

children.text: na cāsarvajñasya jagatkartṛtvamasti- ucyate- na pramāṇamanāptoktirnādṛṣṭe kvacidāptatā /
children.translated_text: Nor does a non-omniscient being have the capacity to create the universe. In reply — "A statement not by a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) is not a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>); nor is there trustworthiness regarding the unseen in any case.

children.text: adṛśyadṛṣṭau sarvajño na ca nityāgamaḥ kṣamaḥ //16 //
children.translated_text: One who sees the unseen is omniscient; and an eternal scripture (<s>āgama</s>) is not capable [of providing this authority]." || 16 ||
They recite [from the <s>Gītā</s>] and so forth. The meaning of this is: there is no ultimate agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) of a conscious being.

children.text:
yadi hi sarvajñakartrabhāvā'vedakaḥ śabdo nāptoktaḥ, na tarhi pramāṇam /
athāpto 'sya vaktā, kathaṃ na tadarthadarśī /
atīndriyārthadarśīti cet- kathamasarvajñaḥ, kathaṃ vā na kartā, āgamasyaiva praṇayanāt /
children.translated_text: "He is a seer of supersensible objects." — If so, how then is he not omniscient, and how is he not an author, since he indeed composed the scripture (<s>āgama</s>)?
And the possibility of an eternal scripture has been refuted, since [Vedic] lineages have been broken — as has been demonstrated.

children.text: [ku.3.383] apica- na cāsau kvacidekāntaḥ sattvasyāpi pravedanāt /
children.translated_text: [ku.3.383] Moreover — "Nor is that [teaching of God's non-existence] invariable in any case, since [scripture] also teaches [His] existence.
And [scripture] purposed to teach the stainless (<s>nirañjana</s>) [Self] is not, even when [teaching God's] existence, directed toward that [as its primary intent]." || 17 ||
For if a verbal statement that does not convey the authorship of an omniscient being is not an authoritative utterance (<s>āptokti</s>), then it is not a valid means of knowledge.

children.text:
nahyasattvapakṣa evāgamo niyataḥ, īśvarasadbhāvasyaiva bhūyaḥsu pradeśeṣu pratipādanāt /
tathācāgre darśayiṣyāmaḥ /
tathāca sati kvacidasattvapratipādanamanekāntaṃ na bādhakam /
sattvapratipādanamapi tarhi na sādhanamiti cet- āpātatastāvadevametat /
yadā tu niḥśeṣaviśeṣaguṇaśūnyātmasvarūpapratipādanārthatvamakartṛkatvāgamānāmavadhārayiṣyate tadā na tanniṣedhe tātparyamamīṣāmiti sattvapratipādakānāmevāgamānāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti /
na ca teṣāmapyanyatra tātparyamiti vakṣyāmaḥ /
[ku.3.384] astvarthāpattistarhi bādhikā /
tathāhi- yadyabhaviṣyat, nopādekṣyat /

children.translated_text: For it is not that He does not know how to set [beings] in motion without instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>).
Therefore instruction itself, being otherwise inexplicable, indicates the absence of such [an indifferent God] or His indifference. — No, because it is explicable otherwise.
"In the absence of the cause, the effect is absent; when the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is absent, there is no valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>).
From its absence, there is no activity — and even in the doctrine of <s>karma</s>, this same rule applies." || 18 ||

For scripture (<s>āgama</s>) is not confined to the thesis of [God's] non-existence, since the very existence of <s>Īśvara</s> is taught in the majority of passages. And this we shall demonstrate further on. And that being so, the occasional teaching of non-existence is inconclusive (<s>anekānta</s>) and not a refutation. "Then the teaching of existence too is not a proof." — At first glance, this is so. But when the teaching of the self's nature as devoid of all particular qualities is examined, those [passages] are understood to teach freedom from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>, not the absence of all qualities whatsoever. Otherwise the teaching of omniscience etc. would also be negated. And even if [some passages] teach the absence of [certain] qualities, they establish [God's] existence by that very act of teaching — for they address a real entity. Moreover, in the <s>Vedānta</s> passages, statements like "from whom these beings are born" etc. directly teach a sentient cause of the universe. Therefore the teaching of existence is more abundant and hence stronger than the teaching of non-existence.

children.text:
buddhipūrvāṃ hi pravṛttirna buddhimanutpādya śakyasampādanā /
na ca prakṛte buddhirapyupadeśamantareṇa śakyasiddhiḥ, tasyaiva tatkāraṇatvāt /
bhūtāveśanyāyena pravartayediti cet- pravartayedeva, yadi tathā phalasiddhiḥ syāt /
na tvevam /
kuta etadavasitam? upadeśānyathānupapattyaiva /
yasyāpi mate adṛṣṭavaśādeva bhūtānāṃ pravṛttiḥ, tasyāpi tulyametat /
yadyasti pravṛttinimittamadṛṣṭam, kimupadeśena, tata eva pravṛttisiddheḥ /
na cet, tathāpi kimupadeśena, tadabhāve tasmin satyapyapravṛtteḥ /
nityaḥ svatantra upadeśo na paryanuyojya iti cet- yūyaṃ paryanuyojyāḥ, ye tama(mana)vadhānato dhārayanti vicārayanti ceti /
children.translated_text: "An eternal, independent instruction is not to be questioned." — You are the ones to be questioned, who maintain and examine that [scripture] by [mere] mental attention.

children.text: [ku.3.385] na cārthāpattiranumānato bhidyate, loke tadasaṅkīrṇodāharaṇābhāvāt prakārāntarābhāvācca /
children.translated_text: [ku.3.385] Nor does <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) differ from <s>anumāna</s> (inference), since in common experience there are no examples where they are unmixed, and since there is no other manner [of operation].
For: "There is no impropriety regarding what is not subject to restriction; nor does a non-restrictor serve as a justification.
There is no contradiction between the two means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>); and even regarding what is well-known, that [objection] applies equally." || 19 ||

For purposeful activity (<s>buddhipūrvā pravṛtti</s>) cannot be accomplished without first producing cognition. And in the present case, even cognition cannot be established without instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>), since that very [instruction] is its cause. "He could set [beings] in motion by the method of spirit-possession (<s>bhūtāveśa</s>)." — He could indeed, if thereby the result would be accomplished. But it is not so. How is this known? By the very inexplicability [of the result] without instruction. Even according to those in whose view the self, being omniscient, does not require instruction — even for them, instruction is useful for removing the obscuration of beginningless ignorance. Without instruction, the self does not attain that [removal], even though it is intrinsically omniscient. Therefore instruction is indeed necessary.

children.text:
jīvaṃścaitro gṛhe nāstīti anupapadyamānamasati bahiḥsadbhāve, tamāpa(māve)dayatītyudaharanti /
tatra cintyate- kimanupapannaṃ jīvato gṛhābhāvasyeti /
na hyaniyamayasyāniyāmakaṃ vinā kiñcidanupapannam, atiprasaṅgāt /
nanu svarūpameva /
tat na tāvadbahiḥ sattvena kartavyam, tadakāryatvāt tasya /
sthitirevāsya tena vinā na syādityasya svabhāva iti cet- evaṃ tarhi tanniyatasvabhāva evāsau; vyāptereva vyatirekamukhanirūpyāyāstathāvyapadeśāt /
[ku.3.386] kathaṃ vā (ca) bahiḥsattvamasyopapādakam? na hi aniyāmako bhavannapyaniyamyamupapādayati, atiprasaṅgādeva /
svabhāvo 'sya, yadanena
 bahiḥsattvena gehāsatvaṃ kroḍīkṛtya sthātavyamiti cet- seyaṃ vyāptirevānvayamukhanirūpyā tathā vyapadiśyate iti /
[ku.3.387] na vayamavinābhāvamarthāpattāvapajānīmahe, kintu tajjñānam /
na cāsau sattā mātreṇa tadanumānatvamāpādayatīti cet- na- anupapattipratisandhānasyāvaśyābhyupagantavyatvāt /
anyathātvatiprasaṅgāt /
arthāpattyābhāsānavakāśācca /
yadā hyanyathaivo(thāpyu)papannamanyathānupapannamiti manyate, tadāsya viparyayaḥ, na tvanyatheti /
[ku.3.388] tathāpi kathamatra vyāptirgṛhyeteti cet- yadāhamiha tadā nānyatra, yadānyatra tadā neheti sarvapratyakṣāsiddhametat; kā tatrāpi kathantā? sarvadeśāpratyakṣatve tatrābhāvo duravadhāraṇa ityapi nāsti, teṣāmeva saṃsargasyātmani pratiṣedhāt /
ayogyānāṃ pratiṣedhe kā vārteti cet- tadavayavānāṃ tatsaṃsargapratiṣedhādevānumānāt; anyeṣāṃ na kācit /
na hyakāraṇībhūtena paramāṇunā nedaṃ saṃsṛṣṭamiti niścetuṃ śakyamiti /
[ku.3.389] na cā(nāpya)vinābhāvaniścayenāpi gamayannapakṣadharmor'thāpattiriti yuktam- pakṣadharmatāyā animittatvaprasaṅgāt; aviśeṣāt /
vyadhikaraṇenāvinābhāvaniścayāyogācca; yat (203) yatra yadeti prakārānupapatteḥ /
[ku.3.390] pramāṇayorvirodhe arthāpattiravirodhopapādikā, na tvevamanumānamityapi nāsti /
virodhe hi rajjusarpādivadekasya bādha eva syāt, na tūbhayoḥ pramāṇyam /
prāmāṇye vā na virodhaḥ, sthūlamidamekamitivat sahasambhavāt; caitro 'yamayaṃ tu maitra itivadvā viṣayabhedāt /
prakṛte kvāpyastīti sāmānyato gehasyāpi praveśādekaviṣayatāpyastīti cet- yadyevam, kvacidasti kvacinnāstītivanna virodhaḥ /
atrāpi virodha eveti cet- ekaṃ tarhi bhajyeta /
[ku.3.391] na bhajyeta, arthāpattyā ubhayorapyupapādanāditi cet- kimanupapadyamānam? virodha evānyathānupapadyamāno vibhinnaviṣayatayā vyavasthāpayatīti cet- athābhinnaviṣayatayaiva kiṃ na vyavasthāpayet /
vyavasthāpanamavirodhāpādanam /
ekaviṣayatayaiva cānayorvirodhaḥ /
sa kathaṃ tayaiva śamayitavyaḥ na hi yo yadviṣamūrcchitaḥ, sa tenaivotthāpyate iti cet- ekaviṣayatayā anayorvirodha ityetadeva kutaḥ /
vibhinnadeśasvabhāvatayaiva sarvatropalambhāditi cet- nanviyaṃ vyāptireva /
tathāca ghaṭṭakuṭyāṃ (204) prabhātamiti /
[ku.3.392] dhūmopi vānupapadyamānatayaiva vahniṃ gamayet /
na hi tena vinā asāvupapadyate /
virodho 'pi- dhūmādvahninā bhavitavyam,anupalabdheśca na bhavitavyamiti /
tathācānu palabdherarvāgbhāgavyavasthāpanam, dhūmasya ca vyavadhānenānupalabhyavahniviṣayatvasthitirarthāpattiriti kuto 'numānam /
vahnimānayamityamanumānaṃ vyāpteḥ; anyathā anumānābhāve virodhāsiddheḥ /
arvāgbhāgānupalabdhivirodhena parabhāge 'sya vahnirityasyārthāpattireveti cet- na- vyāpti grāhakeṇa pramāṇena virodhasyoktatvāt /
nāpyuttarā arthāpattiḥ /
anyathā pāṇḍaratvasyāpālālatvavirodhena pālālatvasthitirapyarthāpattireva syāt /
tadviśiṣṭasya tenaiva vyāpternaivamiti cet- yadyevam, arvāgbhāgānupalabhyamānavanhitvena (matvena) viśiṣṭasya dhūmasya tenaiva vyāpteḥ kathamevaṃ bhaviṣyatīti tulyam /
[ku.3.393] kevalavyatirekyānumānaṃ parābhimatamarthāpattiḥ; anvayābhāvāditi cet- evametāvatā viśeṣeṇānumāner'thāpattivyavahāraṃ na vārayāmaḥ /
tatrānumānavyavahāraḥ kuta iti cet- avinābhūtaliṅgasamutpanna(muttha)tvāt /
sādhyadharmeṇa vinā hyabhavanamanvayina iva vyatirekiṇo 'pyaviśiṣṭam, tanniścayaścānvayavyatirekābhyāmanyatareṇa veti /
tasmādarthāpattirityanumānasya paryāyo 'yam, tadviśeṣavacanaṃ vā pūrvavadādivaditi yuktam /

children.translated_text: [Ku 3.394] But it has been considered that non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) is not a sublating [means of knowledge].
Nor does it exceed perception and the like [in its scope].
On this it is said: Because of the directness of the cognition, because there is no diminishment of the sense-faculty,
Because the instrument [of cognition] is unknown, and because of the entry of a [positive] entity into the mind. || 20 ||

They cite the example: '<s>Caitra</s>, being alive, is not in the house' — [the fact that this] cannot be accounted for in the absence of his being outside, reveals that [he is outside]. There it is considered: what is unaccountable about the absence from the house of one who is alive? For nothing that does not determine is unaccountable without its determinant, due to over-extension. [Objection:] But it is its very nature. That [being outside] need not first be established by [the fact of] existence outside, since that [existence outside] is not an effect of it [the absence from the house]. [Objection:] If [it is said that] its continued existence would not be possible without that [being outside] — that is its nature — then it is of precisely such a determined nature; because the very <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), being established through the negative mode, is so designated. [Ku 3.386] And how can being outside be its establishing [ground]? For what does not determine, even while existing, does not establish what is not determined, due to over-extension alone. [Objection:] If [it is said that] it is its nature that this [person], together with being outside, must remain encompassing the absence from the house — this is the very <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), established through the positive mode, that is so designated. [Ku 3.387] [Objection:] We do not deny the invariable concomitance in <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), but [only] the knowledge of it. And it [arthāpatti] does not become inference merely by [the fact of] the existence [of invariable concomitance]. No, [we reply] — because the consideration of impossibility must necessarily be admitted. Otherwise, there would be over-extension. And there would be no room for semblances of <s>arthāpatti</s> (fallacious presumption). For when one thinks 'what is otherwise accounted for is not accounted for otherwise,' then its [arthāpatti's] reversal [occurs], not [the thought] 'it is not otherwise.' [Ku 3.388] Even so, how is the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) grasped here? [Reply:] 'When I am here, I am not elsewhere; when I am elsewhere, I am not here' — this is not established by any perception. What difficulty is there in that too? Even [the objection that] in the case of non-perception of all places, the absence there is difficult to ascertain — this too does not hold, because the conjunction of those very [places] with the self is negated. [Objection:] What problem is there in negating [conjunction with] those that are unfit? [Reply:] Because of inference from the very negation of conjunction with their parts; for others, there is none. For one cannot ascertain 'this is not conjoined with that atom' when that atom is not a cause [of the conjunction]. [Ku 3.389] Nor is it proper [to say] that <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is a thesis-property that reveals [something] even without the ascertainment of invariable concomitance — because of the undesirable consequence that the thesis-property would be without a reason; and because of the absence of a distinction [from inference]. And because the ascertainment of invariable concomitance is impossible with what has a different locus; because the mode 'what, where, what [exists]' cannot be accounted for. [Ku 3.390] [Objection:] When there is conflict between two <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) establishes non-contradiction, but inference does not do so. This too does not hold. For in a conflict, like the rope-snake and the like, one [of the two] alone would be sublated, and both cannot have validity.

children.text:
[ku.3.395] yā hi sākṣātkāriṇī pratītiḥ, sā indriyakaraṇikā, yathā rūpādipratītiḥ; tatheha bhūtale ghaṭo nāstītyapi /
sākṣātkāritvamasyā asiddhamiti cenna- ekajātīyatve jñātājñātakaraṇatvānupapatteḥ /
na hi tasminneva kārye tadeva karaṇamekadā jñātam ajñātañcaikadopayujyate, liṅgendriyayorapi vyatyayaprasaṅgāt, jñānasyākāraṇatvaprasaṅgācca /
na hi tadatipatyāpi bhavatastatkāraṇatvam,vyāghātāt /
tasmāt jñātānupalabdhijanyasya sākṣātkāritvāt tadviparītakāraṇakamidaṃ tadviparītajātīyamiti nyāyyām /
nanu kva nāma jñātānupalabdhirasākṣātkāriṇīmabhāvapratītiṃ janayati? tadyathā- nipuṇataramanusṛto mayā mandire caitraḥ; na copalabdha iti śrutyā śrotānuminoti, nūnaṃ nāsīdeveti /
etena prāṅnāstitāpi vyākhyātā /
nanu tathāpyavāntarajātibhedo 'stu; ajñātānupalabdhijanye sākṣātkārastu kuta iti cet- kāraṇavirodhāt kāryavirodhena bhavitavyamityuktameva /
[ku.3.396]
 ananyatropakṣīṇendriyavyāpārānantarabhāvitvācca /
adhikaraṇagrahaṇe tadupakṣīṇamiti cenna- andhasyāpi tvagindriyopanīte ghaṭādau rūpaviśeṣābhāvapratītiprasaṅgāt /
asti hi tasyādhikaraṇagrahaṇam /
asti ca pratiyogismaraṇam /
asti ca śyāmeraktatvasya yogyasyābhāvo 'nupalabdhiśca /
adhikaraṇagrāhakendriyagrāhyābhāvavādino 'pi samānametaditi cenna- pratiyogigrāhakendriyagrāhyo 'bhāva ityabhyupagamāt /
mamāpi pratiyogigrāhakendriyagṛhīte 'dhikaraṇe anupalabdhiḥ pramāṇamityabhyupagama iti cenna- vāyau tvagindriyopanīte rūpābhāvapratītyanudayaprasaṅgāt /
tathāpi tattatra sannikṛṣṭamiti cet- hantaivamananyatracaritārthamindriyamavaśyamapekṣaṇīyaṃ rūpābhāvānubhavena /
[ku.3.397] syādetat- tathāpi vastvantaragraha eva tasyopayoga iti cenna- tasya taṃ pratyakāraṇatvāt /
kāraṇatve vā mahāndhakāre karaparāmarśena sparśavaddravyābhāvaṃ na pratīyāt /
pratīyācca purovisphāritākṣaḥ pṛṣṭhalagnasyāśyāmatvam /
ārjavāvasthānamapyadhikaraṇasyopayujyate iti cet- tarhi nayanasannikarṣo 'pyupayokṣyate /
tadekasahakāriprabhāsannikarṣāpekṣaṇāt; vātāyana(205)vivaravisārikaraparāmṛṣṭe 'pyadhikaraṇe tadupalambhaprasaṅgācca /
[ku.3.398] tathāpi yogyatāpādanopakṣīṇañcakṣuḥ /
taditara(206)sāmagrīsākalye hyanupalabhyamānasyābhāvo niścīyate /
tacca cakṣuṣyadhirakaraṇasannikṛṣṭe sati syāditi cet- nanu paripūrṇāni kāraṇānyeva sākalyam /
tathāca kiṃ kutropakṣīṇam /
athānyonyamelanaṃ (207)mithaḥ pratyāsattyādiśabdavācyaṃ tadupakṣayaviṣayaḥ, na tarhi kvaciccakṣuḥ kāraṇaṃ syāditi /
na hi rūpādyupalabdhimapyasannikṛṣṭametadupajanayati /
[ku.3.399] athādhikaraṇasamavetakiñcidupalambho 'pi tadviṣayābhāvagrahe 'nupalabdherapekṣaṇīyaḥ /
tatastatredaṃ caritārtham /
vāyvādiṣu tu rūpādyabhāvapratītirānumānikī /
tathā(208)nupalabdhyā hyanumīyate, ayaṃ nīrūpo vāyuriti- na- asiddheḥ /
na hyupalambhābhāvo bhavatāmabhāvopalambhaḥ /
upalambhasyātīndriyatvābhyupagamāt /
prākaṭyābhāvenānumeya iti cenna- vāyau rūpavattāprākaṭyābhāvasyāpyasiddheḥ /
rūpābhāvena samānatvāt /
vyavahārābhāvenānumeya iti cenna- kāyavāgvyāpārābhāve 'pyupekṣājñānabhāvābhyupagamāt; mūkasvapnopapatteśca /
na ca vyavahārābhāvamātreṇānumātumapi śakyate, anaikāntikatvādasiddheśca /
tadviṣayastu vyavahārastadviṣayajñānajanyo vā, tadviṣayajñānajanako, vā tadāśrayadharmajanako vā /
tadabhāvaśca tajjñānatadāśrayadharmābhāvāntarbhūta evetyaśakyaniścaya eva /
ātmāśrayetaretarāśrayacakrakapravṛttiprasaṅgāt /
[ku.3.400] na cājñātasyopalambhādyabhāvasya liṅgatā /
na ca prākaṭyābhāvaḥ sattāmātreṇopalambhābhāvamāvedayatīti yuktam- liṅgābhāvasya tathātve 'tiprasaṅgāt /
avinābhāvabalena tu niyame tatpratisandhānāpatteḥ /
na hyavinābhāvaḥ sattāmātreṇa jñānahetuṃ niyamayati, dhūmādāvapi tathābhāvaprasaṅgāditi /
[ku.3.401] jñānapratyakṣatvena tvaddiśā bhaviṣyatīti cenna- śabdadhvaṃsādinoktottaratvāt /
[ku.3.402] apica pratiyogigrāhakendriyeṇādhikaraṇadharmapratītiranupalabdheraṅgamiti, tadrahitāyāstasyāḥ kāryavyabhicārādvyavasthāpyeta, vyāptibalādvā (208) /
na tāvaduktarūpānupalabdhistāṃ vinā abhāvapratyayamajanayantī dṛśyate /
nāpi vyāpteḥ, tathā sati vayau rūpābhāvapratyayastāmākṣipet, evambhūtatvāt /
anākṣepe vā,na tatkāraṇako bhavet, na vā bhavet /
tato na bhavatyeva, liṅgāttadutpatti(209)riti cet- nanu liṅgamapi saiva; na tattvāntaram /
yathā yonisambandho 'liṅgadaśāyāmindriyasannikarṣamapekṣate, liṅgadaśāyāṃ tu tadanapekṣa eva brāhmaṇyajñāne, tathaitat syāditi cenna- kāryajātibhedāttadupapatteḥ; prakṛte ca tadanabhyupagamāt /
pārokṣyāpārokṣye vihāyānyathāpyasau bhaviṣyatīti cenna- anupalambhāt /
sambhāvyate tāvaditi cet- sambhāvyatām, na tvetāvatāpi tamāśritya karaṇaniyamaniścayaḥ /
[ku.3.403] ajñātakaraṇatvācca /
yadajñāyamānakaraṇajaṃ jñānaṃ tatsākṣādindriyajam, yathā rūpapratyakṣam /
tathāceha bhūtale ghaṭo nāstīti jñānamiti /
yathā vā smaraṇamajñāyamānakaraṇajaṃ sākṣānmanojanma /
kutastarhi na sākṣātkāryanubhavarūpam? saṃskārātiriktasannikarṣābhāvāditi vakṣyāmaḥ /
[ku.3.404] tathāpi bhāvaviṣaye iyaṃ vyavasthā, abhāvajñānaṃ tvajñātakaraṇatve 'pi na sākṣādindriyajaṃ bhaviṣyatīti cenna- utsargasya bādhakābhāvena saṅkocānupapatteḥ /
anyathā sarvavyāptīnāṃ bhāvamātraviṣayatvaprasaṅgaḥ, aviśeṣāt /
tathāpi vipakṣe kiṃ bādhakamiti cet- nanvidameva tāvat /
anyadapyucyamānamākarṇaya /
tadyathā- akāraṇakakāryaprasaṅgaḥ, rūpādyupalabdhīnāmapi
 vānindriyakaraṇatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
na hyanumityādibhirupalabhyamānakaraṇikābhiścakṣurādivyavasthāpanam, apitvanupalabhyamānakaraṇikābhī rūpādyupalabdhibhireva /
yadyapi sākṣātkāritāpi tatraiva paryavasyati, tathāpi prathamato 'nupalabhyamānakaraṇatvameva prayojakaṃ cakṣurādikalpane /
na hyupalabhyamāne karaṇāntare sākṣātkāriṇīṣvapi tāsu cakṣurādi anupalabhyamānaṃ kaścidakalpayiṣyat /
ata evāsākṣātkāritve 'pi smṛtermana eva karaṇamupāgaman dhīrāḥ /
saṃskārastvarthaviśeṣaprattyāsattāvupayujyate, indriyāṇāṃ prāpyakāritvavyavasthāpanāt /
[ku.3.405] bhāvāveśācca cetasaḥ /
sarvatra hi bāhyārthānubhave janayitavye bhāvabhūtapramāṇāviṣṭameva ceta upayujyate, nāto 'nyatheti vyāptiḥ, tathaiva śakteravadhāraṇāt /
na hyanupalabdhimātrasahāyaṃ tat abhāve 'pyanubhavamādhātumutsahate, śabdaliṅgāderapekṣādarśanāt /
na ca yatra yadapekṣaṃ yasya janakatvamupalabdham,tadeva tasyaiva tadanapekṣaṃ janakamiti nyāyasaham /

children.translated_text: Because even without connection to wet fuel, there is the possibility of smoke arising from fire,
and thus the obsession with establishing the cause-effect relation has been refuted.
[Ku 3.406] Moreover: By capacity with respect to the counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>), by the non-intervention of operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>),
by being the locus of defects (<s>doṣa</s>), the sense organs (<s>indriya</s>) [are the instruments of absence-cognition], and by reasoning through alternatives. //21//

[Ku 3.395] That cognition which is perceptual (<s>sākṣātkāriṇī</s>) has a sense-organ as its instrument, like the cognition of color etc.; so too [the cognition] 'There is no pot on the ground.' If it be said that its perceptual character is unestablished — no, because if [cognitions of presence and absence] were of one universal, it would be impossible for the same instrument to be known and unknown [in the same respect]. For the same instrument is not employed in the same effect as both known and unknown at the same time; otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of interchangeability between a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and a sense-organ, and the absurd consequence that knowledge would not be a cause. Nor does it become a cause even by transcending that, because of contradiction. Therefore, since [the cognition] born from the non-perception of something known is perceptual, it is proper [to say] that this [cognition], being of an opposite kind, has an opposite kind of cause.

Now, where indeed does the non-perception of something known generate a non-perceptual cognition of absence? For example: 'I searched the palace most diligently for <s>Caitra</s>, and did not perceive [him]' — from this testimony, the hearer infers 'surely he was not there at all.' By this, the cognition of prior non-existence is also explained. Even so, let there be a sub-class distinction; but whence would a perceptual [cognition] arise from the non-perception of something unknown? — Because of the contrariety of causes, there must be contrariety of effects — this has already been stated.

[Ku 3.396] And because [perceptual absence-cognition] arises immediately after the operation of a sense-organ that is not employed elsewhere. If it be said that [the sense-organ] is employed in grasping the locus (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) — no, because there would be the absurd consequence that even a blind person, for whom a pot etc. is presented by the tactile sense, would have the cognition of the absence of a particular color. For he does have the grasping of the locus; he does have the recollection of the counterpositive; and there is the absence and non-perception of the suitable [property of] darkness or redness. If even those who hold that absence is grasped by the sense-organ that grasps the locus [face] the same [problem] — no, because they accept that absence is grasped by the sense-organ that grasps the counterpositive. If it be said: 'I too accept that non-perception is the means of knowledge when the locus is grasped by the sense-organ that grasps the counterpositive' — no, because there would be the absurd consequence that the cognition of the absence of color would not arise for wind presented by the tactile sense. If [it be said]: even so, that [sense-organ] is in contact with that [wind] — well then, a sense-organ that has served its purpose nowhere else must necessarily be relied upon for the experience of the absence of color.

[Ku 3.397] Even so, if it be said that its use is only in grasping another object — no, because it is not a cause of that [absence-cognition]. Or if it were a cause, then in deep darkness one would not cognize the absence of a tactile substance through touching with the hand. And yet, one who has eyes wide open in front does cognize the non-darkness of [an object] attached [to him] from behind. If it be said that the locus's being in a direct [facing] position is also required — then the contact of the eye would also be required. Because [this cognition] depends on the contact of light, which is one of the auxiliary causes of that [eye]; and because there would be the absurd consequence of [absence-]perception even when the locus is touched by the hand extending through a window-opening.

[Ku 3.398] Even so, [it may be said that] the eye is employed in establishing fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>). For the absence of what is not perceived is determined when there is completeness of the remaining aggregate [of conditions]. And that [completeness] would exist when the eye is in contact with the locus — [if this is argued,] but surely the causes in their completeness just are that totality. And so what is employed where? If the mutual meeting [of conditions], expressed by terms like 'mutual proximity,' is the subject of that employment — then nowhere would the eye be a cause. For even the perception of color etc. is not generated by this [eye] when not in contact.

[Ku 3.399] Now, [it may be argued that] the perception of some property co-located with the locus is also required as a component of non-perception for grasping the absence of that [property's] object. Then the [sense-organ] has served its purpose here. But in the case of wind etc., the cognition of the absence of color etc. would be inferential. 'By such non-perception one infers: this wind is colorless' — no, because of non-establishment. For the absence of perception is not, for you, the perception of absence; because you accept that perception is supersensory. If it be said: it is to be inferred through the absence of manifestation — no, because even the absence of manifestation of colorfulness in wind is unestablished; being on a par with the absence of color [itself]. If it be said: it is to be inferred through the absence of [verbal] usage — no, because even in the absence of bodily and verbal activity, you accept indifference and ignorance [as explanations]; and because the case of a mute person in a dream is possible. Nor can it be inferred merely from the absence of usage, because of inconclusiveness and non-establishment. For usage regarding that [color in wind] would be either produced by knowledge of that, or productive of knowledge of that, or productive of a property of that substrate. And the absence of that [usage] is included within the absence of that knowledge and that substrate-property — so it is impossible to determine. Because of the absurd consequences of self-dependence, mutual dependence, and circular reasoning.

[Ku 3.400] And the absence of perception etc. of something unknown cannot serve as a mark (<s>liṅga</s>). Nor is it proper [to say] that the absence of manifestation, by mere existence, indicates the absence of perception — because of over-extension if the absence of a mark were [treated] thus. But if the restriction [is imposed] by the force of invariable concomitance, then the connecting of that [with the conclusion] would follow. For invariable concomitance does not restrict a cause of knowledge by mere existence; otherwise even in smoke etc. [the same] absurd consequence [would follow].

[Ku 3.401] If [it be said:] 'this will work in your system through the perceptibility of knowledge' — no, because this has already been answered regarding the destruction of sound etc.

[Ku 3.402] Moreover, if the cognition of a property of the locus by the sense-organ that grasps the counterpositive is a component of non-perception, then it should be established either through the deviation of the effect when that [component] is absent, or through the force of pervasion. Now, non-perception of the described form, without that [component], is not observed to generate absence-cognition. Nor [is it established] through pervasion; for in that case, the cognition of the absence of color in wind would require that [component], since it is of the same kind. If the [requirement] is waived — then [the absence-cognition] either would or would not be caused by that [non-perception]. Therefore, it simply does not [arise] — if it be said that its arising is from the mark [alone] — but surely the mark too is that very [non-perception]; it is not a different reality. Just as the birth-connection, in the non-mark stage, requires sense-contact, but in the mark stage is independent of it for the knowledge of Brahminhood — so too this [absence-cognition] might be — no, because of the difference of effect-universals; and because in the present case that [independence] is not accepted.

If it be said: 'setting aside the distinction between mediate and immediate [cognition], it will be possible otherwise too' — no, because of non-perception. If it be said: 'it is at least conceivable' — let it be conceived; but even so, there is no certainty regarding the restriction of instrumentality based on that [conception alone].

[Ku 3.403] And because [the absence-cognition's] instrument is unknown. That knowledge whose instrument is unknown is directly produced by a sense-organ, like the perception of color. So too the knowledge 'there is no pot on the ground.' Or, just as memory, whose instrument is unknown, is directly born from the mind. Then why is it not of the nature of direct experience (<s>anubhava</s>)? We will say: because of the absence of a contact beyond the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>).

[Ku 3.404] Even so, this determination applies to positive entities; but absence-cognition, even when its instrument is unknown, will not be directly produced by a sense-organ — [if this is argued,] no, because the general rule, in the absence of a sublating [cognition], cannot be restricted. Otherwise, all pervasions would apply only to positive entities — which is absurd, since there is no distinction [to warrant this]. Even so, what sublates [the general rule] in the counter-thesis? — Is not this very [argument] sufficient for now? But hear yet another that is being stated. Namely: the absurd consequence of an effect without a cause; the absurd consequence that even the perceptions of color etc. would not have a sense-organ as their instrument. For the determination of the eye etc. [as instruments] is not [made] by inferences etc., whose instruments are known, but rather by the very perceptions of color etc., whose instruments are unknown. Even though their perceptual character too ultimately rests on the same [criterion], still, primarily it is the unknown-instrument character itself that motivates the postulation of the eye etc. For no one would have postulated the eye etc. — even for those [cognitions] that are perceptual — if an [already] perceived instrument were [available]. For this very reason, the wise have accepted the mind alone as the instrument of memory, even though it is non-perceptual. The impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is useful for the proximity to the particular object, since the instruments [i.e., sense-organs] are established as acting through reaching [their objects].

[Ku 3.405] And because the mind is possessed by a positive entity (<s>bhāva</s>). For everywhere, when an experience of an external object is to be produced, the mind must be occupied by a means of valid knowledge that is a positive entity — and not otherwise — this is the pervasion, since the capacity is ascertained in just this way. For [the mind], aided by mere non-perception alone, is not capable of producing experience even in [the case of] absence, as is observed from the dependence on verbal testimony, marks, etc. Nor is it logically tenable that the very [instrument] which was observed to produce [an effect] of something only when dependent on [a certain factor], would produce that [same effect] of that very [thing] without depending on it.

children.text:
yaddhi pramāṇaṃ yadbhāvāvagāhi, tat tadabhāvagāhi, yathā liṅgaṃ śabdo vā; ghaṭādyavagāhi cendriyamiti /
anyathā hi śabdādikamapi nābhāvamāvedayet, bhāva eva sāmarthyāvadhāraṇāt /
na caivameva nyāyyam /
devadatto gehe nāstīti śabdāt, mayā tatra jijñāsamānenāpi na dṛṣṭo maitra ityavagatānupalabdhyānumānādapyavagateḥ /
[ku.3.407] grāhayatu vā'śrayamindriyam, tathāpi na tenedaṃ vyavadhīyate, vyāpāratvāt /
anyathā sarvasavikalpakānāṃ pratyakṣatvāya datto jalāñcaliḥ syāt /
nanvevaṃ sati dhūmopalambho 'pyasya vyāpāraḥsyāt /
tathā ca gatamanumānenāpīti cenna- yayā kriyayā vinā yasya yatkāraṇatvaṃ na nirvahati, taṃ prati tasyā eva vyāpāratvāt /
na ca dhūmādyupalabdhimantareṇa cakṣuṣo vanhijñānakāraṇatvaṃ na nirvahati saṃyogavaditi /
[ku.3.408] asti ca bhāvābhāvaviparyayaḥ /
so 'yaṃ yasya doṣamanuvidhatte, tadevātra karaṇamiti nyāyyam /
na cānupalabdhiḥ svabhāvato duṣṭā; nāpyadhikaraṇagrahaṇaṃ pratiyogismaraṇaṃ vā svabhāvato duṣṭam; anupatpattidaśāyāmanutpatteḥ,utpattidaśāyāñca svārthaprakāśanasvabhāvatāyā aparāvṛtteḥ /
asaṃsṛṣṭayoradhikaramapratiyoginoḥ saṃsṛṣṭatayā pratimānaṃ duṣṭam; saṃsṛṣṭayoścāsaṃsṛṣṭatayeti cet- nanvayameva viparyayaḥ /
tathācā'tmāśrayo doṣaḥ /
tasmādduṣṭendriyasya tadviparyayasāmarthye aduṣṭasya tatsamīcīnajñānasāmarthyamapi /
tathāca prayogaḥ- indriyamabhāvapramākaraṇaṃ tadviparyayakaraṇatvāt, yat yadviparyayakaraṇaṃ tat tatpramākaraṇam, yathā rūpapramākaraṇaṃ cakṣuriti /
[ku.3.409] vikalpanātkhalvapi /
aghaṭaṃ bhūtalamiti hi viśiṣṭadhīravaśyamindriyakaraṇikā svīkartavyā; pramāṇāntaraṃ vā saptamamāstheyam /
yathā hi viśeṣyamātropakṣīṇamindriyamakaraṇamatra, tathā viśeṣaṇamātropakṣīṇānupalabdhirapi na karaṇaṃ syāt /
svasvaviṣayamātrapravṛttayoḥ pramāṇayoḥ samāhāraḥ kāraṇamiti cenna- viṣayabhede phalavaijātye ca tadanupapatteḥ /
na hi mṛtsu tantuṣu ca vyāpriyamāṇayoḥ kulālakuvindayoḥ samāhāraḥsyāt /
nāpi ghaṭapaṭādikāriṇāṃ cakravemādīnāṃ samāhāraḥ kvacidupayujyate /
tatra karburakāryābhāvānna tathā; prakṛte tu viśiṣṭapratyayasya parokṣāparokṣarūpasya darśanāttatheti cenna- viruddhajātisamāveśābhāvāt /
bhāve vā karambita (karbura) eva kārye dvayorapi śaktirabhyupagantavyā; darśanabalāt /
na hi niyataviṣayeṇa sāmarthyena karburakāryasiddhiḥ; anyatrāpi tathā prasaṅgāt /
nanūbhayorapyubhayatra sāmarthye kor'tho mithaḥsannidhāneneti cenna- tatsahitasyaiva tasya tatra sāmarthyāditi /
etena surabhi candanamityādayo vyākhyātāḥ /
tathācābhāvaviṣaye 'pīndriyasāmarthyasya durapahnavatvādalamasadgraheṇeti /
[ku.3.410] syādetat- nāgṛhīte viśeṣaṇe viśaṣṭabuddhirudeti, tatkāryatvāt /
na ca viśiṣṭasāmarthye kevalaviśeṣaṇe 'pi sāmarthyam, kevalasaurabhe 'pi cakṣuṣo vṛttiprasaṅgāt /
ato 'bhāvaviśeṣaṇagrahaṇāya mānāntarasambhavaḥ /
api ca kathamanālocitor'tha indriyeṇa vikalpyeta? na ca mānāntarasyāpyeṣā rītiḥ,anumānādibhiranālocitasyāpyarthasya vikalpanāt /
aprāpteśca /
na hyabhāvenendriyasya saṃyogādiḥ sambhavati /
na ca viśeṣaṇatvam, sambandhāntarapūrvakatvāttasya /
avaśyābhyupagantavyatvāccānupalabdheḥ /
na hi tadupalabdhau tasyābhāvopalambha iti cet-[ku.3.411] ucyate-(210)avacchedagrahadhrauvyādadhrauvye
children.translated_text: If it be said: when that [counter-correlate] is apprehended, there is apprehension of its absence — [Ku 3.411] it is replied: (210) Because the constancy of apprehension of the delimitor (<s>avacchedaka</s>) [is required], and because of the inconstancy [of the opponent's position],
because it amounts to proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>),
because there would be infinite regress with respect to another connection (<s>prāpti</s>), and here the other [position] too is difficult to establish. //22//

For whatever <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) apprehends the existence of something, that also apprehends its absence — just as <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) or <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony); and the sense organ apprehends things such as pots, etc. Otherwise, even <s>śabda</s> and the like would not convey absence, since their capacity would be determined only with respect to positive entities. But this is not correct, since from the statement '<s>Devadatta</s> is not in the house,' and from <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) — as when I, wishing to ascertain the matter there, did not see [him], O <s>Maitra</s> — even through inference based on ascertained non-apprehension, [absence] is cognized. [Ku 3.407] Or let the sense organ apprehend the substratum; even so, this [absence-cognition] is not obstructed by it, because it is an operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>). Otherwise, a handful of water would be offered for making all determinate cognitions (<s>savikalpaka</s>) into perceptual ones. If it be objected that in that case the perception of smoke too would be its operation — that is not so, because the operation-status belongs only to that activity without which the causal status of [the instrument] with respect to that [effect] cannot be sustained. And it is not the case that the causal status of the eye for fire-cognition cannot be sustained without the perception of smoke and the like, as in the case of contact (<s>saṃyoga</s>). [Ku 3.408] And there is the alternation of presence and absence [of the effect with the presence and absence of the proposed cause]. That with respect to whose defect [the error] conforms — that alone is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) here; this is proper. And <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) is not intrinsically defective; nor is the apprehension of the substratum or the recollection of the counter-correlate intrinsically defective — because in the state of non-origination there is non-origination, and in the state of origination the nature of self-manifestation is not reversed. If it be said that the cognition of the unconnected substratum and counter-correlate as connected is defective, and of the connected as unconnected — well, this is precisely the alternation [we spoke of]. And thus there would be the defect of self-dependence (<s>ātmāśraya</s>). Therefore, given that a defective sense organ has the capacity for the opposite [erroneous] cognition, a non-defective one also has the capacity for correct cognition of that [absence]. And the formal argument is: the sense organ is the instrument of valid cognition of absence, because it is the instrument of the opposite thereof; whatever is the instrument of the opposite of something is the instrument of valid cognition of that thing — just as the eye is the instrument of valid cognition of color. [Ku 3.409] And also by reasoning through alternatives (<s>vikalpana</s>). For the determinate cognition 'the ground is pot-less' must necessarily be accepted as having the sense organ as its instrument; or else a seventh <s>pramāṇa</s> would have to be posited. For just as the sense organ, when it apprehends only the qualificand, is not the instrument here [by itself], so too <s>anupalabdhi</s>, when it apprehends only the qualifier, would not be the instrument either. If it be said that the combination of the two <s>pramāṇas</s>, each operating on its own object alone, is the cause — that is not so, because this is impossible given the difference of objects and the heterogeneity of results. For there would be no combination of a potter and a weaver each engaged in [working with] clay and threads respectively. Nor is the combination of wheel, loom, and the like, which produce pots and cloth, ever useful anywhere. There, because there is no variegated effect, it is not so; but in the present case, since a qualified cognition having both perceptual and non-perceptual aspects is observed, it would be so — this is not correct, because there is no co-presence of contradictory universals. Or, if the effect is indeed mixed (variegated), the capacity of both [instruments] must be acknowledged — based on observation. For the production of a variegated effect cannot be accomplished by a capacity restricted [to a single object]; because otherwise the same consequence would apply elsewhere too. If it be said: when both have capacity for both, what is the purpose of their mutual proximity? — that is not so, because it is only that [instrument] together with that [other] that has the capacity for that [effect]. By this, [examples such as] 'fragrant sandalwood' and the like are explained. And thus, since the capacity of the sense organ even with respect to the object of absence is impossible to deny, enough with grasping at what is false.

children.text:
[ku.3.412] sa hyarthaviśeṣaṇībhaviṣyan kevalo 'pi visphuret, yasyāvacchedakajñānaṃ na vyañjakam /
sa ca (vā) vikalpayitavya ālocyate, yo viśeṣaṇajñānanirapekṣeṇendriyeṇa vijñāpyate /
yastu tatpuraḥsara eva prakāśate, tatra tasya vikalpasāmagrīsamavadhānavata eva sāmarthyānnāyaṃ vidhiḥ /
[ku.3.413] svabhāvaprāptau satyāmapyadhikā prāptiḥ pratipattibalena rūpādāvabhyupagatā /
iha tvanavasthādusthatayā na tadabhyupagamaḥ; na tu svabhāvapratyāsattiretāvataiva viphalāyate /
[ku.3.414] na cedevaṃ, pramāṇāntare 'pi sarvametaddurghaṭaṃ syāt /
tathāhi- sarvameva mānaṃ sākṣātparamparayā vā nirvikalpakaviśrāntam /
na hyanumānādikamapyanālocanapūrvakam /
tato 'nālocito 'bhāvaḥ kathamanupalabdhyāpi vikalpyeta /
na ca tayā tadālocanameva janyate,pratiyogyanavacchinnasya tasya nirūpayitumaśakyatvāt /
śakyatve vā kimaparāddhamindriyeṇa /
tathā sambandhāntaragarbhatvaniyamena viśeṣaṇatvasya, mānāntare 'pi kaḥ pratīkāraḥ; tadabhāvasya tadānīmapisamānatvāt /
parasya tādātmyamastīti cet- nanu yadyasāvasti, astyeva; na cet, naiva /
na hyabhyupagamenārthāḥ kriyante, anabhyupagamena vā nivartante iti /
[ku.3.415] avaśyābhyupagantavyatve kāraṇatvaṃ siddhayet, na tu mānāntaratvam /

children.translated_text: Otherwise, even in the apprehension of a positive entity, <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) of absence alone would be the <s>pramāṇa</s>, and not the sense organ;

because just as non-apprehension of the positive entity [is invoked as pramāṇa] in the apprehension of absence, so too non-apprehension of absence would be invoked as an adamantine principle in the apprehension of a positive entity.
[Ku 3.416] (212) By perception and these other [means of knowledge] thus, [God's existence] is on a firm ground; contradiction is far away.
That [God] whom even the self cannot reach through those who are deprived solely of the vision of [His] face,

[Ku 3.412] For that [absence], if it is to become a qualifier of the object, should manifest even by itself, if the cognition of its delimitor is not a revealer [of it]. And that [absence] which is to be conceptually cognized is [first] perceived — that which is made known by the sense organ independently of the cognition of the qualifier. But that which manifests only as preceded by that [qualifier-cognition] — there, since [the sense organ] already possesses the assemblage of conditions for conceptual cognition, this rule [that the sense organ is not the instrument] does not apply. [Ku 3.413] Even when there is natural connection (<s>svabhāvaprāpti</s>), an additional connection through cognition has been accepted in the case of color and the like. But here, because of the infinite regress that would be troublesome, that [additional connection] is not accepted; yet the natural proximity is not thereby rendered fruitless. [Ku 3.414] If this were not so, all these same difficulties would arise for any other <s>pramāṇa</s> as well. For all means of valid knowledge, either directly or indirectly, rest upon indeterminate perception (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>). For even inference and the like do not operate without prior apprehension. Therefore, how could absence, if not [first] apprehended, be conceptually cognized even through <s>anupalabdhi</s>? Nor does <s>anupalabdhi</s> generate merely the apprehension of that [absence], since that [absence], when not delimited by the counter-correlate, cannot be determined. And if it can be so determined, what fault has the sense organ committed [that it should be denied this role]? Likewise, with the rule that qualifier-status necessarily involves another relation — what remedy is there even for another <s>pramāṇa</s>? For the absence of that [relation] is the same at that time [for any pramāṇa]. If it be said that the other [pramāṇa, i.e. anupalabdhi] has identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) [with absence] — well, if that [identity] exists, it simply exists; if not, it simply does not. For objects are not created by [mere] acceptance, nor do they cease by non-acceptance. [Ku 3.415] If [anupalabdhi] must necessarily be accepted, let it establish [only] its causal status (<s>kāraṇatva</s>), not its status as a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>.
that One to whom all conform, whose unmatched play-festival is spontaneous,
that God of gods — with overflowing faith
we take refuge [in Him]. //23//

children.text: nanu sadapīśvarajñānaṃ na pramāṇam, tallakṣaṇāyogāt; anadhigatārthagantustathābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: Even if [God] exists, the cognition of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge), because the defining characteristics of [a pramāṇa] do not apply to it; since the condition of apprehending a previously unknown object does not hold [for God's eternal omniscient cognition].
Otherwise, even memory (<s>smṛti</s>) would absurdly have the status of a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: na ca nityasya sarvaviṣasyacānadhigatārthatā, vyāghātāt- atrocyate- avyāpteradhikavyāpteralakṣaṇamapūrvadṛk /
children.translated_text: And for an eternal [cognition] that has all objects as its content, there is no [possibility of] apprehending what was previously unapprehended, because of contradiction. To this it is replied: Being a cognition of what is unprecedented (<s>apūrvadṛk</s>), it is not a non-definition due to under-extension or over-extension.
A cognition that corresponds to its object (<s>yathārthānubhava</s>) is accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) independently [of the condition of novelty]. //1//

children.translated_text: And without the recognition of that [prior cognition], the benefit from it does not arise, because this is not accepted.
Or if it is accepted, because the property of being an effect is inconclusive.
Here it is said: [Ku 4.512] Because of the absence of a restriction of nature, the benefit too is difficult to establish.
Even if [benefit is] easily established, when the [qualifying] object is absent, what other recourse is there? || 2 ||

[Ku 4.502] For it is not the case that a cognition of an already-cognized object simply does not arise, because the causes are unobstructed. Nor is it the case that even when arising, it is not valid knowledge because it is not needed by the cognizer, since validity does not depend on that [need]. Nor is there invalidity merely by being indistinct from the prior [cognition]; for by being indistinct from the subsequent [cognition], the prior one too would be invalid. And if that [prior cognition] is valid by being independent of that [subsequent one], the subsequent one too would be likewise, because of no distinction. Nor is it the case that there is simply no greater instrumentality of the eyes and the like in what is delimited, as of axes and the like in what is cut — because of the distinction between the production and non-production of the result. [Ku 4.503] [Objection:] That result is not valid cognition, because it has for its object what is merely already grasped, like memory. No, [we reply] — because when the negation of being a veridical experience is what is to be proved, it is contradicted [by evidence]. And when the negation of having an unapprehended object is [proposed], it establishes what is already established, and it is equal to what is to be proved. And when the negation of practical dealing is [proposed], it has the defect of being conditioned by the absence of its cause, and is contradicted. And the having of an unapprehended object is not itself that cause, for otherwise there would be the undesirable consequence of valid-knowledge-usage even in the case of error. Nor is it this very [property] qualified by veridicality; because it would not pervade a stream of continuous cognitions. [Ku 4.504] Nor should it be maintained that in those [cases] too, having an unapprehended object is established through being qualified by specific time-portions; because time-portions are not ascertained. Nor should it be imagined that the qualified character produced by those [time-portions] is manifest even when the qualifying features are unknown; because when [a cognition] produces [its result] through its own form, there would be a contradiction with the experience of being qualified by the future and the like; and when it produces [its result] through knowledge of those [time-portions], then in the absence of knowledge of the movement of the sun and the like, the qualified character [by time] would not be produced. And there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> (evidence) for this. [Objection:] If when the qualifier and the qualificand are mutually unassisting and unassisted, how is over-extension to be prevented? By the communication of exclusion; and in exclusion, by its own nature. Otherwise, there would be an infinite regress in that. [Ku 4.505] [Objection:] If [it is said that] 'being-known' is the limiting condition — no, because it will be refuted. Or even if it exists, there would be the undesirable consequence that memory too would have validity in the same way. Because even when the object of the generator [cognition] is the same, in each successive memory, the cognized-ness generated by each prior recollection is apprehended. [Ku 4.506] Or let perception be as it may. What need is there of discussion regarding a <s>śruti</s> (scripture) whose content was grasped and then forgotten? [Objection:] If [it is said that] it is simply not valid cognition — then the hope for the validity of the <s>Veda</s> is now gone. For in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence), the meaning of the sentence 'one who desires heaven should sacrifice' has been comprehended by someone; and even in doubt, because of the doubt about validity. And there too, the distinctions of time-portions do not manifest. Nor [is there any limitation to] a single lifetime.

children.translated_text: [Objection:] If [it is said that] through identity, the particular too is known — then when a pot is known by the eye, is its taste also known, through identity? [Objection:] If [it is said that] it is known through the form of a pot — then why is it not known through the form of taste? [Objection:] If [it is said] because [taste] is not the basis of being-known through that form — then in the cognition of the universal 'present' too, the past and future and the like are not known; because [the present] is not the basis of manifestation through that form.
[Ku 4.513] [Objection:] But through the pervasion 'action must do something to the object,' there is an inference.

children.text: na;- (anaikāntyā) anekāntādasiddhervā na ca liṅgamiha kriyā /
children.translated_text: No: Action is not a mark here, because of inconclusiveness or non-establishment.
Because it manifests the distinction of that [object], the perceptual experience is not [something] additional. || 3 ||

Because the restriction 'the result is there alone and not elsewhere' is also impossible to account for in the absence of [a distinction]. And when it is accounted for through the restriction of nature, the determination of the object is accounted for in just that way. And this must necessarily be admitted, because of the requirement that [cognition] has past and other objects. For it is not possible to understand that knowledge does something to that [past object], since it does not exist. Nor is it reasonable [to say] that something is done to something that is the basis of a universal property of that — for then that [basis] alone would become the object.

children.translated_text: For just as: 'The distinction of cognitions, being formless (<s>nirākāra</s>), is [determined] only by the object,'

children.translated_text: so too: 'The distinction of objects in practical activity is [determined] only by the action [performed upon them].'  [verse 4]

[Ku.4.513] If the usage [of the word 'kartṛ/agent'] is intended with reference to the mere meaning of the verbal root (<s>dhātvarthamātra</s>), [there is] non-determination because of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) and the like [also being 'doers' in that sense]. For nothing is produced in space by the conjunction of an arrow; nor by the manifestation of the final sound. If intended with reference to motion (<s>spanda</s>) — [that is] unestablished [for cognition]. If intended with reference to function (<s>vyāpāra</s>) — there is deviation through the functions of words, inferential marks, and sense-organs. For by those, nothing is produced in the object of knowledge; rather, [they produce effects] only in the knower. The same applies if intended with reference to the result (<s>phala</s>). Ultimately, by that very [argument], non-determination and infinite regress [follow]. If intended with reference to the property of being quickly destructible — there is no restriction, because of duality-number (<s>dvitva</s>) and the like [which are also quickly destructible]. If intended with reference to a swift causal agent — [it is] unestablished [that cognition is a swift agent] with respect to the object. For what is to be proved is precisely this: that cognition is a swift causal agent with respect to the object. Because the swift agency of the agent is not pervaded by [the meaning of] being contributory to the object; and because there is non-determination through the functions of words and the like alone. [Ku.4.514] It may be objected: Manifestation (<s>prākaṭya</s>) is established by experience itself.
