children.translated_text: [Objection:] Let size come from <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) alone; what need for apprehensive cognition? — No, because [if one says] 'let everything come from that alone, what need for observed causes?' — this would lead to the impossibility of settling [anything].
[Ku.5.636] Or the [verse beginning with] 'from effect' and so on may be interpreted otherwise.
The enumeration [of proofs] merely [states] the intention; the explanation, cognizing the universe,
renders the word 'God' (<s>Īśvara</s>) and the like meaningful, following the course of the world.  [verse 6]

'These worlds would perish if I did not perform action' — thus (<s>Gītā</s> 3.23-24). By this, the <s>Yajus</s> passages such as 'Salutation to the potters, to the smiths' and so on should be understood. [Ku.5.628] Also from [the argument of] trust (<s>pratyaya</s>). By the word 'trust' here is meant the validity that is the object of confidence. And thus the formal argument: This scriptural tradition is preceded by the quality of [its] cause, because it is valid — like perception and the like. For without the cognition of validity, there is no confidence anywhere. And there is no cognition of validity that is unestablished. And it has been shown that validity is not intrinsic (<s>svataḥ</s>). And [we have] said that this is a means of knowledge, from the acceptance of the multitude. And one who is not omniscient cannot independently produce <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. And that the quality [of being authored by] a non-omniscient [being does not apply here] — this is beyond doubt. [Ku.5.629] And indeed from scripture (<s>śruti</s>). For thus: The <s>Vedas</s> are composed by an omniscient [being], because they are <s>Vedas</s>. Whatever is not composed by an omniscient being is not a <s>Veda</s>, like any other statement. [Objection:] What is this 'Veda-hood'? Because 'being a statement' and 'being a statement concerning the unseen' are contradictory. And because the [property of] 'being a valid statement concerning the unseen' is unestablished. And because there is contradiction since it applies to the statements of <s>Manu</s> and others. — No, because [Veda-hood] consists in being a statement accepted by the multitude while no other basis is apprehended. For the statements about rites and so on do not have perception etc. as their basis. Nor [are they based on] error or deception, since [they are] accepted by the multitude — as stated. Nor is tradition alone the basis, since there is interruption at the great dissolution — as stated. [Ku.5.630] Or [the argument may proceed] through positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>): Vedic sentences are authored by a person (<s>pauruṣeya</s>), because they are sentences — like our sentences. [Objection:] [They are] not so, because no author is remembered. — No, because [that is] unestablished: 'And immediately the <s>Vedas</s> issued forth from His mouths' — 'And in each <s>Manvantara</s>, another <s>Śruti</s> is ordained' — 'And I am the maker of the <s>Vedānta</s> and the knower of the <s>Vedas</s>' — thus the <s>Smṛtis</s>. And: 'From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the <s>Ṛcs</s> and <s>Sāmans</s> were born' — thus the <s>Śruti</s> passages and <s>Smṛtis</s>. [Objection:] This is merely eulogy (<s>arthavāda</s>). — No, because the recollection of an author is never for the purpose of injunction. And thus, if not recollected, [it would be] like not recollecting <s>Kālidāsa</s> and the like. And then there would follow the authorlessness of the <s>Kumārasambhava</s> and the like; or the reason [in the inference] would be inconclusive. [Ku.5.631] [Objection:] [Vedic content] has as its object what is not accessible to other means of knowledge, and the counter-thesis does not exist. — No, because with respect to the author, [this is] unestablished; and with respect to another [entity], it is inconclusive. Because a particular cause — inaccessible to other means of knowledge with respect to another — is communicated by that very speaker, like the recollection of the cause of a suddenly arising, causeless smile. [Ku.5.632] [Objection:] A speaker is simply impossible in the present case, because without a cause there is no effect. Because the eyes and other [senses] are incapable there — like our senses. Because the mind is not independent externally. — No, because whether one takes as the subject consciousness, knowledge, a sense-organ, or the mind, the unestablished basis has already been elaborated. And because [the opponent] is incapable of refuting the eternal [nature of God]. [Objection:] Atoms and the like are not perceptible to anyone, since the aggregate [of conditions for perception] is absent for them. — No, because with respect to the seer [God], [this is] unestablished; and with respect to another, it [merely] proves what is already established. [Ku.5.633] [Objection:] Even so, 'being a sentence' is not a valid reason, because it is non-probative. The authorship in [Vedic texts] is motivated by [their] having an object accessible to other means of knowledge, not motivated by 'being a sentence.' — No, because there would follow the authorlessness of the Buddhist and other scriptures. [Objection:] For valid sentences only. — No, because [the property] 'having an object accessible to means of knowledge other than the author' is already part of what is to be proved. For authorship (<s>pauruṣeyatva</s>) means being composed by an independent person; independence consists of the intention and effort that are focused on the same object as the cognition of meaning. And there would follow the authorlessness of <s>Manu</s>'s and others' statements, since their content is inaccessible to means of knowledge other than verbal testimony. [Objection:] [The property is merely] 'having an object other than that of the sentence being employed.' — No, because that also exists in the <s>Veda</s>, since the same meaning is communicated by multiple sentences in different <s>śākhās</s> (recensions). [Objection:] Granted, but they are not mutually each other's basis. — No, because this has been answered. [Ku.5.634] And indeed from the specific number [of atoms]. In dyads and triads, for a start, [there is] size (<s>parimāṇa</s>) of the same [type] as atoms, because they are substances. And that size is an effect, because it is a quality of effects. And its cause is neither the size of atoms nor the size of dyads, because [atomic size] is eternal; and because [it] is atomic-sized [which cannot produce gross size]. Otherwise, there would follow the production of an effect without a basis; and the dyad would have the unwanted consequence of being large — because, like the triad, the dyad too is constituted by atoms, and since the plurality of causes [is what produces] largeness in the triad, while atomic size is established as non-productive [of largeness]. Nor is it proper [to say] that atomic-ness alone is the distinguishing factor in producing largeness — because there would follow that a large [size] cannot produce a large [effect]; and because of the contradiction of atomic-ness and largeness, there would follow the inability to produce effects of the same class. And because even many atoms could be the starting point, as could two dyads. [Objection:] If so, what is the fault? — The unwanted consequence that the effect of atoms would be large, since plurality of causes is the reason for that. Otherwise, if atoms could start [an effect] without a fixed number — by two, three, or four indifferently — that [fixed number] would be purposeless. [Objection:] Let there be gradation among atoms themselves, independent of number. — That cannot be, since number itself is the motivating [factor] in gradation. And accumulation (<s>pracaya</s>) need not be considered, since there is no contact of parts [in atoms]. Therefore, the established position is that both size and accumulation are productive only of the large [i.e., composite things]. [Ku.5.635] Hence, plurality-number remains [as what needs to be explained]. That [number] is produced by an apprehensive cognition (<s>apekṣābuddhi</s>), because it is a plurality-number. But we [ordinary beings] cannot have apprehensive cognition of atoms. Therefore, He for whom that [cognition exists] is omniscient. Otherwise, in the absence of apprehensive cognition, number would not arise; without that, the size belonging to that [composite] would not arise; and an unmeasured substance being non-productive, triads would not arise — [leading to] the unwanted consequence that the universe would not arise. [Objection:] Let the apprehensive cognition be our own, inferred [rather than direct]. — No, because there would follow mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>). For when a gross effect exists, one infers atoms from it; and given those [atoms], gross things arise in the order of dyads and so on.

children.text:
āmnāyasya hi bhāvyārthasya kārye puruṣapravṛttinivṛttī /
bhūtārthasya tu yadyapi nāhatya pravartakatvaṃ nivartakatvaṃ vā, tathāpi tātparyatastatraiva prāmāṇyam /
tathāhi- vidhiśaktirevāvasīdantī stutyādibhiruttabhyate /
praśaste hi sarvaḥ pravartate, ninditācca nivartate iti sthitiḥ /
[ku.5.637] tatra padaśaktistāvadabhidhā; tadbalāyātaḥ padārthaḥ /
ākāṅkṣādimattve sati cānvayaśaktiḥ padānāṃ padārthānāṃ vā vākyam; tadbalāyāto vākyārthaḥ /
tātparyārthastu cintyate /
tadeva paraṃ sādhyaṃ pratipādyaṃ prayojanamuddeśyaṃ vā yasya, tadidaṃ tatparam /
tasya bhāvastattvam /
tad yadviṣayam, sa tātparyārtha iti syāt /
[ku.5.638] tatra na prathamaḥ, pramāṇenārthasya karmaṇo 'sādhyatvāt /
phalasya ca tatpratipattito 'nyasyābhāvāt /
praśastaninditasvārthapratipādanadvāreṇa pravṛttinivṛttirūpaṃ sādhyaṃ paramucyate iti cenna- gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityatra tīrasyāpravṛttinivṛttirūpasyāsādhyasyāpi paratvāt /
tīraviṣaye pravṛttinivṛttī sādhye iti tīrasyāpi paratvamiti cenna- svarūpākhyānamātreṇāpi paryavasānāt /
[ku.5.639] na dvitīyaḥ,padavākyayoḥ padārthatatsaṃsargau vihāya pratipādyāntarābhāvāt /
padaśaktisaṃsargaśaktī vinā svārthāvinābhāvena pratipādyaṃ paramucyate ityapi na sāmapratam- na hi yad yacchabdārthāvinābhūtaṃ tatra tatra tātparyaṃ śabdasya; ati prasaṅgāt /
tadā hi gaṅgāyāṃ jalamityādyapi tīraparaṃ syāt; avinābhāvasya tādavasthyāt /
mukhye bādhake sati tattathā syāditi cet- na- tasminnasatyapi bhāvāt /
tad yathā- "gaccha gacchasi cet kānta panthānaḥsantu te śivāḥ /
mamāpi janma tatraiva bhūyād yatra gato bhavān" iti mukhyārthābādhane 'pi vāraṇe tātparyam /
na ca paraṃ vyāpakameva, avyāpake 'pi tātparyadarśanāt /
tad yathā, mañcāḥ krośantīti puruṣe tātparyam /
na ca mañcapuruṣayoravinābhāvaḥ, nāpi puruṣakrośanayoḥ /
[ku.5.640] nāpi tṛtīyaḥ /
taddhi pratipādyāpekṣitam, pratipādakāpekṣitaṃ vā syāt /
nādyaḥ; śabdaprāmāṇyasyātadadhīnatvāt /
tathātve vātiprasaṅgāt /
yasya yadapekṣitam,
 taṃ prati tasya paratvaprasaṅgāt /
tadarthasādhyatvenāpekṣāniyama iti cenna- kāryajñāpyabhedena sādhyasya bahuvidhatve bhinnatātparyatayā vākyabhedaprasaṅgāt /
dhūmasya hi pradeśaśyāmalatāmaśakanivṛttyādyanekaṃ kāryam; ārdendhanadahanādyanekaṃ jñāpyam /
tathāceha pradeśe dhūmodgama ityabhihite tātparyataḥ ko vākyārtho bhavet; cetanāpekṣāyāniyantumaśakyatvāt /
nāpi pratipādakopekṣitam, vede tadabhāvāt /
[ku.5.641] caturthastu syāt /
yaduddeśena yaḥśabdaḥ pravṛttaḥ sa tatparaḥ /
tathaiva lokavyutpatteḥ /
tathāhi- praśaṃsāvākyamupādānamuddiśya loke prayujyate /
tadupādānaparam /
nindāvākyaṃ hānamuddiśya prayujyate tat hānaparam /
evamanyatrāpi svayamūhanīyam /
tasmāllokānusāreṇa vede 'pyevaṃ svīkāraṇīyam; anyathā arthavādānāṃ sarvathaivānarthakyaprasaṅgāt /
sa coddeśo vyavasāyo 'dhikāro 'bhiprāyo bhāva āśaya ityanarthāntaramiti tadādhārapraṇetṛpuruṣadhaureyasiddhiḥ /
tathā ca prayogaḥ- vaidikāni praśaṃsāvākyāni upādānābhiprāyapūrvakāṇi praśaṃsāvākyatvāt pariṇatisurasamāmraphalamityādilokavākyavaditi /
evaṃ nindāvākyāni hānābhiprāyapūrvakāṇi nindāvākyatvāt pariṇativirasaṃ panasaphalamityādivākyavat /
anyathā nirarthakatvaprasaṅgaśca vipakṣe bādhakamuktam /
[ku.5.642] apica no cedevam, śrutārthāpattirapi hīyeta /
siddho hyarthaḥ pramāṇaviṣayaḥ, na tu tenaiva kartavyaḥ /
na ca pīno devadatto divā na bhuṅkte ityatra rātrau bhuṅkta iti vākyaśeṣo 'sti; anupalambhabādhitatvāt; utpattyabhivyaktisāmagrītālvādi vyāpāravirahāt; ayogyasyāśaṅkitumapyaśakyatvāt /
tasmādabhiprāyastha eva pariśiṣyate, gatyantarābhāvāt /
sa cedvede nāsti, nāsti śrutārthāpattiriti tadvyutpādanānarthakyaprasaṅgaḥ /
tasmāt kāryāttātparyādapyunnīyate, asti praṇeteti /
[ku.5.643] ayojanāt khalvapi /
nahi vedādavyakhyātāt kaścidarthamadhigacchati /
na caikadeśadarśino vyākhyānamādaraṇīyam; "paurvāparyāparāmṛṣṭaḥ śabdo 'nyāṃ kurute matim" iti nyāyenānāśvāsāt /
tricaturapadakādapi vākyādekadeśaśrāviṇo 'nyathārthapratyayaḥ syāt, kimutātīndriyādantarāntarāvākyasambhedaduradhigamāt /
tataḥsakalavedavedārthadarśī kaścidevābhyupeyaḥ, anyathāndhaparamparāprasaṅgāt /
sa ca śrutādhītāvadhṛtasmṛtasāṅgopāṅgavedārthastadviparīto vā na sarvajñādanyaḥ sambhavati /
kohyapratyakṣīkṛtaviśvatadanuṣṭhānaḥ, etāvānevāyamāmnāya iti niścinuyāt /
kaścārvāgdṛk niḥśeṣāḥ śratīrgranthator'thatovādhīyīta, adhyāpayedvā /
atrāpi prayogaḥ- vedāḥ kadācit sarvavedārthavidvyākhyātāḥ, anuṣṭhātṛ(254)maticalane 'pi niścalārthānuṣṭhānatvāt /
yadevaṃ tatsarvaṃ tadarthavidvyākhyātam, yathā manvādisaṃhiteti /
anyathātvanāśvāsenāvyavasthānādananuṣṭhānamavyavasthā vā bhavedanādeśikatvāt (255) /
anuṣṭhātāra evādeṣṭāra iti cenna- teṣāmaniyatabodhatvāt /
vedavadvedārthānuṣṭhānamapyanādīti cenna- taddhi svatantraṃ vā vedārthabodhatantraṃ vā /
ādye nirmūlatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
dvitīye tvaniyamāpattiḥ /
nahyasarvajñāviśeṣe pūrveṣāṃ tadavabodhaḥ pramāṇam, na tvidānīntanānāmiti niyāmakamasti /
[ku.5.644] padāt khalvupi /
śrūyate hi praṇaveśvareśānādipadam /
tacca sārthakam /
avigānena śrutismṛtītihāseṣu prayujyamānatvāt ghaṭādipadavaditi sānāsyataḥ siddheḥ, ko 'syārthaḥ iti vyutpatsorvimarśe sati nirṇayaḥ, svargādipadavat, "uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ /
yo lokatrayamāviśya bibharttyavyaya īśvaraḥ" ityarthavādāt, yavavarāhādivadvākyaśeṣādvā /
tad yathā īśvarapraṇidhānamupakramya śrūyate- sarvajñatā tṛptiranādibodhaḥ svatantratā nityamaluptaśaktiḥ /
anantaśaktiśca vibhorvidhijñāḥ ṣaḍāhuraṅgāni maheśvarasya" iti /
evambhūtor'thaḥ pramāṇabādhita iti cenna- prāgeva pratiṣedhāt /
tathāpi na tatra pramāṇamastīti cet- svarge astīti kā śraddhā? nahyuktaviśeṣaṇe sukhe kiñcit pramāṇamastyasmadādīnām /
yājñikapravṛttyanyathānupapatyā tathaiva tadityavadhāryate iti cenna- itaretarāśrayaprasaṅgāt /
avadhṛte hi svargarūpe tatra pravṛttiḥ pravṛttyanyathānupapattyā ca tadavadhāraṇamiti /
pūrvavṛddhapravṛttyā tadavadhāraṇe 'yamadoṣa iti cenna- andhaparamparāprasaṅgāt /
viśiṣṭādṛṣṭavaśāt kadācit kasyacidevaṃ vidhamapi sukhaṃ syāditi nāsti virodhaḥ; tanniṣedhe pramāṇābhāvāditi cet- tulyamitaratrāpi /
atrāpi prayogaḥ- yaḥśabdo yatra vṛddhairasati vṛttyantare pyujyate sa tasya vācakaḥ, yathā svargaśabdaḥ sukhaviśeṣe prayujyamānastasya vācakaḥ /
prayujyate cāyaṃ jagatkartarīti /
anyathā nirarthakatvaprasaṅge sārthakapadakadambasamabhivyāhārānupapattiriti /
etena rudropendramahendrādidevatāviśeṣavācakā
 vyākhyātāḥ /
apica asmatpadaṃ lokavadvede 'pi prayujyate /
tasya ca loke nācetaneṣvanyatamadarthaḥ, tatra sarvathaivāprayogāt /
nāpyātmamātramarthaḥ; parātmanyapi prayogaprasaṅgāt /
apitu yastaṃ svātantryeṇoccārayati, tamevāha; tathaivānvayavyatirekābhyāmavasāyāt /
tato lokavyutpattimanatikramya vede 'pyanena svaprayoktaiva vaktavyaḥ /
anyathāprayogaprasaṅgāt /
na ca yo yadoccārayati vaidikamahaṃ śabdam, sa eva tadā tasyārtha iti yuktam /
tathāsati māmupāsītetyādau sa evopāsyaḥsyāt /
ahaṃ sarvasyaprabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṃ pravartate, ityupādhyāyaśiṣyaparamparaivātmanyaiśvaryaṃ samadhigacchet /
tathācopāsanāṃ pratyunmattakeliḥsyāt /
lokavyavahāraścocchidyeta /
tasmannānuvaktāsya vācyaḥ, api tu vaktaiveti sthite prayujyate vede asmacchabdaḥ svaprayoktṛvacanaḥ asmacchabdatvāllokavaditi /
evamanye 'pi yaḥ kaḥ sa ityādi śabdā draṣṭavyāḥ, teṣāṃ buddhyupakramapraśnaparāmarśādyupahitamaryādatvāt; tasya ca vaktṛdharmatvāt /
buddhyapakramo hi prakṛtatvam, jijñāsā'viṣkaraṇañca praśnaḥ, pratisandhānañca parāmarśa iti /
evañca saṃśayādivācaka apyunneyāḥ /
na ca jijñāsāsaṃśayādayaḥ sarvajñe pratiṣiddhā iti yuktam /
śiṣyapratibodhanāyāhāryatvenāvirodhāt /
ko dharmaḥ kathaṃ lakṣaṇaka ityādibhāṣyavaditi /
etena dhigaho bata hantetyādayo nipātā vyākhyātāḥ /

children.translated_text: [Ku 5.645] And also from cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>).

children.text: liṅgādipratyayā hi puruṣadhaureyaniyogārthā bhavantastaṃ prati pādayanti /
children.translated_text: For the cognitions [arising] from inferential marks (<s>liṅga</s>) and the like, being intended for the employment of a person of excellence, establish that [God] with respect to him.

children.text: tathāhi- pravṛttiḥ kṛtirevātra, sā cecchato, yataśca sā /
children.translated_text: For thus: Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) here is effort (<s>kṛti</s>) alone; and that [belongs to] one who wills; and the source of that
is knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>); the object of that [knowledge] is the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), or that which makes [the object] known. //7//

For with respect to the <s>Āmnāya</s> (Vedic tradition), when the content pertains to what is to be done (<s>bhāvyārtha</s>), its effects are human activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and abstention (<s>nivṛtti</s>). But when it pertains to existing facts (<s>bhūtārtha</s>), although it does not directly impel or restrain, still its authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) lies in that [factual content] itself by way of purport (<s>tātparya</s>). For the power of injunction (<s>vidhiśakti</s>), when faltering, is supported by praise (<s>stuti</s>) and the like. For everyone is impelled toward what is commended, and turns away from what is censured — such is the established rule.
[ku.5.637] Therein, word-power (<s>padaśakti</s>) is denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>); the word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>) is derived from it. And the connective power of words (or word-meanings), when possessing expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) and the like, constitutes a sentence (<s>vākya</s>); the sentence-meaning (<s>vākyārtha</s>) is derived from it. But the purport-meaning (<s>tātparyārtha</s>) must be determined. Now, that whose supreme goal, or what is to be established, conveyed, useful, or intended — that is "directed toward that" (<s>tatpara</s>). Its state is its essence (<s>tattva</s>). The object of that is called the purport-meaning.
[ku.5.638] Therein, not the first [= what is to be accomplished], because an object or action is not to be accomplished by a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). And there is no result beyond the cognition of it. "What is called 'supreme' is the activity or abstention accomplished through conveying something as commendable or censurable." — No, because in "there is a village on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>," the bank — which is not [directly] an object of activity or abstention — is also the purport. "Activity or abstention regarding the bank is what is to be accomplished, so the bank too is the purport." — No, because the matter concludes with mere description of the thing itself.
[ku.5.639] Not the second [= what is to be conveyed], because apart from word-meanings and their connections, there is no other thing to be conveyed by words and sentences. "What is inseparable from the word-meaning, through word-power and connective-power, is called the supreme conveyed meaning." — This too is not right; for not everything that is inseparable from a word-meaning is the purport of that word — there would be overextension. For then "there is water in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>" etc. would also have the bank as its purport, since the inseparability [of water and bank] remains constant. "That would be so when there is obstruction of the primary meaning." — No, because it occurs even when there is no such obstruction. For example: "Go, O beloved, if you go — may the paths be auspicious for you. May my birth too be wherever you have gone" — even when there is no obstruction of the primary meaning, the purport is [still] dissuasion. Nor is the purport necessarily something more extensive (<s>vyāpaka</s>), since purport is seen even regarding something less extensive. For example, in "the platforms are shouting," the purport is the people [on the platforms]. And there is no inseparability between platforms and people, nor between people and shouting.
[ku.5.640] Nor the third [= purpose/utility]. For that would be relative to the conveyed [meaning] or to the conveying [words]. Not the first; because the authority of words does not depend on that [purpose]. And if it did, there would be overextension — whatever is needed by anything would be its purport. "The restriction of need is by being the means to an end (<s>sādhya</s>)." — No, because given the multiplicity of things to be accomplished — as effects, things to be indicated, etc. — there would follow a difference of purport and hence a splitting of the sentence. For smoke has many effects — darkening the area, warding off mosquitoes, etc.; and many things it indicates — burning of damp fuel, etc. So when it is said "smoke rises in this place," what would be the sentence-meaning by purport? Since the intention of the conscious agent cannot be restricted. Nor is it relative to the conveying [words], since in the <s>Veda</s> there is no such [purpose-relative usage].
[ku.5.641] But the fourth [= intention/aim] is correct. A word that is used with a particular aim (<s>uddeśa</s>) is directed toward that. This is established from ordinary linguistic usage. For in the world, a sentence of praise is used with the aim of [encouraging] adoption — its purport is adoption. A sentence of censure is used with the aim of abandonment — its purport is abandonment. Likewise in other cases, one should reason for oneself. Therefore, following ordinary usage, the same should be accepted in the <s>Veda</s> too; otherwise, <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory) passages would be entirely purposeless. And that aim — [called] resolve (<s>vyavasāya</s>), jurisdiction (<s>adhikāra</s>), intention (<s>abhiprāya</s>), disposition (<s>bhāva</s>), or purpose (<s>āśaya</s>) — is synonymous. Hence the existence of a composing person (<s>praṇetṛpuruṣa</s>) as the bearer of that [intention] is established. And thus the argument: "Vedic sentences of praise are preceded by an intention to commend, because they are sentences of praise — like worldly sentences such as 'the ripe mango is a divine fruit.'" Similarly, sentences of censure are preceded by an intention to discourage — like worldly sentences such as "the jackfruit is an insipid fruit." The absurdity of purposelessness in the contrary case has been stated as a refutation.
[ku.5.642] Moreover, if this were not so, even <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (verbal presumption) would be undermined. For an established fact is an object of a means of knowledge, but is not something to be done by that [means]. And in "fat <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day," the complement "he eats at night" is not part of the sentence; because it is contradicted by non-apprehension, lacking the causal conditions of production or manifestation, and because what is unfit cannot even be suspected. Therefore only intention (<s>abhiprāya</s>) remains, for lack of an alternative. And if that is absent in the <s>Veda</s>, then <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> would not exist — and the teaching of that [topic] would be purposeless. Therefore, even from purposive purport (<s>kāryatātparya</s>), a composer is inferred: "there exists a composer."
[ku.5.643] Also from the need for exposition (<s>vyākhyāna</s>). For no one understands the meaning from an unexplained <s>Veda</s>. And the exposition of one who sees only a part is not to be relied upon; because of the principle that "a word, when its sequence is not considered, produces a different understanding" — hence there is no confidence. Even from a sentence of three or four words, one who has heard only part may have a wrong understanding — how much more from what is supersensible, difficult to comprehend due to the intermixture of separate sentences. Therefore some being who sees the meaning of the entire <s>Veda</s> and its ancillaries must be accepted; otherwise there would be the fallacy of blind-leading-the-blind. And such a one — who has heard, studied, retained, and remembered the <s>Veda</s> with all its limbs and sub-limbs, and not one who is the opposite — is possible only as an omniscient being (<s>sarvajña</s>). For who, without having directly perceived the entire universe and its proper conduct, could determine: "this alone is the extent of this scriptural tradition"? And what limited seer could master all the <s>Śruti</s> texts, by text or by meaning, or teach them? Here too the argument: "The <s>Vedas</s> were at some time expounded by one who knew the meaning of all the <s>Vedas</s>; because they have stable ritual application even when the understanding of practitioners wavers. Whatever is like this is explained by one who knows its meaning — like the compilations of <s>Manu</s> and others." Otherwise, due to lack of confidence and resulting instability, there would be either non-performance or instability — since there would be no authoritative guide. "The practitioners themselves are the guides." — No, because their understanding is not certain. "Like the <s>Veda</s> itself, the practice of Vedic meaning too is beginningless." — That practice would be either independent or dependent on understanding of Vedic meaning. In the first case, there would be groundlessness. In the second, the regularity would fail. For there is no determining factor [to establish] that the earlier non-omniscient [sages'] understanding is authoritative, but not that of present-day [scholars].
[ku.5.644] Also from the [Vedic] words themselves. For words like <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>), <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, etc. are heard [in the <s>Veda</s>]. And they are meaningful. Since they are used without dispute in <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and <s>Itihāsa</s> — like words such as "pot" — their existence is established from usage. And when one seeking to learn asks "what is its meaning?", the determination [is made] like the word "heaven" (<s>svarga</s>) — from <s>arthavāda</s>: "But the Supreme Person is other, called the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), who, entering the three worlds, sustains [them] — the imperishable Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>)"; or from contextual completion, as with "barley" and "boar" [words whose meaning is known from context]. Thus, beginning with <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s> (devotion to God), it is heard: "Omniscience, contentment, beginningless knowledge, independence, eternally undiminished power, and infinite power — these six, say the knowers of the rules, are the attributes of the Great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>)." "Such a meaning is contradicted by evidence." — No, that has already been refuted. "Still, there is no evidence for it." — Then what confidence do you have in heaven (<s>svarga</s>)? For we too have no evidence for a pleasure with such qualifications. "It is determined thus from the inexplicability of the activity of sacrificers without it." — No, because of mutual dependence: the nature of heaven being determined, there is activity toward it; and from the inexplicability of that activity, the nature of heaven is determined. "This is no fault, since the determination comes from the activity of earlier elders." — No, because of blind-leading-the-blind. "Due to special <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), at some time for someone such pleasure might exist — there is no contradiction; since there is no evidence to negate it." — The same applies in our case [regarding God]. Here too the argument: whatever word is used by learned elders in the absence of any other usage — that word denotes that [meaning]. Just as the word "heaven" used for a special kind of pleasure denotes that. And this word [Īśvara] is used for the creator of the world. Otherwise, the absurdity of meaninglessness would make the use of meaningful words alongside it inexplicable. By this, words denoting particular deities like <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>, etc. are explained. Moreover, the word <s>asmat</s> ("I/we") is used in the <s>Veda</s> as in ordinary speech. And in the world, it does not refer to unconscious things — since it is never used for them at all. Nor does it merely mean the self [abstractly]; since it would then apply to other selves too. Rather, whoever independently utters it, refers to himself; as determined by positive and negative concomitance. Therefore, not transgressing ordinary linguistic usage, even in the <s>Veda</s> this word must refer to its own speaker. Otherwise there would be misapplication. And it is not right that whoever recites the Vedic word "I" is himself its referent at that moment. For then in "worship me" etc., the reciter himself would be the object of worship. And in "I am the origin of all; from me everything proceeds" — the succession of teacher and student would attribute lordship to themselves. And worship would become a madman's play. And ordinary usage would be destroyed. Therefore the referent is not the repeater but the [original] speaker. And thus the word <s>asmat</s> is used in the <s>Veda</s> as referring to its own [original] speaker — being the word <s>asmat</s>, just as in the world. Similarly, other words like "who," "what," "he" etc. should be understood, since they have conventions established by contexts of inquiry, investigation, questioning, deliberation, etc.; and these are properties of a speaker. For "inquiry" means dealing with the topic at hand; "questioning" means manifesting a desire to know; and "deliberation" means reconsideration. And thus even words expressing doubt etc. can be inferred [to require a speaker]. And it is not right to say that desire-to-know, doubt, etc. are precluded in an omniscient being; for there is no contradiction, since they are assumed [by Him] deliberately for the instruction of students — like [the questions in] the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: "What is <s>dharma</s>? What are its characteristics?" etc. By this, particles (<s>nipāta</s>) such as "alas!" "oh!" "indeed!" etc. are also explained.

children.text:
[ku.5.646] pravṛttiḥ khalu vidhikāryā satī na tāvatkāyaparispandamātram, ātmā jñātavya ityādyavyāpanāt /
nāpīcchāmātram tata eva phalasiddhau karmānārambhaprasaṅgāt /
tataḥ prayatnaḥ pariśiṣyate /
ātmajñānabhūtadayādāvapi tasyāḥ (sya?) bhāvāt /
taduktam, "pravṛttirāramabhaḥ" iti /
[ku.5.647] seyaṃ pravṛttiryataḥsattāmātrāvasthitād, nāsau vidhiḥ; tatra śāstravaiyarthyāt /
apratītādeva kutaścit pravṛttisiddhau tatpratyāyanārthaṃ tadabhyarthanābhāvāt /
na ca pravṛttihetujananārthaṃ tadupayogaḥ; pravṛttihetoricchāyā jñānayonitvāt jñānamanutpādyatadutpādanasyāśakyatvāt tasya ca nirālambanasyānutpatteḥ; apravartakatvācca, niyāmakābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is that [injunction] useful for generating the cause of activity; because desire (<s>icchā</s>), which is the cause of activity, has knowledge as its source, and it is impossible to generate that [knowledge] without it having already arisen, and because that [knowledge], being without a support, does not arise [independently]; and because [the injunction would be] non-prompting, due to the absence of a determining factor.

children.text: tasmād yasya jñānaṃ prayatnajananīmicchāṃ prasūte, sorthaviśeṣastajjñāpako vār'thaviśeṣo vidhiḥ preraṇā pravartanā niyuktirniyoga upadeśa ityanarthāntaramiti sthite vicāryate- sa hi kartṛdharmo vā syāt, karmadharmo vā, karaṇadharmo vā niyoktṛdharmo veti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, that which generates desire that gives rise to effort through knowledge — that particular object, or the particular object that makes it known — is the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), prompting (<s>preraṇā</s>), instigation (<s>pravartanā</s>), assignment (<s>niyukti</s>), commission (<s>niyoga</s>), instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>) — these are synonymous. This being established, it is examined: Is it a property of the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>), or a property of the object (<s>karman</s>), or a property of the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), or a property of the commissioner (<s>niyoktṛ</s>)?
Not the first — [Ku 5.648] Because of the loss of what is desired and the attainment of what is undesired; because of the contradiction with non-activity;

because of non-existence [of the supposed property]; because of the abandonment of the cognition [i.e. verbal suffix]; it is not a property of the agent; because of the confusion [that would result]. //8//

[Ku 5.646] Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), being the effect of an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), is not merely bodily movement, because it does not extend to [cases like] 'the self should be known' and the like. Nor is it mere desire (<s>icchā</s>), because if the result were accomplished from that alone, there would be the undesirable consequence of not undertaking action. Therefore, effort (<s>prayatna</s>) remains [as the meaning], since it is present even in the cognition of the self, compassion toward beings, and so on. As it has been said: 'Activity is commencement.' [Ku 5.647] And this activity — if it were to arise from what merely exists [without prompting], that would not be an injunction; because scripture would be purposeless in that case. Since if activity is accomplished from some [cause] that is not comprehended, there would be no seeking to convey that [cause], and hence no solicitation for it.

children.text:
sa hi na spanda eva; ātmānamanupaśyedityādyavyāpteḥ; grāmaṃ gacchatītyādāvativyāpteśca /
nāpi tatkāraṇaṃ prayatnaḥ; tasya sarvākhyātasādhāraṇatvāt /
[ku.5.649] nanu na sarvatra prayatna eva pratyayārthaḥ; karotītyādau prakṛtyarthātirekiṇastasyābhāvāt /
saṅkhyāmātrābhidhānena pratyayasya caritārthatvāt /
tato liṅgādivācca eva prayatna iti- na- kuryādityatrāpi tulyatvāt /
prayatnamātrasya prakṛtyarthatve 'pi tasya parā(256)ṅgatāpannasya pratyayārthatvānna tulyatvamiti cet- na- tathāpi tulyatvāt /
na caikasya tadvācakatve 'nyasya tadviparyaya āpadyeta /
eko dvau bahava eṣiṣatītyādau vyabhicārāt /
tatra dvitīyasṅkhyecchādikalpane karoti prayatate ityādāvapi tathā syāt /
pratyekamanyatrasāmarthyāvadhṛtau sambhede tathā kalpanāyāstulyatvāt /
ratho gacchatītyādau tadasambhave kā gatiriti cet- tantavaḥ paṭaṃ kurvantītyatra yā /
lokopacāro 'yamaparyanuyojya iti cettulyam /
liṅaḥ kāryatve vṛddhavyavahārādvyutpattau sarvaṃ samañjasam /
ākhyātamātrasya tu na tatheti cet- na- vivaraṇāderapi vyutpatteḥ /
asti ca tadiha /
kiṃ karoti? pacati, pākaṃ karotītyartha ityādidarśanāt /
[ku.5.650] tathāpi phalānukūlatāpannadhātvarthamātrābhidhāne tadatiriktaprayatnābhidhānakalpanāyāṃ kalpanāgauravaṃ syāt /
ato vivaraṇamapi tāvanmātraparamiti cet /
bhavedapyevam, yadi pākeneti vivṛṇuyāt /
na tvetadasti /
dhātvarthasyaiva pākamiti sādhyatvena nirdeśāt /
tatastaṃ pratyeva kiñcidanukūlatāpannaṃ pratyayenābhidhānīyamiti yuktam /
[ku.5.651] tathāpi tena prayatnenaiva bhavitavyam, na tvanyeneti kuta iti cet- niyamena tathā vivaraṇāt /
bādhakaṃ vinā tasyānyathākartumaśakyatvāt /
anyathātiprasaṅgāt /
syādetat- yasya kasyacit- phalaṃ pratyanukūlatāpattimātrameva karotyarthaḥ, na tu prayatna eva /
so 'pi hyanenaivopādhinā pratyayena vaktavyaḥ, na tu yatnatvamātreṇa; prayatnapadenāviśeṣaprasaṅgāt /
tadvaraṃ tāvanmātramevāstu lāghavāya /
anyathā tvanukūlatvaprayatnatve dvāvupādhī kalpanīyau; acetaneṣu sarvatra gauṇārthāstiṅo 'sati
children.translated_text: Otherwise, however, two limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) — favorableness and effort-ness — would have to be postulated; [and] in all inanimate [subjects], the finite verbal forms (<s>tiṅ</s>) with figurative meaning, in the absence

children.text: bādhake kalpanīyā iti cet- atrocyate-[ku.5.652] kṛtākṛtavibhāgena kartṛrūpavyavasthayā /
children.translated_text: of a counter-proof, would have to be postulated. — To this it is replied: [Ku 5.652] By the distinction between what is done and what is not done, and by the determination of the form of the agent,

children.text: yatna eva kṛtiḥ pūrvā (257) parasmin saiva bhavanā //9 //
children.translated_text: effort alone is the primary meaning of <s>kṛ</s> ('to do'); in the other [i.e. the injunctive mood], that very [effort] is <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive operation). //9//

For it [the meaning of the verbal suffix] is not mere movement (<s>spanda</s>); because it does not extend to 'one should perceive the self' and the like; and because it over-extends to 'he goes to the village' and the like. Nor is it the cause of that [movement], namely effort (<s>prayatna</s>); because that is common to all verbal roots (<s>ākhyāta</s>). [Ku 5.649] [Objection:] But effort is not the meaning of the verbal suffix everywhere; because in 'he does' and the like, it is absent as something over and above the meaning of the verbal root. And because the verbal suffix accomplishes its purpose by merely expressing number. Therefore, effort is [expressed] only by the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and the like [moods] — [we reply:] No, because the same applies to 'he should do' [optative]. [Objection:] If it be said that even when effort alone is the meaning of the verbal root, [in the optative] it becomes the meaning of the suffix because it takes on a secondary role — [we reply:] No, because even so the same [difficulty] applies. And it is not the case that when one [form] expresses that [meaning], the other must express its opposite. Because there is deviation in 'one, two, many wish' and the like. If in those cases the second number, desire, etc. are to be postulated [as suffix-meanings], then in 'he does,' 'he strives,' etc. also the same [postulation] would apply. Because when the capacity [of root and suffix] to [express] different things is determined separately, there is equal difficulty in postulating [additional meanings] in their combination. [Objection:] If it be said, what is the recourse in 'the chariot goes' and the like, where that [effort] is impossible? — [we reply:] The same as in 'the threads make the cloth.' [Objection:] If it be said that this is merely a figurative popular usage not to be questioned — the same [reply applies to your case]. When the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) [mood] has effect-ness [as its meaning], everything is consistent through derivation from conventional usage of elders (<s>vṛddha</s>). [Objection:] If it be said that for the verbal form as a whole this is not so — [we reply:] No, because derivation [of meaning] from explanatory sentences (<s>vivaraṇa</s>) is also [possible]. And that [explanatory usage] exists here. As is seen from: 'What does he do? He cooks — meaning, he performs cooking,' and so on. [Ku 5.650] [Objection:] Even so, when merely the meaning of the verbal root — which has acquired favorableness toward the result — is expressed, postulating the additional expression of effort beyond that would involve the fault of over-postulation. Therefore, the explanatory sentence too is directed only to that much. — [We reply:] This might be so if one were to explain [it as] 'by cooking.' But that is not the case; because the meaning of the verbal root — cooking itself — is indicated as what is to be accomplished. Therefore, it is proper that something favorable to that [cooking], over and above it, should be expressed by the verbal suffix. [Ku 5.651] [Objection:] Even so, why must it be effort and nothing else? — [We reply:] Because the explanatory sentence invariably explains it in that way. Because without a counter-proof, it cannot be made otherwise. Because otherwise there would be over-extension. [Objection:] It might be this: the meaning of 'does' for anyone is merely the acquisition of favorableness toward the result, and not effort specifically. For that [effort] too should be expressed by this very qualifying suffix, not by mere effort-ness; because [expressing] by the word 'effort' [alone] would lead to non-specificity. Therefore, let only that much [favorableness] be [the meaning], for the sake of parsimony.

children.text:
yatnapūrvakatva.ṃ hi pratisandhāya ghaṭādau kṛta iti vyavahārāt /
hetusattvapratisandhāne 'pi yatnapūrvakatvapratisandhānavidhurāṇāmaṅkurādau tadavyavahārāt karotyartho yatna eva tāvadavasīyate /
anyathā hi yatkiñcidanukūlapūrvakatvāviśeṣāt "ghaṭādayaḥ kṛtāḥ, na kṛtāstvaṅkurādaya" iti kuto vyavahāraniyamaḥ /
tena ca sarvamākhyātapadaṃ vivriyate iti sarvatra sa evārtha iti nirṇayaḥ /
tathāca samudite pravṛttaṃ padaṃ tadekadeśe 'pi prayujyate, viśuddhimātraṃ puraskṛtya brāhmaṇe śrotriyapadavat /
anyathāpi madhyamottamapuruṣagāminaḥ pratyayāḥ, prathame puruṣe jānāti icchati prayatate adhyavasyati śete saṃśete ityādayaśca gauṇārthā evācetaneṣu /
na ca vṛttyantareṇāpi prayogasambhave śaktikalpanā yuktā; anyāyaścānekārthatvamiti sthiteḥ /
ata evānubhavo 'pi, yāvaduktaṃ bhavati pākānukūlavartamānaprayatnavān, tāvaduktaṃ bhavati pacatīti /
evaṃ tathābhūtātivṛttaprayatno 'pākṣīditi /
evaṃ tathābhūtabhāviprayatnaḥ pakṣyatīti /
na tu pacatīti pākānukūlayatkiñcidvāniti /
anyathātithāvapi paraśramaśayāne pacatīti pratyayaprasaṅgāt /
[ku.5.653] apica kartṛvyāpāra eva kṛñarthaḥ /
cetanaśca kartā; anyathā tadvyavasthānupapatteḥ /
na hyabhidhīyamānavyāpāravattvaṃ kartṛtvam, anabhidhānadaśāyāṃ kurvato 'pyakartṛtvaprasaṅgāt /
nāpyākhyātapratyayābhidhānayogyavyāpāraśālitvaṃ kartṛtvam, yogyatāyā evānirūpaṇāt /
phalānuguṇamātrasya sarvakārakavyāpārasādhāraṇatvāt /
nāpi vivakṣāto niyamaḥ, avivakṣādaśāyāmaniyamaprasaṅgāt /
svavyāpāre nedamaniṣṭamiti cet- evaṃ tarhi, "svavyāpāre ca kartṛtvaṃ sarvatraivāsti kārake" iti nyāyena karaṇādivilopaprasaṅgaḥ /
na svavyāpārāpekṣayā karaṇādivyavahāraḥ; kintu pradhānakriyāpekṣayā /
asti hi kāñcit kriyāmuddiśya pravartamānānāṃ kārakāṇāmavāntaravyāpārayogaḥ, natvavāntaravyāpārārthameva teṣāṃ pravṛttiriti cet- tarhi tadapekṣayaiva kartṛkarmādivyavahāraviśeṣaniyame kiṃ kāraṇamiti cintyatām /
svātantryāditi cet- nanu tadeva kimanyat prayatnādisamavāyāditi vivicyābhidhīyatāmiti /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If it be said: because of independence (<s>svātantrya</s>) — well then, what is that other than co-inherence with effort and the like? Let this be analyzed and stated.
Therefore, the meaning of the verbal form is everywhere a uniform operation [namely, effort].

children.text: [ku.5.654] tathāpi phalānuguṇataivāstu pratyayasya pravṛttinimittam; prayatnastvākṣepato lapsyate iti cenna- bhāvanaiva hi yatnātmā sarvatrākhyātagocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: [Ku 5.654] [Objection:] Even so, let the occasion for the application of the verbal suffix be mere favorableness to the result; and effort will be obtained by implication (<s>ākṣepa</s>). — [We reply:] No, for <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive operation), which is of the nature of effort, is everywhere the domain of the verbal form.
Because of the constancy of [its being confirmed through] explanatory sentences, and because implication is untenable [as the means of conveying it]. //10//

For it is from the recollection of being preceded by effort that the usage 'done' applies to pots and the like. And because in sprouts and the like, which lack the recollection of being preceded by effort — even when the presence of a [mere] cause is recollected — the usage [of 'done'] does not apply, the meaning of 'does' is determined to be effort alone. For otherwise, since there would be no distinction in being preceded by just anything favorable, whence would come the restriction of usage: 'Pots and the like are made (<s>kṛta</s>), but sprouts and the like are not made'? And by that [effort-meaning], every verbal form (<s>ākhyāta-pada</s>) is explained; therefore, this is the meaning everywhere — this is the conclusion. And thus a word applied to the whole is also used for a part of it, taking into account only [the relevant] purity, like the word <s>śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar) [applied to] a brahmin. Moreover, the suffixes pertaining to the second and third persons [of the verb], and [expressions like] 'he knows,' 'he desires,' 'he strives,' 'he resolves,' 'he sleeps,' 'he lies down,' and the like in the first person — these are all figurative in meaning when applied to inanimate [subjects]. Nor is the postulation of a [separate] linguistic capacity proper when usage is possible through another [already established] function; and it is established that polysemy is irregular. For this very reason, experience too [confirms this]: to the extent that one says 'he possesses present effort favorable to cooking,' to that extent one says 'he cooks.' Likewise, 'he who had such effort in the past, cooked.' And 'he who will have such effort in the future, will cook.' But 'he cooks' does not mean 'he possesses just anything favorable to cooking.' For otherwise, even regarding a guest sleeping exhausted from another's labor, the cognition 'he cooks' would absurdly arise. [Ku 5.653] Moreover, the meaning of the root <s>kṛ</s> is precisely the operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>) of the agent. And the agent is a conscious being; because otherwise the determination of that [agency] would be impossible to account for. For agency is not merely possessing the operation that is being expressed [by the verb], because even for one who acts in a state of non-expression, there would absurdly be non-agency. Nor is agency the possession of an operation expressible by verbal-suffix expression, because expressibility itself cannot be determined. Because mere favorableness to the result is common to the operations of all <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations). Nor is the restriction [of agency] due to the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>), because in the state of non-intention there would absurdly be non-restriction. [Objection:] If it be said that this objection does not apply to one's own operation — then by the principle 'agency with respect to one's own operation belongs to every <s>kāraka</s> everywhere,' there would be the undesirable consequence of the elimination of instrument and other [kārakas]. The usage of instrument and the like is not with respect to [each one's] own operation, but with respect to the principal action. For the <s>kārakas</s> operating with reference to some [principal] action have subordinate operations, but their operation is not for the sake of the subordinate operation alone. — [Objection:] If so, then let it be considered what is the reason for the restriction of the specific usages of agent, object, etc. with respect to that [principal action].

children.text:
kena hi tadākṣipyeta /
natāvadanukūlatvamātreṇa; tasya prayatnatvenāvyāpanāt /
na hi yatnatvaikārthasamavāyyevānukūlatvam /
ata eva na saṅkhyayā; tasyāḥ saṅkhyeyamātraparyavasāyitvāt /
kartreti cet- na- dravyamātrasyākartṛtvāt /
vyāpāravataścābhidhāne vyāpārābhidhānasyāvaśyābhyupagamanīyatvāt /
nāpi dhātvarthena tadākṣepaḥ; vidyate ityādau tadasambhavāt /
na hyatri dhātvartho bhāvanāpekṣī; sattayā nityatvāt /
tatra na bhaviṣyatīti cet- na- pūrvāparībhūtabhāvanānubhavasyāviśeṣāt /
bhāvanoparāgeṇa hyatathābhūto 'pyarthastathā bhāsate iti /
na ca padāntaralabdhayā bhāvanayānukūlatāyāḥ pratyayārthasyānvayaḥ; tadasambhavāt /
na khalu prakṛtyaiva sābhidhīyate /
dhātūnāṃ kriyāphalamātrābhidhāyitvāt /
anyathā pāka ityādāvapi bhāvanānubhavaprasaṅgāt /
nāpi caitra ityādinā padāntareṇa; prakṛtipratyayayorubhayorapyakārakārthatvāt /
odanamityādeḥ kārakapadatvāt tasya ca kriyopahitatvāttenābhidhānamākṣepo vā /
kathamanyathā odanamityukte kiṃ bhuṅkte pacati veti viśeṣākāṅkṣeti cet- na- pacatītyukte kimodanaṃ temanaṃ veti viśeṣākāṅkṣādarśanāt /
sā cākṣepābhidhānayoranyataramantareṇa na syāt /
tasyāṃ daśāyāṃ na cedākṣepaḥ, nūnamabhidhānameveti /
[ku.5.655] syādetat- abhidhīyatāṃ tarhi kartāpi /
tadanabhidhāne hi saṅkhyeyamātramākṣipya saṅkhyā kathaṃ kartāramanviyāt, na tu karmādikamapi /
śākasūpau pacati śākasūpaudanān pacatītyādau virodhanirastā saṅkhyā caitra iti kartāramaviruddhamanugacchatīti cet- caitra odanaṃ pacatītyatrakā gatiḥ /
ekatra nirṇītaḥ śāstrārtho 'paratrāpi tathā, yavavarāhādivaditi cenna- pacyate ityādāvapi tathābhāvaprasaṅgāt /
caitrābhyāṃ caitrairiti virodhanirastā sūpa ityaviruddhaṃ karma samanukrāmatīti cet /
caitramaitrābhyāṃ pākasūpau pacyete ityatra kā gatiḥ /
anyatra nirṇītenārthena vyavahāra iti cenna- pacatītyādāvapi tathābhāvaprasaṅgāt /
tatra pūrvaka eva nirṇayaḥ, pacyate ityatratvapara iti cenna- viśeṣābhāvāt /
ātmanepadaparasmaipadābhyāṃ viśeṣa iti cenna- pacyate pacate pakṣyate ityādau viplavaprasaṅgāditi /
[ku.5.656] dṛśyate ca samānapratyayābhihitenānvayaḥsaṅkhyāyāḥ /
tad yathā, bhūyate supyate ityādau /
na
 hi tatra kartrā karmaṇā vānyenaiva vā kenacidanvayaḥ, kintu bhāvenaiva /
ananvaye tadabhidhāyino 'narthakatvaprasaṅgāt /
ākṣiptenacānvaye tatrāpi kartrevānvayāpatteḥ /
ko hisupyate svapitītyanayoḥ kartrākṣepaṃ prati viśeṣaḥ /
syādetat- (a.1-3-13) bhāvakarmaṇorityādyanuśāsanabalāttāvat bhāvakarmaṇī pratyayavācye /
tatastadabhihitā saṅkhyā tābhyāmanvīyate /
yastu pratyayo na tatrotpannaḥ, tadabhihitā saṅkhyā, "mukhyaṃ vā pūrvacodanāllokavat'(mī.12,2,23) iti nyāyena kartāramevāśrayate iti niyamaḥ- na- viparyyayaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: But [for] the suffix not produced in that [<s>bhāva</s>/<s>karma</s>] context, the number denoted by it, by the principle 'the primary [meaning applies], or [it follows] from the prior injunction, as in ordinary usage' (<s>Mīmāṃsā Sūtra</s> 12.2.23), rests on the agent alone — this is the rule — no, because of the absurd consequence of the reverse.

children.text: "śeṣāt kartari parasmaipadam" (a.1-3-78), "kartari śap" (a.3-1-68) ityanuśāsanabalādbhāvakartārau pratyayavācyau, tatastadabhihitā saṅkhyāpi tābhyāmanvīyate; yastu pratyayo na tatrotpannastadabhihitā saṅkhyā tenaiva nyāyena karmaiva samāśrayediti niyamopapatteḥ tasmānmatikardamamapahāya yathānuśāsanameva gṛhyate iti prāptam /
children.translated_text: By the force of the grammatical teachings 'the active voice [is used] when the remaining [<s>kārakas</s>, i.e.,] the agent [is prominent]' (A. 1.3.78) and '<s>śap</s> [is affixed] when the agent [is prominent]' (A. 3.1.68), <s>bhāva</s> and agent are denoted by the suffix; then the number denoted by that also connects with those two. But [for] the suffix not produced in that [agent] context, the number denoted by it, by that very principle, would rest on the object alone — this alternative rule is also tenable. Therefore, setting aside the confusion of [competing] opinions, [the meaning] should be accepted just as the grammatical teaching [prescribes] — this is the established position.

children.text: evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate- [ku.5.657] ākṣepalabhye saṅkhyeye nābhidhānasya kalpanā /
children.translated_text: When this has been established, it is declared: [Ku 5.657] When the countable is obtainable by attraction, there is no need to postulate denotation [of the agent by the suffix].
Even when only the countable is obtained [by attraction], the determination [of agent, object, etc.] is by [the word] that has expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>). (Verse 11)

[Ku 5.654 cont.] For by what would that [number] be attracted [to a referent]? Not merely by favorability, since that does not extend to effort [alone]. For favorability is not co-extensive in meaning with efforthood alone [as inhering in the same thing]. For this very reason, not [attracted] by number [itself]; because number culminates in the mere countable. If [it be said:] by 'the agent' — no, because a mere substance is not an agent. And when a [substance] possessing activity is being denoted, the denotation of the activity must necessarily be accepted. Nor is that [agent-meaning] attracted by the verbal root meaning; because that is impossible in [expressions like] 'vidyate' (it exists) and the like. For there the verbal root meaning does not require <s>bhāvanā</s> (bringing-into-being); because of the eternality of existence. If it be said that [<s>bhāvanā</s>] will not apply there — no, because there is no distinction from the experience of <s>bhāvanā</s> that has earlier and later [moments]. For through the superimposition of <s>bhāvanā</s>, even an object that is not actually so appears as if it were so. Nor does the [predication-meaning] of the suffix (<s>pratyayārtha</s>) — favorability — connect with the <s>bhāvanā</s> obtained from another word; because that is impossible. For the verbal root itself does not denote it [<s>bhāvanā</s>]; because verbal roots denote only the fruit of action. Otherwise, even in [expressions like] 'cooking' (<s>pāka</s>) etc. there would be the absurd consequence of experiencing <s>bhāvanā</s>. Nor [is it attracted] by another word such as '<s>Caitra</s>'; because both the root and the suffix have non-<s>kāraka</s> meanings. Since the word 'rice' (<s>odanam</s>) is a <s>kāraka</s>-word, and since it is qualified by the action, either the denotation or the attraction [of the agent] is by that. If it be said: how else, when 'rice' is uttered, [does one have] the specific expectation 'does he eat or cook [it]?' — no, because when 'cooks' is uttered, the specific expectation 'rice or husked grain?' is observed. And that [expectation] would not exist without either attraction or denotation. In that situation, if there is no attraction, surely it is denotation indeed.
[Ku 5.655] It may be objected: then let the agent also be denoted [by the suffix]. For if the agent is not denoted, how would number — having attracted merely the countable — connect with the agent, and not also with the object etc.? If it be said: in 'he cooks greens and sauce,' 'he cooks greens, sauce, and rice' — the number, [its connection] with incompatibles having been eliminated, follows the agent '<s>Caitra</s>' which is compatible — [then what about] 'Caitra cooks rice' — what is the procedure here? If it be said: the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s> determined in one case [applies] in another as well, like [the rules for] barley and pig [offerings] — no, because the same absurd consequence would arise in 'is cooked' etc. If it be said: the number, [its connection] with '<s>Caitras</s> (dual)' and '<s>Caitras</s> (plural)' having been eliminated as incompatible, follows 'sauce,' the compatible object — [then what about] '<s>Caitra</s> and <s>Maitra</s> cook sauce [dual] and rice' — what is the procedure here? If it be said: one proceeds with the meaning determined elsewhere — no, because the same absurd consequence would arise in 'cooks' etc. If it be said: the determination follows the former [rule] there, and [the rule for] 'is cooked' follows the latter — no, because of the absence of a distinction. If it be said: the distinction is from the middle voice (<s>ātmanepada</s>) and the active voice (<s>parasmaipada</s>) — no, because of the absurd consequences of confusion in 'pacyate,' 'pacate,' 'pakṣyate,' etc.
[Ku 5.656] And it is observed that number connects with what is denoted by the same suffix. For example, in '<s>bhūyate</s>' (it is become), '<s>supyate</s>' (it is slept), and the like. For there the connection is not with the agent, or with the object, or with anything else, but with the <s>bhāva</s> (mere being/action) alone. Because in the absence of connection, those [suffixes] that denote it would be meaningless. And if [the connection occurs] through attraction, then even there the connection would consequentially be with the agent alone. For what distinction is there between '<s>supyate</s>' and '<s>svapiti</s>' with respect to the attraction of the agent? It may be objected: by the force of the grammatical teaching '<s>bhāvakarmaṇoḥ</s>' (A. 1.3.13) etc., <s>bhāva</s> and <s>karma</s> are first [established as] denoted by the suffix. Then the number denoted by that [suffix] connects with those two.

children.text:
saṅkhyāp.i tāvadiyaṃ bhāvanānugāminī; yaṃ yaṃ bhāvanānveti, taṃ taṃ saṅkhyāpīti sthiteḥ; ekapratyayavācyatvaniyamāt /
bhāvanāca śuddhaṃ prātipadikārthamātramākāṅkṣati /
na hi vyāpāravantaṃ vyāpāra āśrayate, ātmāśrayāt (258) /
samavāyaṃ prati tadanupayogāt /
vijātīyavyāpāravato 'kartṛtvācca /
na ca dvitīyādyāḥ prātipadikavibhaktayaḥ /
tataḥ prathamānirdiṣṭenaiva bhāvanānvīyate iti tasyānvayayogyatāniyamāt saṅkhyāpi tadanugāminī tenaivānvīyate iti nāti prasaṅgaḥ nañarthavat /
yathā hi caitro na brāhmaṇo na (259) gauro na spandate na kuṇḍalītyādau viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasamabhivyāhāraviśeṣe 'pi nañā tadanabhidhānāviśeṣe 'pi nañarthasya viśeṣaṇāṃśairevānvayaḥ na viśeṣyāṃśena /
nanu bādhāttatra tathā /
na hi viśeṣyeṇa tadanvaye viśeṣaṇopādānamarthavadbhavet, tanniṣedhenaiva viśeṣaṇaniṣedhopalabdheḥ /
ubhaniṣedhe cāvṛttau vākyabhedāt; anāvṛttau nirākāṅkṣatvāditi cet- tulyatvāt /
samānapratyayopāttabhāvanākṣiptānvayopapattau bādhakaṃ vinā sannihitatyāgena vyavahitaparigrahasya gurutvāt /
bhāvanāyāśca sāmānyākṣepe 'pi sākāṅkṣaparityāge nirākāṅkṣānvayānupapatteḥ /
nahyanyatarākāṅkṣā anvayahetuḥ apitūbhayākāṅkṣā /
prātipadikārtho hi phalenānvayamalabhamānaḥ kriyāsambandhamapekṣate, bhāvanāpi vyāpārabhūtā satī vyāpāriṇamityubhayākāṅkṣā anvayahetuḥ /
kaṭaṃ kaṭenetyādi tu kārakatayaiva phalasamanvitaṃ na vyāpārāntaramapekṣate iti nirākāṅkṣamiti /
ata evāsyate supyate ityādau nākṣiptenānvayaḥ /
nahi caitreṇeti tṛtīyāntaśabdasya bhāvanāyāmākāṅkṣāsti /
bhāvyākāṅkṣāstīti cet- na- phalena śayanādidhātvarthenānvayāt /
phalasambandhinaścātra kartranatirekāt /
na hi śayanādayo dhātvarthāḥ kartratirekisambaddhāḥ /
na ca phalatatsambandhivyatirekeṇānyo bhāvyo nāma,yamapekṣeta /
[ku.5.658] syādetat- kimiti na prayujyate kaṭaḥ karoti caitramityādi, abhihitānabhihitavyavasthābhāvāditi cet- na cetramiti prathamāntasyāsādhutvāt /
dvitīyāntasya tu karmavacanatvena tatsambandhād(260)bhāvyānapekṣiṇī bhāvanā bhāvakamātramapekṣeta /
na ca kaṭasya caitraṃ pratibhāvakatvam, viryayāt /
anāptena tu vivakṣāyāṃ prayujyata eva /
prayujyatāṃ tarhi kaṭaḥ karoti caitra ityādi- na- nityasandigdhatvena vākyārthāsamarpakatvāt /
tatastadupapattaye viśeṣasyavyañjanīyatvāt /
vyajyatāṃ tarhi tṛtīyayā caitreṇeti, evaṃ devadattaḥ kriyate kaṭamiti vyajyatāṃ dvitīyayeti cet- na- aprayogāt /
nahyanāptenāpyevaṃ prāyāṇi prayujyante /
lakṣaṇāvirodhena kuta etadeveti cet- lokasyāparyanuyojyatvāt /
na hi gārgikayeti padaṃ sādhviti ślāghābhidhāyipadasannidhimanapekṣya prayujyate /
tasya tadupādhinaiva vihitatvāditi cet- etadeva kutaḥ? loke tathaiva prayogadarśanāditi cet- tulyam /
karotītyādi karmavibhaktisamabhivyāhāreṇaiva prayujyate, kriyate iti kartṛvibhaktisamabhavyāhāreṇaiveti kimatra kriyatām /
[ku.5.659] imameva viśeṣamurarīkṛtyānabhihitādhikārānuśāsanena hyetāvān parāmarśaḥsarveṣāṃ hṛdi padamādadhātītyabhidhānānabhidhānavibhāga eva vyutpādanadaśāyāṃ peśala iti /
[ku.5.660] syādetat- bhavatu sarvākhyātasādhāraṇī bhāvanā; kālaviśeṣasambandhinī sā laḍādyarthaḥ, kālatrayāparāmṛṣṭā liṅārtha iti cet- na yatnapadena samānārthatvaprasaṅgāt /
viṣayoparāgānuparāgābhyāṃ viśeṣa iti cenna- yāgayatna ityanena paryāyatāpatteḥ /
kartṛsaṅkhyābhidhānānabhidhānābhyāṃ viśeṣa iti cenna- yāgayatnavānityanena sāmyāpatteḥ /
iṣṭa evāyamartha iti cenna- ito vatsaraśatenāpyapravṛtteḥ /
phalasamabhivyāhārābhāvānna pravarttate iti cenna- svargakāmo yāgayatnavānityato 'pyapravṛtteḥ /
tat kasya hetoḥ? na hi yatno yatnasya
 heturyatnapratītirvā yatnasya kāraṇam; api tvicchā /
[ku.5.661] na ca sāpi pratītā yatnajananī- yena saiva vidhyartha ityanugamyatām- apitu sattayā /
na ca liṅaḥ śrutikāle sā satī /
na ca liṅeva tāṃ janayati; arthaviśeṣamapratyāyayantyāstasyāḥ ( 261) tajjanakatve vyutpattigrahaṇavaiyarthyāt /
anupalabdhaliṅāñcecchānutpattiprasaṅgāditi /
etena- vṛddhavyavahārādvyutpattirbhavantī bālasyātmani pravṛttiheturyo 'vagatastamevāśrayet, svayañca kuryāmiti saṅkalpādevāyaṃ pravṛttaḥ, tataḥsa eva liṅārtha iti nirastam /
kuryāmiti prayatno vā syādicchā vā? nādyaḥ,svātmani vṛttivirodhāt /
na dvitīyaḥ; sā hi sattayaiva prayatnotpādinī /
na ca liṅaḥ śrutikāle sā satītyuktam /
phalecchā tu nisargavāhitayā satyapi na prayatnaṃ prati hetuḥ; anyaviṣayatvāt /

children.translated_text: And for that purpose, the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) would be pointless.
Because that [bhāvanā] is established from another cause, scripture is not required even for the cognition of it.
Because that [bhāvanā] is knowable by the mind [alone].

children.text: aprāpte (262) ca śāstramarthavat; prāpte ca śāstrānavakāśāt //
children.translated_text: And scripture is meaningful when [the bhāvanā] has not been obtained; but when obtained, there is no scope for scripture.

Moreover, this number [of the verbal suffix] follows the <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive operation); for the established principle is: whatever the <s>bhāvanā</s> is connected with, the number too [agrees with that]. This is because of the rule that it [number] is expressible by a single suffix. And the <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive operation) requires only the pure stem-meaning. For an operation does not depend on what already has an operation — that would be self-dependence. Because it is of no use with respect to <s>samavāya</s> (inherence). And because what has a different type of operation is not an agent. Nor are the second and other case-endings stem-suffixes. Therefore, the <s>bhāvanā</s> is connected with what is denoted by the nominative alone — and because of the restriction on what is fit for connection, number too, following it [the bhāvanā], is connected with that alone — so there is no over-extension, just as with the meaning of the negative particle. For just as in '<s>Caitra</s> is not a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,' 'is not fair,' 'does not move,' 'does not wear earrings,' and the like — even though there is the joint expression of qualifier and qualificand, and even though the negative particle does not express the qualificand, the meaning of the negative particle connects with the qualifier portion alone, not with the qualificand portion. [Objection:] But there it is so because of contradiction. For if it connected with the qualificand, the use of the qualifier would not be meaningful, since the negation of the qualificand itself would yield the negation of the qualifier. And if both are negated, either there is repetition and hence sentence-splitting, or there is non-repetition and hence completeness. [Reply:] Because the cases are equal. When the connection is established through the <s>bhāvanā</s> invoked by the same suffix, it is more burdensome to abandon what is proximate and adopt what is distant, without a contradicting [consideration]. And even when the <s>bhāvanā</s> invokes the general [meaning], in abandoning what has expectancy, if the connection is with what has no expectancy, it cannot be established. For expectancy on one side alone is not the cause of connection, but rather mutual expectancy. For the stem-meaning, not obtaining connection with the result, requires a relation with the action; and the <s>bhāvanā</s> too, being an operation, [requires] an operator — thus mutual expectancy is the cause of connection. But 'a mat, by a mat' and the like, being connected with the result precisely as an instrument, does not require a further operation — hence it is complete. For this very reason, in 'he sits,' 'he sleeps,' and the like, there is no connection with what is invoked. For the word ending in the third case, such as 'by <s>Caitra</s>,' does not have expectancy for the <s>bhāvanā</s>. [Objection:] If [it is said] there is expectancy for the object-to-be-produced — no, because of its connection with the result, namely the verbal root meaning such as sleeping. And because here, the one connected with the result is identical with the agent. For the verbal root meanings such as sleeping are not connected with something different from the agent. And there is no other 'object-to-be-produced' apart from the result and what is connected with it, which [the bhāvanā] would require. [Ku 5.658] It may be objected: Why is 'the mat makes <s>Caitra</s>' and the like not used, since there is no distinction between what is expressed and what is not expressed? No, because '<s>Caitra</s>' in the nominative [after an accusative verb] is ungrammatical. As for the accusative,

tadabhidhāne ca svargakāma iti kartṛviśeṣaṇapaunaruktyāt /
tadā hi yajetetyasyaiva yāgakartā svargakāma ityarthaḥsyāt /
[ku.5.662] yadica phalaviṣayaiva sādhanaviṣayaṃ prayatnaṃ janayet, anyatrāpi prasuvīta niyāmakābhāvāt /
hetuphalabhāva eva niyāmaka iti cenna- ajñātasya tasya niyāmakatve liṅaṃ vināpi svargecchāto yāge pravṛttiprasaṅgāt /
jñātasya tu tatsādhanatvasya niyāmakatve tadicchaiva tatra pravartayatuḥ yo yatkāmayate sa tatsādhanamapi kāmayata eveti niyamāt /
na ca sā tadānīṃ satī /
na ca tajjñānameva prayatnajanakam, tacca liṅā kriyate iti yuktam; svargakāmo yāgacikīrṣāvānityato 'pi pravṛttiprasaṅgāt /
liṅo vecchāṃ pratītyānicchannapi sarvaḥ pravarteta /
svasambandhitayā tadavagamastathā na tu sāmānyata iti cenna- prathamapuruṣeṇa tadanabhidhāne tasyāvidhyarthatvaprasaṅgāt /
odanakāmastvaṃ pākacikīrṣāvānityato 'pi pravṛttyāpatteśca (tteḥ) apica saṅkalpajñānādyadi prayatno jāyeta, tathāpi saṅkalpasya kuto janma kimarthañca? saṅkalpajñānādeva, prayatnārthañceti cet- nanvicchāviśeṣaḥ saṅkalpaḥ, sa tāvatsukhe svabhāvataḥ, tatsādhane caupādhikaḥ, saṅkalpaviṣayastu katham? tatsādhanatvādeveti cet- tarhi tatsādhanatvājñānāt, na tu saṅkalpasvarūpajñānādbhavitumarhatīti /
anyatheṣṭasādhanatājñānamapyanarthakamāpadyeta /
tasmāt, saṅkalpaḥ pravartaka ityabhyupeyate, kintu sattāmātreṇa, na tu jñāta iti nāsau vidhiḥ /
jñānañca viṣayopahāreṇaiva vyavahārayatīti tadviṣaya evāvaśiṣyate /

children.translated_text: Thus the rejection of [bhāvanā as] a property of the agent [is concluded].
[Ku 5.663] Then let it be a property of the object. It is said: no.
Because of over-extension, [bhāvanā] is not the result; nor is it <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit), because of the loss of its nature;
Because of the non-attainment of that [apūrva], it is not the effect; nor is it the action [itself], because of the non-engagement [in action]. || 12 ||

And in expressing that [bhāvanā], there would be redundancy of the qualifier of the agent in 'one who desires heaven.' For then, the meaning of 'he should sacrifice' would be: the performer of the sacrifice desires heaven. [Ku 5.662] And if the [bhāvanā] whose object is the result were to generate effort whose object is the means, it would produce [effort] elsewhere too, in the absence of a restricting factor. [Objection:] If [it is said that] the cause-effect relation itself is the restricting factor — no, because without a mark [of inference], the restrictive capacity of what is unknown [cannot be established].

na cākāmyaphale kāmī niyoktuṃ śakyate /
tato 'nyadevālaukikaṃ kiñcidanenopalakṣyate, yo liṅādipravṛttigocara iti kimanupapannimiti cet- na- (264) upalakṣaṇaṃ hi smaraṇamanumānaṃ vā /

yataḥ śrutasvargaphalatve 'pi sādhyavivṛddhirucyate /

nahi liṅā kāryaṃ svargasādhanamuktam /

yaṃ janayitvaiva hi yaṃ prati yasya pūrvabhāvanirvāhaḥ sa eva taṃ prati tasya vyāpāro nāparaḥ /
